stays.name: & Beyond Amazon Explorer
stays.tagline: A small-ship voyage into the Amazon’s hidden waterways.
stays.quote: You wake to the river, not an alarm, and the forest is the first thing you hear.
stays.bestMonths: July to December for drier trails and concentrated wildlife viewing; January to June for high-water canoeing and flooded-forest experiences.

paras: The & Beyond Amazon Explorer is a compact river vessel that moves at the pace of the rainforest, threading narrow channels and anchoring under a canopy of stars. Interiors are quietly refined, with cabins that open onto the river, open-air observation areas for wildlife watching, and communal dining that feels like a conversation between naturalists and guests. Days are structured around excursions by skiff and on foot, led by experienced naturalists who read the river and the forest for wildlife, seasons, and local life. Nights are spent moored in remote tributaries, where the rhythm of the Amazon becomes the traveler's calendar: dawn birdsong, a late-afternoon skiff glide, a quiet evening under unpolluted sky.

Signature days begin at first light with birdwatching from the river, followed by skiff excursions into narrow blackwater channels where herons, kingfishers and monkeys congregate. When water levels allow, short guided walks on terra firme reveal forest understory species and track lines of mammals. In the evening and at night, guides use headlamps and spotlights for nocturnal explorations, searching for caimans and night birds. Visits to riverside communities are woven into itineraries, offering perspectives on local livelihoods, river transport and artisanal fishing techniques.

Intimate river-boat design with river-facing cabins, open observation decks and small-group dining; expert, bilingual naturalist guides; flexible daily itineraries shaped by water levels and wildlife activity; emphasis on locally sourced provisions and low-impact operations.

onlyHere: Only aboard a small vessel like the Amazon Explorer can you spend full days moving between narrow tributaries, anchoring at sunset in places with no road access and waking within earshot of the forest. The combination of small-group, guide-led exploration and sleeping on the river offers a continuity of experience you do not get from land-based lodges. This property’s value is the intimacy of travel: the ability to follow a fleeting whale of migratory birds, to linger while a family of monkeys moves through an island, and to tailor the day to the river’s moods rather than a fixed schedule.

why.body: DEEP ECOLOGICAL IMMERSION Travel by small vessel into channels and flooded forests that larger ships cannot reach, with guided skiff excursions, canoeing and short jungle walks that place you close to birds, primates and riverine life.

INTIMATE, EXPLORER-STYLE COMFORT The boat is deliberately small, keeping group sizes low so excursions feel private and responsive; communal spaces encourage relaxed conversation and informal briefings with guides.

EXPERT NATURALIST GUIDING Local and international naturalists lead every outing, translating behavior into understanding and tailoring outings to what the river is showing that day, from birding to nocturnal spotlighting.

RESPONSIBLE, PLACE-BASED TRAVEL The voyage emphasizes low-impact exploration and genuine engagement with riverside communities, prioritizing cultural respect and practices that minimize footprints on fragile habitats.

facts.best_months: July to December for drier trails and concentrated wildlife viewing; January to June for high-water canoeing and flooded-forest experiences.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Manaus, then join the vessel via an arranged transfer by road or river from the city; logistical details are coordinated by the operator.
facts.who_its_for: Travelers seeking intimate, expedition-style luxury: couples and honeymooners, small families with older children, solo travelers, adventure seekers and wildlife photographers.
facts.signature_experiences: Skiff and canoe excursions into narrow tributaries, dawn birding from the river, nocturnal spotlighting for caimans and night birds, visits to riverside communities.

faqs.q: What is & Beyond Amazon Explorer known for?
faqs.a: & Beyond Amazon Explorer is known for intimate, small-ship voyages on the Amazon that combine wildlife-focused excursions, experienced naturalist guiding and immersive access to remote river channels.

faqs.q: How many rooms does & Beyond Amazon Explorer have?
faqs.a: The Amazon Explorer is an intimate river vessel with a limited number of cabins designed to keep group sizes small; contact & Beyond for current cabin configuration and maximum capacity.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit & Beyond Amazon Explorer?
faqs.a: For easier jungle trails and concentrated wildlife viewing, the drier months around July to December are often preferred; the higher-water season, roughly January to June, brings flooded-forest canoeing and different bird and fish activity.

faqs.q: Is & Beyond Amazon Explorer good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, the vessel can suit families, particularly those with older children who can participate in guided excursions; check age restrictions and activity suitability with & Beyond when booking.

faqs.q: How do you get to & Beyond Amazon Explorer?
faqs.a: Most guests fly to Manaus, Brazil, and then join the vessel via transfers arranged by the operator; & Beyond coordinates logistics from Manaus to the boarding point.

faqs.q: Are meals and excursions included on the Amazon Explorer?
faqs.a: Meals and scheduled daily excursions led by the on-board naturalist team are typically included; confirm inclusions and any optional activities with & Beyond when booking.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a voyage on the Amazon Explorer?
faqs.a: Pack light, breathable clothing, a waterproof jacket, insect repellent, binoculars and a good camera; bring sturdy shoes for short jungle walks and a compact daypack for excursions.

stays.name:
& Beyond Phinda
Homestead Residence
stays.tagline: Under-canvas nights on the Serengeti lakeshore, close to the migration and empty horizons.
stays.quote: Wake to the slow light on water, spend your days following the herds, then sleep under a canvas roof and a sky full of stars.
stays.bestMonths: June to October for dry-season game viewing and predators, December to March for southern Serengeti calving and concentrated migration activity.

paras: Set on the edge of the Serengeti ecosystem, & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas is an intimate mobile tented camp that brings guests close to seasonal wildlife concentrations and quiet lakeshore mornings. The camp’s canvas suites and shared living areas are pared-back and purposeful, designed so each view and every visit feels immediate and unmediated by excess. Because the camp moves with the seasons and the animals, a stay here is about presence: early starts for soft light on the plains, long afternoons by the lake, and guides who orient each day around where the wildlife is. The result is a private, low-key safari experience that privileges wildlife encounters and the rhythms of the land over fixed luxury trappings.

Signature experiences center on game drives timed for the best light and animal activity: sunrise successes when predators are active, long midday stakeouts for crossings or calving gatherings, and late-afternoon drives that end with sundowners on the plains. Photographic drives run at a measured pace and guides will position the vehicle to optimise light and angles. When permitted by park regulations and conditions, guests can also join guided bush walks to read tracks and encounter the smaller details of the ecosystem. For quieter moments, lakeshore picnics, private dinners on the camp deck and sunrise visits to nearby vantage points round out the program.

Standout features: a seasonally mobile, low-footprint canvas camp; intimate tented suites with direct views to the water or plains; experienced guides focused on wildlife and photographic outcomes; small guest numbers ensuring personalised service; and engagement with local conservation efforts and community projects.

onlyHere: Because the camp can be positioned close to seasonal water, guests often experience a rare combination of shoreline wildlife concentrations and wide-open Serengeti plains in a single day. That lakeside vantage creates moments you will not get from a distant lodge: quiet dawns at water’s edge, reflections of animals in still pools, and sundowners with the lake and horizon as your backdrop. The mobile nature of the property also means it can offer extremely private game-viewing windows when the migration or calving herds are in the vicinity, frequently placing guests ahead of the crowd and within striking distance of headline wildlife action.

why.body: Lakeside location The camp’s position on the edge of a seasonal lake means mornings and evenings are framed by water reflections and concentrations of game that gather at the shore. Birdlife is prolific and the light is singular for photographers.

Small, mobile and personal As a tented, seasonally mobile camp, the scale is intentionally small. Service is warm and unobtrusive, and the flexible setup lets guides place you where the action is, often with few other vehicles nearby.

Guiding that follows the herds Guides here work to match the day to the wildlife: morning and evening drives, optional guided walks when conditions allow, and adjustments to camp location to follow the migration and calving patterns in the southern Serengeti.

Authentic evenings and stargazing Meals are simple but refined, often shared around the campfire or on a private deck, with unpolluted night skies and the sounds of the bush forming the evening soundtrack.

facts.best_months: June to October for dry-season game viewing and predators, December to March for southern Serengeti calving and concentrated migration activity.
facts.how_to_get_there: International arrivals normally connect via Kilimanjaro or Nairobi and transfer to Arusha; from Arusha guests fly on light aircraft to a Serengeti airstrip and complete the trip by vehicle, or arrange an overland transfer by road depending on season and itinerary.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers who want an intimate, wildlife-first Serengeti experience: couples and honeymooners seeking seclusion, photographers chasing the migration, solo travellers comfortable with small mobile camps, and adventurous guests who prefer flexible, guide-led days over a fixed lodge routine.
facts.signature_experiences: Close-up seasonal migration viewing and calving season encounters, dawn and dusk game drives tailored for photographic results, lakeshore sundowners and private picnics, and guided bush walks when park rules and conditions allow.

faqs.q: What is & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas known for?
faqs.a: It is known as an intimate, seasonally mobile tented camp in the Serengeti ecosystem that places guests close to lakeshore wildlife concentrations and the seasonal migration.

faqs.q: How many rooms does & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas have?
faqs.a: The camp operates on a deliberately small scale with fewer than a dozen guest tents; the exact number can vary by season and the camp’s temporary location.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas?
faqs.a: June to October offers the best dry-season predator and plains viewing, while December to March is prime for calving season and close migration activity in the southern Serengeti.

faqs.q: Is & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas good for families?
faqs.a: The camp’s intimate, tented format is ideal for families who are comfortable with simple, mobile accommodation and who want wildlife-focused days; age restrictions and family-specific amenities should be confirmed with the operator.

faqs.q: How do you get to & Beyond Lake Serengeti Under Canvas?
faqs.a: Guests typically connect from Arusha or Kilimanjaro to a regional airstrip in the Serengeti or nearby, followed by a short drive into camp; road transfers from Arusha are also possible depending on itinerary and season.

faqs.q: Are game drives included at the camp?
faqs.a: Yes, game drives led by experienced guides are the core activity and are scheduled for early morning and late afternoon to match wildlife movement.

faqs.q: Does the camp move location during the year?
faqs.a: Yes, the camp is seasonally mobile and its position is adjusted to follow wildlife patterns and to maximise access to migration and calving areas when appropriate.

stays.name: &Beyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge
stays.tagline: Ten suites and a Star Dune Suite in a private desert reserve beside the NamibRand
stays.quote: Wake to the colors of sunrise over the desert, hike dunes, and fall asleep under a sky full of stars
stays.bestMonthsNote: April to October brings cooler temperatures and dramatic light; November to March is warmer with occasional rain.
stays.airportDirections: Scheduled or chartered flight to the lodge's private airstrip, with transfers included; or about 400 km by gravel road from Windhoek.

paras: Ten Suites sculpted from stone and glass, each with a private plunge pool, shaded veranda, lounge with fireplace, glass-encased rain shower and a skylight above the bed for stargazing. One Star Dune Suite joins two en-suite suites with a shared lounge, private dining area and veranda for up to four guests.

Big Dune walk with breakfast below. Dune walk at Deadvlei in Namib-Naukluft National Park. Living Dune experience by ATV. Desert Rock and Desert People experiences. Scenic desert drives. Self-guided e-biking and hiking. Guided stargazing. Hot air ballooning and scenic helicopter flights at extra cost.

Private plunge pools. Retractable skylights above every bed. On-site observatory with a Celestron telescope and expert astronomers. Walk-in wine cellar. Wellness floor with yoga, a desert-view gym and Healing Earth treatments. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and grey water recycling.

onlyHere: &Beyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge is for the stargazer and the explorer. Sleep beneath a skylight on the edge of Africa's first International Dark Sky Reserve, walk dunes in a private reserve where self-guided exploration is encouraged, and return to a suite with its own plunge pool. Suited to couples, families, solo travellers and friends.

why.title: Desert Dreaming, Stargazer's Paradise
why.body: &Beyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge pairs privacy and design with the freedom to explore the Namib at your own pace. Best for couples, families and solo travellers drawn to the desert, wellness and the night sky.

facts.best_months: Year-round: April to October for cooler days and dramatic light, November to March warmer with occasional rain.
facts.how_to_get_there: Scheduled or charter flight to the lodge's private airstrip with included transfers, or about 400 km by gravel road from Windhoek.
facts.signature_experiences: Observatory stargazing on the edge of Africa's first International Dark Sky Reserve, the Big Dune walk, ATV Living Dune outings and self-guided e-biking.
facts.who_its_for: Solo travellers, couples and friends in the Suites, and families or friends together in the Star Dune Suite.

faqs.q: Where is &Beyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: It is in southern Namibia, within the 12,715-hectare &Beyond Sossusvlei Private Desert Reserve, adjacent to the NamibRand Nature Reserve and Namib-Naukluft National Park. The reserve forms part of the Namib Sand Sea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

faqs.q: How do I get to &Beyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: Guests arrive by scheduled or chartered flight to the lodge's private airstrip, and transfers to and from the airstrip are included. Road transfers can be arranged, and self-drivers face about 400 km from Windhoek or 380 km from Swakopmund on gravel roads, with a 4x4 advised in the rainy season from November to May.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: &Beyond calls the desert a year-round destination. April to October brings cooler temperatures and dramatic light, while November to March is warmer with occasional rain.

faqs.q: How many suites does the lodge have?
faqs.a: There are ten Suites for up to two guests each, plus one Star Dune Suite for up to four. The Star Dune Suite is two en-suite suites joined by a shared lounge, private dining area and veranda.

faqs.q: Can children stay?
faqs.a: Yes. The Star Dune Suite is designed for families, and &Beyond's rates treat guests aged 17 and over as adults, with reduced rates for children up to 16 sharing with adults, subject to triple-room availability.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Guided stargazing at the on-site observatory, a Big Dune walk with breakfast below, the Living Dune ATV experience, Desert Rock and Desert People experiences, scenic drives and self-guided e-biking and hiking. Hot air ballooning and scenic helicopter flights cost extra.

faqs.q: Who is the lodge best for?
faqs.a: &Beyond describes the Suites as ideal for solo travellers, couples and friends sharing, and the Star Dune Suite for families and friends travelling together.

stays.name: & Beyond Vira Vira
stays.tagline: Nature, adventure, and flavor in the heart of Chile
stays.quote: Wake up to views of the Liucura River, explore forests and volcanoes, and savor a farm to table experience in Chile’s Lake District
stays.bestMonthsNote: October to April is warm and green, perfect for hiking, biking, river sports, and cultural festivals. The weather is mild, and all experiences are available.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Santiago, connect to Temuco or Pucón. Road transfer 1.5 to 2 hours to lodge from Temuco, 30 minutes from Pucón.

paras: Eighteen rooms and suites including villa suites on the river, hotel rooms, and a two-bedroom family villa, each with views of river, forest, or gardens, and contemporary Chilean design.

items: Relax in the hot tub or wellness spa
Outdoor hot tub and wellness center
Access to Villarica National Park and volcano

onlyHere: &Beyond Vira Vira is for the traveler who wants to blend comfort, adventure, and local flavor. Perfect for couples, families, food lovers, and outdoor enthusiasts who crave immersive nature and authentic experiences in the Lake District of Chile.

why.title: Where Adventure Meets Flavor
why.body: &Beyond Vira Vira Lodge offers the best of Chile’s Lake District, with daily activities, incredible food, and a setting of peaceful riverfront and wild forest. Best for active couples, families, and anyone seeking culinary discovery and outdoor thrills.

stays.name:
Benguerra Island 
 by & Beyond
stays.tagline: Where turquoise waters meet barefoot luxury
stays.quote: Wake up to the sound of the ocean, explore coral reefs, and unwind in your private beach paradise
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to October is dry, sunny, and best for beach, diving, and island exploration. November to April is warm and green, with calm seas and rich marine life.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Vilanculos, then 10 minute helicopter or 30 minute boat transfer to the lodge.

paras: Fifteen beachside cabanas, casinhas, and family villas, each with plunge pool, shaded deck, ocean views, and direct beach access. Traditional Mozambican style meets barefoot luxury.

items: White sand beaches and turquoise lagoons

onlyHere: Benguerra Island by &Beyond is for those seeking barefoot luxury, marine adventure, and island peace. Ideal for couples, honeymooners, families, solo travelers, and anyone who dreams of turquoise waters, vibrant reefs, and soulful relaxation.

why.title: Barefoot Luxury, Island Magic
why.body: Benguerra Island by &Beyond combines pristine beaches, marine adventures, and warm island hospitality. Best for couples, families, and ocean lovers who want comfort, privacy, and unique experiences in the Indian Ocean.

stays.name: & Beyond Chobe Under Canvas
stays.tagline: Glamp at the water’s edge in Botswana’s legendary Chobe
stays.quote: Fall asleep beneath the stars and wake to elephants wandering past your tent. This is safari at its purest, yet most comfortable.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These are the dry season months, when wildlife gathers at the river and sightings are at their best. Expect large elephant herds, excellent game viewing, and pleasant weather.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Kasane International Airport. It is a short drive and game-drive transfer into the park to the camp’s current location. Camp location changes every few days but transfers are always provided.

paras: Safari Tent for two guestsFive mobile tents set along the river

items: Morning game drives in Chobe National
ParkBoat safaris on the Chobe River
Relaxed afternoons in camp watching wildlife
Evening game drives and sunset drinks
Photographic boat experience on stays of two nights or more
Spacious walk-in tents with ensuite flush toilet and hot bucket shower
Unfenced camp with wildlife roaming freely
Simple solar lighting for true wilderness feel
Incredible elephant and wildlife viewing on your doorstep

onlyHere: Chobe Under Canvas is for travelers who want to get truly close to nature, unplug, and enjoy a small, authentic safari camp that moves with the seasons. The experience is perfect for couples, solo explorers, families, and anyone looking to experience wild Africa with just a handful of other guests. This is a rare chance to slow down, connect to the earth, and truly feel the spirit of Chobe.

why.body: Stay at Chobe Under Canvas to experience Botswana’s legendary wildlife at its best, from the comfort of a mobile camp set right on the Chobe River. This camp is ideal for couples seeking romance, families wanting adventure, solo travelers seeking connection, and anyone with a passion for wild spaces and conservation.

stays.name: andBeyond Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge
stays.tagline: Where wild rivers meet the great migration
stays.quote: Awaken to hippos stirring in the river, watch wildebeest cross at dawn, and unwind in the pure comfort of riverside luxury.
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to July is when the Great Migration often moves through the western corridor and may cross the Grumeti River. Other months bring fewer visitors and a more private Serengeti.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to the lodge airstrip; transfers between the airstrip and the lodge are included.

paras: Ten spacious river-facing suites, including one family suite, each featuring a private plunge pool, outdoor shower, and panoramic views across the Grumeti River.
Twice-daily game drives, hot air balloon safaris, guided nature walks, birding, stargazing, community visits, riverside yoga and in-suite wellness treatments.

A remarkable river setting alive with hippos and wildlife. Contemporary African design inspired by the Maasai manyatta. Private plunge pools. Family-friendly with the WILDchild programme. Interactive kitchen and starlit boma dinners. Built with sustainability at its core.

onlyHere: andBeyond Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge is made for travelers who want front row seats to river crossings, wildlife drama, and the gentle rhythm of the Serengeti. Ideal for couples, families, and solo travelers seeking a blend of wild authenticity and refined luxury.

why.title: River Drama and Migration Magic
why.body: andBeyond Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge delivers uncrowded riverfront wildlife viewing, Great Migration scenes from May to July, and beautiful contemporary suites. Best for couples, families, and solo travelers seeking comfort and action.

facts.best_months: May to July is when the Great Migration often passes through the western corridor, while other months offer a quieter, more private Serengeti.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to the lodge airstrip in the western Serengeti, with transfers between the airstrip and the lodge included.
facts.signature_experiences: Uncrowded game drives in the western corridor, Grumeti River migration crossings in season, guided walks and riverside yoga beside the resident hippos.
facts.who_its_for: Solo travellers, couples and friends sharing in the Suites, and families of up to two adults and two children in the Family Suite.

faqs.q: Where is &Beyond Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge?
faqs.a: Inside Serengeti National Park, in the remote western corridor. The lodge sits on a quiet tributary of the Grumeti River that is home to a resident pod of hippo.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge?
faqs.a: Many guests visit between May and July, when the Great Migration herds often move through the western corridor and may cross the Grumeti River. Travelling outside those months brings fewer visitors and a more private Serengeti.

faqs.q: How many suites does the lodge have?
faqs.a: Ten river-facing Suites, including one Family Suite. Each has a private plunge pool, a deep-soaking tub and views over the river.

faqs.q: Is Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The Family Suite adds a second, smaller bedroom for children and sleeps two adults and two children, and andBeyond's WILDchild programme is included in the rate.

faqs.q: What can you do at the lodge?
faqs.a: Twice-daily game drives, guided nature walks, birdwatching with over 350 species and stargazing are offered. Hot air balloon safaris, private riverside yoga, in-suite wellness treatments and a full-day visit to the Lukungu community are available at extra cost.

faqs.q: How do you get to Grumeti Serengeti River Lodge?
faqs.a: Guests fly to the lodge airstrip in the western Serengeti. Road transfers between the airstrip and the lodge are included in the rate.

faqs.q: Who is the lodge best suited to?
faqs.a: andBeyond describes the Suites as ideal for solo travellers, couples and friends sharing, and the Family Suite as made for families.

stays.name: &Beyond Kichwa Tembo Tented Camp
stays.tagline: The classic Mara camp on the edge of the migration
stays.quote: Wake up to the call of wildebeest, sip coffee overlooking the plains, and fall asleep under endless stars
stays.bestMonths: July to October, December to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: July to October is Great Migration season with river crossings and peak wildlife. December to March is lush and green, with excellent resident game and birding, plus fewer crowds.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Nairobi, connect by light aircraft to Kichwa Tembo Airstrip, 15 minute road transfer to camp.

paras: Forty tents including Superior View, Superior, and Classic, each with en-suite bathroom and private veranda, many with Mara or forest views, and family tents available.

items: Iconic Mara location for Great Migration
Beautiful pool with endless savanna views
Dedicated guides and private vehicles available

onlyHere: &Beyond Kichwa Tembo Tented Camp is for the classic safari lover who wants front row seats to the Mara and the migration, paired with warm hospitality, legendary views, and immersive experiences. Perfect for couples, families, solo travelers, and photographers seeking adventure with comfort.

why.title: The Heart of the Mara
why.body: &Beyond Kichwa Tembo Tented Camp offers the Masai Mara’s iconic wildlife, dramatic migration, and local culture in a stylish, family friendly setting. Best for families, couples, and photographers who want action and authenticity.

stays.name: &Beyond Klein’s Camp
stays.tagline: Private hills, wild Serengeti
stays.quote: Wake to sweeping valley views, watch the migration from your terrace, and explore private wilderness at the edge of the Serengeti
stays.bestMonths: June to October, January to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October is the dry season andBeyond recommends for safaris; November to March is great for birdwatching.
stays.airportDirections: Scheduled morning flights from Arusha to Klein's Airstrip, then a drive of about 1.5 hours to camp with game viewing en route. Flights to Lobo Airstrip are followed by a 1.5 to 2 hour drive.

paras: Ten cottages, each with private veranda, en-suite bathroom, and wide views of the valley and hills, plus one Family Cottage made of two cottages joined by an interleading walkway.

Exclusive 10,000 hectare private concession with off road safaris. Night drives and bush walks allowed. Lodge pool and lounge with panoramic vistas. Family friendly with kids activities. Locally inspired cuisine and private dining. Maasai-guided walks and community engagement.

onlyHere: &Beyond Klein’s Camp is for those who want a truly private Serengeti. With exclusive wilderness, night drives, off road safaris, and Maasai culture, it’s perfect for families, couples, and adventurers seeking privacy, flexibility, and the drama of the migration.

why.title: Your Private Serengeti
why.body: &Beyond Klein’s Camp delivers rare access to private wilderness, the Great Migration, and Maasai culture, with the freedom of night drives and personalized adventures. Best for couples, families, and wildlife enthusiasts seeking something special.

facts.best_months: June to October is andBeyond's recommended dry season for safaris, with November to March best for birdwatching.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly from Arusha to Klein's Airstrip, then drive about one and a half hours to camp with game viewing en route.
facts.signature_experiences: Off-road game viewing with only andBeyond vehicles, night game drives, bush walks and visits to a nearby Maasai boma.
facts.who_its_for: Families of all ages and travellers who want private game viewing, night drives and walking safaris on an exclusive concession.

faqs.q: Where is &Beyond Klein's Camp?
faqs.a: In a remote corner of the Serengeti, on a private 10,000 hectare (24,700 acre) wildlife concession leased from Maasai landlords. The camp sits on the edge of the Kuka Hills, looking down a valley that borders the Serengeti and the Masai Mara National Reserve.

faqs.q: How do you get to Klein's Camp?
faqs.a: Scheduled flights run each morning from Arusha to Klein's Airstrip, followed by a drive of about one and a half hours with game viewing on the way. andBeyond also lists morning flights to Lobo airstrip, followed by a one and a half to two hour drive.

faqs.q: How many cottages does Klein's Camp have?
faqs.a: Ten cottages, plus one Family Cottage made up of two cottages joined by an interleading walkway. Each cottage has a private verandah looking out over the hills.

faqs.q: Does Klein's Camp welcome children?
faqs.a: Yes, all ages are welcome. The WILDchild programme offers fun, interactive activities for children, and the Family Cottage suits families travelling together.

faqs.q: What makes Klein's Camp different from other Serengeti camps?
faqs.a: It is a private concession, so only andBeyond vehicles are at sightings and guides can drive off-road. Guests can also take night game drives and explore on foot, free from roads and vehicles.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Klein's Camp?
faqs.a: Game drives, night game drives, bush walks and birdwatching, plus breakfast, lunch or dinner served out on the concession. Guests can also visit a Maasai boma near camp to learn about daily life and culture.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Klein's Camp?
faqs.a: andBeyond's Tanzania advice names June to October, the dry season, as ideal for safaris. November to March is highlighted as a great time for birdwatching.

stays.name: Aguas Claras
stays.tagline: Artful Caribbean hideaway on Playa Chiquita
stays.quote: A soulful Caribbean escape where art, sea and rainforest fold into slow, private days.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Driest months on the Caribbean coast, with especially clear reef and rainforest conditions; May to mid December is Wildlife Season.
stays.airport: Limón Airstrip (LIO); Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO)
stays.airportDirections: 35-min flight SJO to LIO, then 60-min transfer; or 5h30m drive.

paras: Set beside Playa Chiquita, with its own private gate and pathway to the beach, Aguas Claras is an intimate 12-room retreat of 6 Pavlova Suites and 6 bungalows spread across jungle gardens. Rooms are furnished with locally made pieces and natural materials that reference the region's Afro-Caribbean heritage.

Days here move between the beach and the jungle: morning swims and snorkeling, afternoons by the pool, in a private plunge pool or at the DaLime Beach Club, and evenings at Papaya Restaurant or around a bonfire. The small scale means experiences are easy to personalize, whether you want a surf lesson, a Talamanca Bribrí cacao tour, or simply a hammock and a book.

Aguas Claras programs center on the dual rhythm of sea and forest. Mornings might include snorkeling at Punta Uva or along the coral reef in Cahuita National Park, 25 minutes away, or a surf lesson at Playa Cocles, while afternoons can be spent on a bike, hike or kayak tour.

Cultural experiences include the Talamanca Bribrí Reserve and Cacao Tour and evenings of live local music, bonfires and theme nights at Papaya. For slower days, the team arranges spa and wellness therapies in the privacy of your bungalow and optional yoga sessions.

Standout features: Papaya Restaurant, the DaLime Beach Club on Playa Chiquita, private plunge pools in the two-bedroom Deluxe Bungalows, a pool, spa and wellness therapies on your private veranda, optional full or half board plans, complimentary bicycles and free Wi-Fi. The property's small size enables tailored itineraries, with sustainable sourcing and community partnerships woven into operations.

onlyHere: Aguas Claras specializes in intimate Caribbean moments: bonfires with live local music, theme nights and impromptu acoustic gatherings at Papaya, and a private gate straight onto Playa Chiquita.

onlyHere: Conservation ledger

Kimana Sanctuary belongs to 844 Maasai landowners and covers 5,700 acres. Big Life Foundation holds the head lease and runs protection; Angama's tourism sub-lease commits over US$11 million to the landowning families across 25 years.
About 70% of the team was hired from nearby villages and towns. The Angama Foundation guest donation also supports elephant protection with Big Life.
Also: a raised rim-flow pool with an elephant drinking trough, the Mnara viewing tower, and an art gallery and weaving studio.

why.body: Angama Amboseli sits in Kimana Sanctuary, Kenya's first community-owned wildlife sanctuary, on the corridor that links Amboseli, the Chyulu Hills and Tsavo West. Kilimanjaro fills the view from bed, shower and pool.
Exclusive traversing in the sanctuary means night drives, walks and early pyjama safaris, with Amboseli National Park a half or full day away.

facts.best_months: June to October and January to February are the dry months, with the clearest Kilimanjaro views. The climate is warm year round.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly Safarilink from Nairobi Wilson to Kimana Airfield inside the sanctuary, charter from the Maasai Mara, or drive about 3.5 hours from Nairobi.
facts.who_its_for: Families (children of all ages, childminding 6 pm to 10 pm), photographers and travellers pairing the Mara with Kilimanjaro.
facts.signature_experiences: Night drives and walks in Kimana Sanctuary, day trips into Amboseli National Park, the Mnara tower at sunset, and a visit to Big Life Foundation HQ.

Family & Generational
Romantic Settings for Honeymoon and

onlyHere: Conservation ledger
The Angama Foundation, set up in 2015, is funded by a US$20 per person per night guest donation. It supports:

Schools: three classrooms and two early-childhood classrooms at Partakilat Primary, over 100 desks, 300 backpacks and five 10,000-litre water tanks for local schools, plus a scholarship programme for Saparingo Primary graduates.
Health: a community and staff clinic at the lodge with a full-time medical officer.

Wildlife: predator-proof bomas with the Anne K. Taylor Fund (99% success protecting livestock), an anti-poaching vehicle for rhino monitoring with the Mara Conservancy, and elephant collaring with the Mara Elephant Project.
Also: a one-acre Shamba garden where guests pick lunch, and a Beading Studio run by Maasai women.

why.body: Angama Mara sits 1,000 feet above the Mara Triangle on the Oloololo Escarpment, on the edge of the Great Rift Valley. A private road reaches the reserve in under 20 minutes, so game drives start fast and the view comes home with you.
Children of every age are welcome, which makes it one of the easier Mara lodges for families and generations travelling together.

facts.who_its_for: Families of all ages (no minimum age), honeymooners and photographers.

faqs.q: Where is Arenas del Mar?
faqs.a: Arenas del Mar is a beachfront and rainforest resort at Punta Quepos in Manuel Antonio, on Costa Rica's Central Pacific coast. It sits within an 11-acre private nature reserve that borders Manuel Antonio National Park.

faqs.q: How do you get to Arenas del Mar?
faqs.a: The quickest route is a 20-minute connecting flight from San José (SJO) to the Quepos airstrip (XQP) with Sansa or Green Airways, then a 15-minute transfer to the resort. By road it is about 3 hours from SJO or 4.5 hours from Liberia (LIR), and the resort can arrange a private driver from either airport.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Arenas del Mar?
faqs.a: The dry season runs December to April, with a short mini dry season in late July and early August. The resort calls May to November Wildlife Season, when rains feed the rivers and waterfalls; September and October are the rainiest months.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Arenas del Mar have?
faqs.a: Arenas del Mar has 37 suites and rooms: Ocean View Premium Suites, Ocean Breeze Suites, Ocean View Superior Rooms, Ocean Breeze Superior Rooms, Rainforest View Suites and the two-bedroom Playitas Suite. The Premium, Ocean Breeze and Playitas suites have private hot tubs on their balconies.

faqs.q: Is Arenas del Mar good for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes. The resort welcomes children of all ages, has two pools and kids' menus, and notes that nearby activities suit kids over six especially. The Playitas Suite sleeps up to 8 and connecting rooms are available.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Arenas del Mar?
faqs.a: Private walks in Manuel Antonio National Park with the resort's naturalist guides, surf lessons with in-house instructors on Espadilla Beach, mangrove kayaking, humpback whale watching in season, night walks on the property and treatments at Barisas Spa.

faqs.q: Who is Arenas del Mar best for?
faqs.a: Couples, honeymooners, families and nature lovers who want rainforest wildlife and the beach in one stay. The resort describes its guest as the traveler who seeks substance over scale.

stays.tagline: Lake Kariba panoramas, intimate safari comfort
stays.quote: Wake to expansive water views, spend the day between safari tracks and sunset cruises, and end beside a fire under a brilliant southern sky.
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to October for dry weather, clear lake views, and peak wildlife. November to April for lush scenery, baby animals, and birdlife.

paras: Set on the shores of Lake Kariba, Bumi Hills Safari Lodge pairs wide water panoramas with classic Zimbabwean safari experiences. The property's ten lake-view suites and the two-bedroom Baobab Villa all have private decks and en suite bathrooms that frame the light and movement on the water.

The main lodge concentrates relaxed luxury: an infinity pool that looks across the lake, a wellness spa and gym, a fire pit for evening storytelling, and a canvas-covered bar and open dining area on the viewing deck. The feel is informal but polished, equal parts family refuge and a base for serious wildlife days.

Days here are built around two landscapes: the shoreline and the plains. Morning and late-afternoon guided game drives track plains game and predators in the surrounding conservancy, while guided walking safaris bring you closer to spoor, birdsong, and the small dramas of bush life.

On the water, launch for calm lake cruises and sunset trips that concentrate birdlife, fishing opportunities, and wide photographic horizons. Cultural village visits, optional spa treatments, and evening stargazing round out a program that balances active days with slow, restorative moments by the lake.

Infinity pool overlooking Lake Kariba. Ten lake-view suites with air-conditioning, freestanding baths, indoor and outdoor showers and private viewing decks, plus the private two-bedroom Baobab Villa with its own butler, guide and safari vehicle. Wellness spa and gym. Canvas-covered bar and open dining area on the viewing deck. Game drives, walking safaris, boat cruises, fishing and birdwatching with the lodge's guides.

onlyHere: What is unique to Bumi Hills is the pairing of lake life and classic Zimbabwean safari from a single, intimate lodge: within a day you can track game in the bush, then be on the water for a sunset cruise photographing reflected skies.

The Baobab Villa provides a private, residential feel that works for families or small groups who want a villa of their own combined with the lodge's guiding and activity program, creating moments that feel both private and rooted in place.

why.body: LAKEFRONT PERSPECTIVE Lake Kariba at sunrise and sunset, experienced from private decks, the infinity pool, and evening cruises that make the water another dimension of your safari.

WATER AND BUSH, FROM ONE BASE Combine guided game drives and walking safaris with lake cruises, fishing, and birdwatching without changing lodges: you get both the bush rhythms of Zimbabwe and slow water days on Kariba.

FAMILY-FRIENDLY VILLA The two-bedroom Baobab Villa gives families or small groups their own living room, bar and dining decks, with a private butler, guide and vehicle, and the Ngwana Club offers activities for children of all ages.
GUIDED ON LAND AND WATER The lodge's guides lead game drives, night drives, walking safaris for those over 16, boat cruises and birding.

facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Bumi Hills Airstrip, about 1 hour 30 minutes from Harare, then a 5-minute transfer to the lodge.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives and walks on a private concession, sunset cruises and fishing on Lake Kariba, and the Lady Jacqueline houseboat.
facts.who_its_for: Families and travellers who want lake and bush safari from one lodge, with a private villa option.

faqs.q: Where is Bumi Hills Safari Lodge?
faqs.a: Bumi Hills sits on a ridge overlooking Lake Kariba in northern Zimbabwe, on its own private safari concession next to Matusadona National Park.

faqs.q: How do you get to Bumi Hills Safari Lodge?
faqs.a: Fly to Bumi Hills Airstrip, then a 5-minute transfer to camp. African Bush Camps gives flight times of about 1 hour 30 minutes from Harare, 1 hour 40 minutes from Victoria Falls, 30 minutes from Mana Pools and 1 hour 30 minutes from Hwange.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Bumi Hills Safari Lodge have?
faqs.a: There are ten lake-view suites, including one interleading pair, plus the private two-bedroom Baobab Villa with its own butler, guide and safari vehicle.

faqs.q: Is Bumi Hills Safari Lodge good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no age restriction, the Ngwana Club runs activities for children of all ages, and the Baobab Villa is designed for families. Walking safaris are limited to children over 16.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Bumi Hills?
faqs.a: Game drives, night drives, walking safaris, boat cruises at sunrise and sunset, catch-and-release fishing, birdwatching and cultural tours, plus half-day or overnight trips aboard the houseboat Lady Jacqueline.

faqs.q: Can you see rhino from Bumi Hills?
faqs.a: Black rhino have returned to neighbouring Matusadona National Park, and from 1 September 2026 the lodge offers a game drive, walking safari and dedicated Conservation Experience in the park.

stays.tagline: Floating tents on the Tatai River at the foot of the Cardamom Mountains, run since 2009 by the couple who built them.

why.title: Place
why.body: The Tatai River runs out of the Cardamom Mountains through mangrove and rainforest in Cambodia's far south-west, and the camp floats on it: thirteen tents on the water and five family tents on land, reached only by boat.

why.title: People
why.body: Valentin and Anna, husband and wife, opened Canvas & Orchids in 2009 and still run it. They describe it as the world's first floating tented camp, and they built it to work for the villages around it.

why.title: Impact
why.body: The camp's team comes from the local villages, among them former poachers and hunters who now work as cooks, boat drivers and guides (as the camp reports on its own site).

why.title: James' note
why.body: I haven't slept on the Tatai yet. But a camp where the man steering your boat used to hunt in these hills is a better conservation argument than any brochure, and fireflies over a river is not something you forget.

facts.how_to_get_there: On the Tatai River in Koh Kong Province, about 278 km from Phnom Penh and 20 km from Koh Kong City. The last stretch is by the camp's own boat from its dock before Tatai Bridge; transfers run daily at no charge.
facts.signature_experiences: Sleeping in a floating tent on the river; fireflies and river sunsets; the mangroves, the waterfall and the Cardamom Mountains behind; days out with a local team, some of them former hunters, as guides and boat drivers.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and families who want rainforest, river and fireflies, and a stay that pays local people well.

stays.name: Cap Karoso

why.body: Cap Karoso is more than a stay. It’s your gateway to the soul of Sumba. Rooted in culture, wrapped in nature, and elevated by conscious luxury, this is where slow exploration meets refined indulgence. Let us guide your journey. One rich in flavor, discovery, and unforgettable connection.

Cap Karoso is where design‑led architecture, regenerative farming, community empowerment and immersive island rituals converge in a traveler’s dream. Perfect for: Adventure & Nature seekers discovering Suma’s wild coast; Wellness & Health travelers drawn to spa, shamanic healing, yoga; Conservation & Eco Mindfulness visitors valuing regenerative impact; Couples & Honeymooners craving seclusion and bespoke dining; Creative Epicureans eager for chef residencies and farm‑driven gastronomy.

why.body: Capella Lodge brings polished comfort to one of Australia’s most extraordinary island settings. Beneath Mount Gower and Mount Lidgbird, its suites sit close to Lord Howe Island’s lagoon, beaches and protected marine environments. Days can unfold on guided walks, reef excursions or the mountain trail, then return to thoughtful dining, spa time and unhurried views. It is a rare combination of World Heritage wilderness and intimate, service-led accommodation.

faqs.q: What is Beckon Capella Lodge known for?
faqs.a: Beckon Capella Lodge is known for refined island accommodation on Lord Howe Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed destination. It combines personalised hospitality, fine dining and spa experiences with access to volcanic peaks, beaches, lagoon waters and coral reefs.

faqs.q: How do you get to Beckon Capella Lodge?

faqs.a: Experiences include guided island walks, Mount Gower treks, snorkelling, glass-bottom boat tours, bird watching and other marine adventures. Guests can also spend time at the Capella Spa or enjoy island dining.

Whether you are a wellness seeker, a nature lover, or a couple longing for romance deep in the forest, this is where you dissolve distractions. Families and solo travelers alike will find restorative silence and tailored adventures, from Mayan ceremonies to bee‑keeping and cenote soaks.

why.body: Chablé Yucatán offers a profound pause in the Mayan forest, where ancient energies, modern luxury, and ecological care converge. stays.name: Chablé Maroma
stays.tagline: Seventy private pool villas on Maroma Beach in the Riviera Maya
stays.bestMonthsNote: Chablé names December to April as the best time to visit, when the Riviera Maya is warm and dry and ideal for the beach.
stays.airportDirections: About 35 to 40 minutes by car from Cancún International Airport. Chablé can arrange private transfers.

paras: Seventy villas designed by Paulina Morán, each with a private outdoor terrace and plunge pool, floor-to-ceiling windows and indoor-outdoor showers, including the Chablé signature moon shower. Treetop Pool Villas and Treetop Double Pool Villas sit on the second floor among the trees; Jungle Pool Villas are steps from the sand; and Serenity Pool Villas have a heated plunge pool and space for two.

Beach yoga, kayaking, paddle boarding and snorkelling on the Mesoamerican reef, with cenote diving, catamaran sailing and visits to Mayan sites such as Tulum and Cobá further afield. Mayan recipe workshops with local home cooks, tasting dinners and mixology classes fill the slower days.

Set in the protected Reserve of Punta Maroma, 12 miles north of Playa del Carmen, with a 650-foot private beach on the Caribbean. All Chablé restaurants are led by chef Jorge Vallejo of Quintonil in Mexico City: Bu'ul for contemporary Mexican cuisine and a wine list, Kaban for coastal flavours from the Pacific to the Riviera Maya, and the Raw Bar, a terrace cocktail bar facing the sea. The spa centres on the ocean, with a hydrotherapy circuit, the Mayan water ceremony and a temazcal.

onlyHere: A villa with its own plunge pool and moon shower in a protected stretch of jungle, a private beach on the Caribbean, and Jorge Vallejo's cooking at every table.

why.title: Jungle Villas on a Caribbean Beach
why.body: Best for couples and honeymooners after privacy and wellness by the sea.

facts.best_months: December to April, warm and dry.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 35 to 40 minutes by car from Cancún (CUN).
facts.signature_experiences: The water ceremony and temazcal, cenote diving and Jorge Vallejo's cooking.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, honeymooners and wellness seekers who want a private pool villa by the sea.

faqs.q: Where is Chablé Maroma?
faqs.a: On Maroma Beach in the Reserve of Punta Maroma, Riviera Maya, 12 miles north of Playa del Carmen in Quintana Roo, Mexico.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chablé Maroma?
faqs.a: Fly into Cancún International Airport (CUN); the drive takes about 35 to 40 minutes and Chablé can arrange private transfers.

faqs.q: What villas does Chablé Maroma have?
faqs.a: Seventy villas, each with a private terrace and plunge pool: Treetop Pool Villas and Treetop Double Pool Villas, Jungle Pool Villas and Serenity Pool Villas.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Chablé Maroma?
faqs.a: Yes, families are welcome, though Chablé says the resort especially suits guests seeking tranquillity. Treetop villas take two adults and two children, Jungle Pool Villas two adults and one child under 12, and Serenity Pool Villas two guests.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Chablé Maroma?
faqs.a: Chablé recommends December to April, when the weather is warm and dry and ideal for the beach.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Chablé Maroma?
faqs.a: The ocean-centred spa with its water ceremony and temazcal, cenote diving and reef snorkelling, and dining by chef Jorge Vallejo at Bu'ul, Kaban and the Raw Bar.

faqs.q: Who is Chablé Maroma best for?
faqs.a: Couples and honeymooners seeking privacy, beachfront time and wellness.

Walking safaris and game drives with experienced guides
Three chalets, with a maximum of six guests in camp

onlyHere: Chamilandu is perfect for couples, honeymooners, and solo travelers who want close encounters with wildlife, romance in the trees, and quiet adventure in a pristine, remote setting.

why.title: Treehouse Dreams, Wild River

facts.best_months: Open 3 June to 1 November, with peak game viewing from mid-June to October.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport, then about a 2 hour 45 minute game drive transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Walking safaris, treehouse river views and wildlife viewing from the veranda and lagoon hideout.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and walkers who want a three-chalet camp with no more than six guests.

faqs.q: Where is Chamilandu?
faqs.a: Chamilandu is perched on stilts beneath ebony trees on a bend of the Luangwa River in South Luangwa National Park, Zambia, looking towards the Chindeni Hills. It is inside The Bushcamp Company's exclusive 140,000-acre concession.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chamilandu?
faqs.a: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport (MFU). The transfer to camp takes about 2 hours 45 minutes, with a refreshment stop at Mfuwe Lodge and game viewing on the way.

faqs.q: When is Chamilandu open?
faqs.a: Chamilandu is open from 3 June to 1 November. The Bushcamp Company's peak season runs from mid-June to October, when wildlife concentrates along the river.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Chamilandu have?
faqs.a: There are three thatched treehouse chalets raised on stilts, with a maximum of six guests in camp.

faqs.q: Are children welcome at Chamilandu?
faqs.a: The Bushcamp Company lists 12 as the minimum age for walking safaris at Chamilandu.

faqs.q: What can you do at Chamilandu?
faqs.a: Walking safaris, game drives and sundowners, plus wildlife viewing from your veranda and the lagoon hideout. Inter-camp walks link Chindeni and Chamilandu.

faqs.q: Who is Chamilandu best for?
faqs.a: Travellers who want a three-chalet camp with no more than six guests, river views from a treehouse and walking at the heart of the stay.

facts.who_its_for: Couples, honeymooners, families with children aged 4 and older, and anyone wanting a slow, privately guided safari with wellness built in.

faqs.q: Where is Chem Chem Lodge?
faqs.a: Chem Chem Lodge sits within the exclusive-use Burunge Wildlife Management Area in northern Tanzania, between Lake Manyara and Tarangire national parks. The lodge lies in a wildlife corridor that connects the Tarangire and Manyara ecosystems.

faqs.q: How do I get to Chem Chem Lodge?
faqs.a: Fly from Kilimanjaro or Arusha to Chem Chem Airstrip on Miracle Air scheduled or private charter flights, usually 20 to 40 minutes depending on routing. From the airstrip it is a short game drive transfer to the lodge, and arrival and departure transfers are included.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Chem Chem Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge is open year-round apart from a short break from early April to mid-May. Auberge Safari describes June to mid-November as the dry season, with short rains usually from mid-November to early December.

faqs.q: How many suites does Chem Chem Lodge have?
faqs.a: There are seven tented suites and one family unit, each set well apart from the next with a private verandah and indoor and outdoor showers. The lodge also has a swimming pool, a fully-equipped gym and a spa.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Chem Chem Lodge?
faqs.a: Yes. Children aged 4 and older are welcome, and the two-bedroom family unit sleeps up to 2 adults and 3 children. Walking safaris are for guests aged 12 and over, and children of all ages are welcome when the lodge is booked exclusively.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Chem Chem Lodge?
faqs.a: Game drives with your own private guide and vehicle, a silent walk, a run with the Maasai, wild dining and Maasai celebrations. Stays are all-inclusive, covering meals and drinks, unlimited game drives, select cultural experiences and airstrip transfers.

faqs.q: Who is Chem Chem Lodge best for?
faqs.a: Travellers who want an unhurried, privately guided safari: the lodge calls itself the birthplace of the Slow Safari. Its wellness offering includes silent walks, runs with Maasai warriors and spa rituals, and it suits families with children aged 4 and up.

stays.name: Chiawa Camp
stays.tagline: The pioneer camp of the Lower Zambezi, shaped by the river and the wild.
stays.quote: Wake to the sounds of the Zambezi and experience safari at nature’s pace.
stays.bestMonthsNote: The dry season offers ideal wildlife viewing as animals gather along the Zambezi River and floodplains. Cooler weather also creates excellent conditions for canoe safaris, walking safaris, and wildlife photography.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Lusaka (LUN), then take a 35-minute Proflight flight to Jeki Airstrip (JEK).

paras: Safari Tents (eight, each about 100 square metres with a bench wallow plunge pool). Safari Suite (almost 220 square metres with a private plunge pool). Safari Sleepout (an open-air star bed on the Zambezi).

items: Riverfront camp under mahogany trees on the Zambezi
Pioneer camp of the Lower Zambezi National Park, since 1989
Safari tents with bench wallow plunge pools
Swimming pool and exercise area overlooking the river
Walking safaris with an award-winning guiding team

onlyHere: Chiawa Camp is the pioneer of the Lower Zambezi National Park, the first camp to settle on the banks of the Zambezi River, where the Cumings family created the park's first photo safari operation in 1989. It is a gentle, unhurried safari built around river and walking adventures with an award-winning guiding team.

facts.best_months: May to mid-November, with prime game viewing from June; closed mid-November through April.
facts.how_to_get_there: A 35-minute flight from Lusaka to Jeki Airstrip, with seasonal non-stop flights from Mfuwe and Livingstone.
facts.signature_experiences: Canoeing, walking safaris, day and night game drives, river safaris and catch-and-release angling on the Zambezi.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, honeymooners and families with children aged 8 and over who want river and walking safaris.

faqs.q: Where is Chiawa Camp?
faqs.a: On the banks of the Zambezi River under a grove of mahogany trees in the heart of Zambia's Lower Zambezi National Park. It was the first camp in the park, where the Cumings family started the first photo safari operation in 1989.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chiawa Camp?
faqs.a: Fly into Lusaka (LUN), then take a 35-minute Proflight flight to Jeki Airstrip (JEK). From June to October there are usually non-stop flights to Jeki from Mfuwe (90 minutes) and Livingstone (100 minutes).

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Chiawa Camp?
faqs.a: From May to November, with prime game viewing from June. Chiawa's camps are closed from mid-November through April.

faqs.q: How many tents does Chiawa Camp have?
faqs.a: Eight Safari Tents of about 100 square metres each plus the Safari Suite of almost 220 square metres. A Safari Sleepout star bed on the river can be added for a night.

faqs.q: Does Chiawa Camp accept children?
faqs.a: The minimum age at Chiawa Camp is 8. Children from 5 can stay in the Safari Suite but are kept out of the social areas unless the camp is booked on an exclusive-use basis.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Chiawa Camp?
faqs.a: Canoeing, walking safaris, day and night game drives, river safaris, catch-and-release angling and wildlife hides, all with Chiawa's guides.

faqs.q: Who is Chiawa Camp best for?
faqs.a: Travellers wanting a gentle, unhurried river safari with walking and canoeing; Chiawa also positions the camp for honeymoons, anniversaries and other special occasions.

stays.name: Chindeni Lodge
stays.tagline: Elevated lagoon tents, wild Luangwa, Chindeni Hills views
stays.quote: Wake up to hippos grunting in the mist, watch elephants cross the lagoon, and fall asleep above the wild. Chindeni is a dream for nature lovers
stays.bestMonthsNote: Open 15 May to 1 November; peak game viewing mid-June to October.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Mfuwe (MFU), then about a 2 hour 15 minute game drive transfer.

paras: Four elevated Meru-style tents beneath ancient ebony trees, one of them a family suite. Each has wooden floors, a four-poster bed, a private plunge pool, indoor and outdoor showers and a private veranda overlooking the lagoon. The main area is decking on several levels around the ebony trees, with dining area, lounge and bar.
Guided walking safaris, including inter-camp walks to Chamilandu and Bilimungwe. Day and night game drives. Birdwatching. Lagoon wildlife viewing from camp. Sundowners.

items: Elevated tents with private plunge pools
Small camp of four tents, including a family suite

onlyHere: Chindeni is perfect for couples, honeymooners, small groups, and solo travelers who want romance, adventure, and iconic South Luangwa wildlife at their doorstep.

why.title: Sleep Above the Wild
why.body: Best for those seeking seclusion, breathtaking views, and close encounters with hippos, elephants, and birds. Ideal for anyone who wants the romance of wild Africa in style.

facts.best_months: Open 15 May to 1 November, with peak game viewing from mid-June to October.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport, then about a 2 hour 15 minute game drive transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Walking safaris including inter-camp walks, night drives and lagoon wildlife viewing from camp.
facts.who_its_for: Walkers, couples and families with older children who want a four-tent lagoon camp.

faqs.q: Where is Chindeni?
faqs.a: Chindeni is on the edge of a permanent lagoon in a remote area of South Luangwa National Park, Zambia, with the Chindeni Hills behind it. It sits inside The Bushcamp Company's exclusive 140,000-acre concession.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chindeni?
faqs.a: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport (MFU). The transfer to camp takes about 2 hours 15 minutes, with a refreshment stop at Mfuwe Lodge and game viewing along the way.

faqs.q: When is Chindeni open?
faqs.a: Chindeni is open from 15 May to 1 November. The Bushcamp Company's peak season runs from mid-June to October, when wildlife gathers at the remaining water.

faqs.q: How many tents does Chindeni have?
faqs.a: There are four elevated Meru-style tents, one of them a family suite. Each has a private plunge pool, outdoor shower and a veranda over the lagoon.

faqs.q: Are children welcome at Chindeni?
faqs.a: There is a family suite, and 12 is the minimum age for walking safaris.

faqs.q: What can you do at Chindeni?
faqs.a: Walking safaris, including inter-camp walks to Chamilandu and Bilimungwe, day and night drives and sundowners. Giraffe, puku, buffalo, elephant and hippo visit the lagoon in front of camp, and its surroundings are leopard habitat.

faqs.q: Who is Chindeni best for?
faqs.a: Walkers and wildlife lovers who want a small, four-tent camp on a lagoon, as part of a Bushcamp Company circuit.

stays.name: Chisa Busanga Camp
stays.tagline: Four weaver-nest rooms on the Busanga Plains
stays.bestMonthsNote: Open 1 May to 1 November; the plains open as the floods recede.
stays.airportDirections: Light-aircraft flights from Lusaka or Livingstone to Busanga Plains Airstrip, then a 20-minute drive.

paras: Four Nests inspired by weaver bird nests, each with a window above the bed for stargazing. The whole camp can be booked privately.

items: Game drives across the watery dambos

paras: On a small tree-lined island on the Busanga Plains in northern Kafue National Park. Chisa is the Nyanja word for bird's nest. Solar powered camp and game vehicles.

onlyHere: The Busanga Plains are among Africa's most untouched wilderness: rosy morning mist, elephants crossing the floodplain and muddy lion prides, with only four Nests to share it.

why.title: Inside the Horizon
why.body: Best for small groups, families taking the whole camp and solo travelers.

facts.best_months: Open 1 May to 1 November, with the plains opening up as floodwaters recede from June.
facts.how_to_get_there: A flight to Busanga Airstrip from Lusaka or Livingstone, then a 20-minute drive to camp.
facts.signature_experiences: Sleeping in one of four tree-level Nests above the Busanga Plains, with solar e-Cruiser drives, e-bikes and walking safaris.
facts.who_its_for: Small groups taking the whole camp, couples and solo travellers.

faqs.q: Where is Chisa Busanga Camp?
faqs.a: Chisa sits on a small tree-lined island on the Busanga Plains in the northern part of Kafue National Park, Zambia.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chisa Busanga Camp?
faqs.a: Fly to Busanga Airstrip, about a 20-minute drive from camp. Green Safaris lists Skytrails flights from Lusaka (1 hr 15 to 1 hr 40) and Livingstone (1 hr 45 to 2 hr 15).

faqs.q: When can you visit Chisa Busanga?
faqs.a: The camp is open from 1 May to 1 November. Green Safaris says the plains become accessible as the floodwaters recede over June to November, and the camp closes in the wet season.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Chisa have?
faqs.a: Four Nests, raised on stilts and inspired by weaver bird nests, including a Nest With Lift. The whole camp can be booked privately.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Chisa?
faqs.a: Solar-powered e-Cruiser game drives across the dambos, walking safaris with an armed scout, guided e-bike outings, birding among some 450 species and boma dinners.

faqs.q: Who is Chisa Busanga best for?
faqs.a: Small groups or families taking the whole camp, couples and solo travellers who want a quiet, low-impact safari.

stays.name: Chumbe Island, Zanzibar
stays.tagline: Where Coral, Culture, and Conservation Meet
stays.quote: Discover an island sanctuary where sustainability leads the way and every sunrise brings a new marine adventure.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dry months bring the best visibility for snorkeling and calm seas for island life; green season is lush and peaceful.
stays.airportDirections: Arrive at Zanzibar (ZNZ); Chumbe's scheduled boat transfer from its Mbweni base is included.

paras: Seven Eco-Bungalows. Private Island.

Award-winning eco-lodge with seven solar-powered bungalows. Open-air bathrooms and sea views. Rainwater harvesting and composting toilets. All meals included. All waste managed sustainably. Solar energy throughout. Only accessible by boat.

onlyHere: Chumbe Island is ideal for couples, eco-minded families, solo adventurers, and groups who want to reconnect with nature and each other. Experience real sustainability, a private coral reserve, and a true escape from the modern world, barefoot and blissful.

why.title: Sleep on a Living Reef
why.body: Stay at Chumbe for world-class snorkeling, conservation, and off-grid comfort in a place where every stay helps preserve coral reefs and local communities. Perfect for adventure seekers, marine lovers, and travelers who want meaning with their magic.

facts.best_months: Chumbe does not name a best month, but full intertidal walks around the island are only possible at spring low tides near new and full moon.
facts.how_to_get_there: Take Chumbe's scheduled boat transfer from Zanzibar, included in the Full Package, with private boats available to match flights.
facts.signature_experiences: Snorkelling the protected Chumbe Reef, the coral rag forest walk, intertidal walks and the evening coconut crab walk.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, solo travellers and families who want an off-grid eco-lodge where every stay funds reef conservation and education.

faqs.q: Where is Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: About 8 km west of Unguja, the main island of Zanzibar. Chumbe is a small, privately managed conservation area with a Coral Reef Sanctuary and Forest Reserve, gazetted in 1994 as Tanzania's first marine protected area.

faqs.q: How do you get to Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: By boat. Scheduled boat transfers to and from the island are included in the Full Package, Chumbe's office is at Mbweni, and private boats can be arranged to fit flight times.

faqs.q: How many bungalows are there on Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: Seven solar-powered eco-bungalows set between the beach and the forest: two Seafront Bungalows, Seaview Bungalows and a single-storey Garden Bungalow. Each has a king-size bed and a self-contained bathroom with a composting toilet.

faqs.q: Can children stay on Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: Yes, children are welcome and baby cots are available on request. Chumbe notes that the ground is rocky, the bungalows are very open, including the upstairs sleeping platforms, and there is no babysitting service.

faqs.q: What activities are included at Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: All activities are included in an overnight stay: guided snorkelling on the protected reef, the forest walk, intertidal walks, the evening coconut crab walk and birding from the bird hide. Guests can also climb the 132 steps of the 1904 lighthouse.

faqs.q: What makes Chumbe Island an eco-lodge?
faqs.a: The bungalows are built with renewable materials, powered by the sun, collect and clean their own rainwater and manage all waste sustainably. Lodge revenue funds the island's conservation and free environmental education for local school children.

faqs.q: What is the food like on Chumbe Island?
faqs.a: Stays are full board, with a daily selection of Swahili dishes made from locally sourced ingredients. Chumbe buys only fresh fish from local fishers under a sustainable seafood policy, and vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free and lactose-free dishes are offered.

stays.name: Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge
stays.tagline: Extraordinary wilderness. Uncompromising luxury.
stays.quote: Adventure becomes unforgettable when luxury disappears into nature.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Late spring through early autumn provides ideal conditions for wildlife viewing, kayaking, horseback riding, hiking, and heli-adventures. Summer offers the warmest temperatures, while September and October deliver fewer visitors and spectacular wilderness scenery.
stays.airport: Tofino-Long Beach Airport (YAZ) Vancouver International Airport (YVR) Victoria International Airport (YYJ)

onlyHere: At Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge, luxury is not defined by what surrounds you, but by how deeply you connect with the natural world. Hidden within ancient temperate rainforest and accessible only by water or air, this is a place where grizzly bears roam nearby valleys, whales breach offshore, and every day offers a new adventure.

stays.name: Coco Costa Rica

items: Bedroom and living pods suspended above the treetops

onlyHere: Breaking architectural conventions, the Coco shelters at Art Villas are intimate bedroom and living pods hung above the treetops, joined by cushion-dotted wooden skybridges, resting nets and trampoline landings.

why.title: Glamping in the treetops
why.body: The Coco suits couples who want to sleep among the canopy in a playful, design-led pod, with the rest of Art Villas and its concierge close by.

facts.best_months: Art Villas does not name a best season on its own site; ask James Wild & Co for seasonal timing.
facts.how_to_get_there: Self-drive to Punta Achiote road, Playa Hermosa, Dominical; Art Villas says a 4x4 vehicle is a must.
facts.signature_experiences: Treetop pods with skybridge walkways, resting nets and trampoline landings, plus concierge-arranged waterfall, boat and chocolate trips.
facts.who_its_for: Couples looking for design-led glamping in pods suspended above the jungle.

faqs.q: What is Coco Costa Rica?
faqs.a: The Coco is the glamping area at Art Villas, a small owner-run resort with two architect-designed villas. Its private Coco shelters are bedroom and living pods suspended above the treetops, linked by skybridge-style wooden walkways, resting nets and trampoline landings.

faqs.q: Where is The Coco?
faqs.a: At Art Villas on Punta Achiote road, Playa Hermosa, Dominical, in the Osa area of Costa Rica's Pacific coast, in jungle overlooking the ocean.

faqs.q: How do you get to The Coco?
faqs.a: Art Villas asks every guest to arrive with a 4x4 vehicle, which it calls a must have. The concierge, reachable on WhatsApp, can help with arrival details.

faqs.q: How many Coco pods are there?
faqs.a: There are four pods, Coco 1 to Coco 4, each with its own shower, bathroom and walk-in closet; Coco 1 is the largest, with a premium bathtub and a resting net. Art Villas lists the Coco unit for 2 guests, with 1 bedroom and 1 bathroom.

faqs.q: Who is The Coco best for?
faqs.a: Couples who want a playful, architecture-led take on glamping. Art Villas notes that Coco 3 is closest to the restaurant, which limits privacy.

faqs.q: What experiences can Art Villas arrange?
faqs.a: The concierge can arrange boat trips, local waterfall trips, an indigenous village visit, horseback riding, a chocolate plantation experience, a local cooking class and massages or spa treatments.

faqs.q: What is Coco Plum Island Resort known for?
faqs.a: Coco Plum Island Resort is known for its private island setting off Belize’s southern coast and its relaxed, sea-focused atmosphere. It offers a secluded base for enjoying the Caribbean and nearby reef waters.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Coco Plum Island Resort have?
faqs.a: The available property information does not specify the number of rooms. Confirm current room inventory directly with the resort before booking.

faqs.a: The island setting lends itself to time on the water, including snorkeling, kayaking, fishing and boat excursions. Ask the resort which activities are available and whether they require advance arrangements.

stays.name: Coot Club

onlyHere: Coot Club is for families, couples, friends, and solo travelers looking for playful riverside days, wild Overberg beauty, and the freedom to reconnect with nature and each other.

why.body: Coot Club is perfect for families, nature lovers, couples, and friends who want river adventures, Cape wilderness, and space to relax and play, all within easy reach of Stanford and Hermanus.

facts.signature_experiences: Kayaking, sailing and SUP from private water access.

faqs.a: Coot Club is on the R326 at Stanford in the Western Cape, within easy reach of Stanford and Hermanus.

faqs.q: How do you get to Coot Club?

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Coot Club?
faqs.a: September to April, for sunny days, warm river swimming and family activities. May to August suits peaceful escapes and birding.

faqs.q: Is Coot Club good for families?

faqs.q: What can you do at Coot Club?
faqs.a: Kayaking, sailing and SUP, river cruises, cycling, guided nature walks, birdwatching and farm activities.

stays.name: Cork’s Vienna Woods
stays.tagline: A historic country retreat in the woods of Cork.
stays.quote: Step away from the ordinary and into a place with history, woodland and soul.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Spring through early autumn is an especially appealing time to experience Vienna Woods because the woodland setting becomes part of the stay. Longer days also make it easier to combine walks, Cork City exploration, family adventures and time outdoors.
stays.airportDirections: The property is located in Glanmire, just a few minutes' drive from Cork City.
onlyHere: Vienna Woods gives travelers the rare feeling of being surrounded by nature while remaining only minutes from Cork City. The story begins in 1756, when Davis Ducart built the house as a summer lodge for Lord Barrymore. Today, that history lives alongside the warmth of a peaceful country retreat.

A single eco-camp on Wizard Island, with communal areas and sea views.
Saltwater fly fishing with Alphonse Fishing Company on vast, wadeable sand flats.
Scuba diving among schooling reef fish, pelagics and sharks (pre-book through Blue Safari).
Snorkelling, including manta ray snorkelling with the activities team.
Blue Safari excursions offshore, with encounters that change by season.
Nesting green turtles, hawksbill turtles and large seabird populations around the atoll.
The only camp on Cosmoledo Atoll, set on Wizard Island.
Private deck and outdoor shower at every Eco Pod.
Amenities from Africology.
Farm-to-table cuisine with produce from The Farm on Alphonse Island and line-caught fish.

onlyHere: Cosmoledo Atoll lies just over 1,000 km from Mahé, a short distance from the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aldabra, in the Aldabra Group. Blue Safari counts 21 islands, over 120 species of healthy coral, a large population of nesting green turtles and the largest population of hawksbill turtles in the Aldabra group, with vast wadeable sand flats around the lagoon.

why.title: Eight pods on a far atoll near Aldabra

faqs.q: Where is Cosmoledo Eco Camp?

faqs.q: How many rooms does Cosmoledo Eco Camp have?

faqs.q: Can children stay at Cosmoledo Eco Camp?
faqs.a: Blue Safari lists the Eco Pods for two adults and does not publish a children's policy for Cosmoledo. Ask us and we will confirm with Blue Safari for your dates.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Cosmoledo?
faqs.a: Blue Safari does not publish a best season for Cosmoledo. Its offshore Blue Safari excursions bring different encounters by season, so we plan your dates around what you most want to do, whether fly fishing, diving or turtles.

faqs.q: What can you do at Cosmoledo Eco Camp?
faqs.a: Saltwater fly fishing with Alphonse Fishing Company on wadeable sand flats, scuba diving, snorkelling including manta ray snorkelling, and Blue Safari offshore excursions. The atoll has nesting green turtles, hawksbill turtles and large bird populations. Diving must be pre-booked through Blue Safari.

faqs.q: Who is Cosmoledo Eco Camp best for?
faqs.a: Fly fishers, divers and couples who want an eight-pod eco-camp on a remote atoll near Aldabra, with turtles, seabirds and wadeable flats.

faqs.q: Where is Dulini Anabezi?
faqs.a: On the banks of the Zambezi River at the eastern end of Lower Zambezi National Park, Zambia, in the Winterthorn forest. There are few camps at this end of the park, so sightings often have few or no other vehicles.

faqs.q: How do you get to Anabezi?
faqs.a: Anabezi is about a 40-minute flight from Lusaka. Proflight scheduled flights land at Jeki Airstrip, a 40-minute drive from camp that can be extended into a 2-hour game drive, while charter flights land at Kulefu Airstrip, a 10-minute drive away.

faqs.q: When is Anabezi open?
faqs.a: Anabezi is a seasonal camp, open from April until mid-November. May to mid-August is cool and dry, and mid-August to mid-November is hot and dry.

faqs.q: How many suites does Anabezi have?
faqs.a: Twelve tented suites on elevated decks, each with a private plunge pool, including one family tent with two connected rooms that share a deck and plunge pool.

faqs.q: Does Anabezi accept children?
faqs.a: Anabezi does not accept children under 12 unless they are part of a group booking.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Anabezi?
faqs.a: Day and night game drives, walking safaris with a professional guide and an armed wildlife officer, canoeing, water safaris, catch-and-release tigerfish angling, birding and in-room spa treatments.

faqs.q: Where is Dunia Camp?
faqs.a: Dunia Camp is in the heart of Tanzania's Serengeti National Park, directly in the path of the Great Migration. It lies away from the main tourist routes, with game viewing around the Seronera River, the Moru Kopjes and the southern Serengeti plains.

faqs.q: How do I get to Dunia Camp?
faqs.a: Fly to Seronera airstrip, the primary airstrip in the Serengeti National Park. The camp is about a 45 minute drive away.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Dunia Camp?
faqs.a: Wildlife can be seen year round. Asilia says the Great Migration passes the camp heading north between March and June, and the herds return south through the central Serengeti near camp in November and December.

faqs.q: How many tents does Dunia Camp have?
faqs.a: Dunia has 8 tents, including 1 family suite. Each tent has an en suite bathroom with a fully plumbed hot shower, Wi-Fi and a private veranda.

faqs.q: Does Dunia Camp welcome children?
faqs.a: Yes. Children as young as five are welcome, and the camp has a family tent with separate bedrooms.

faqs.q: What makes Dunia Camp different?

faqs.q: What wildlife can I see at Dunia Camp?
faqs.a: Big cats, the rare black rhino, wildebeest, zebra, gazelle and elephant. Game drives run twice daily in custom-modified 4x4 vehicles, and the Moru Kopjes are known for big cats.
