why.body: In the olive hills outside Estremoz, where the plain rolls red and silver toward the Spanish border, a former farmstead has been made into something rare: a small hotel that behaves like a private gallery, with only eight rooms and suites.

The house asks for almost nothing of its guests. Days are spent between the pool, the library and the grounds; the loudest sound is the wind through the olives. It is the counterpoint this house looks for in Europe: a stay with no adrenaline in it at all.

onlyHere: From the rolling swells of the Pacific to the volcanic shores of remote islets, Evolve is your gateway to a Galápagos expedition unlike any other. Whether you’re traveling as a family, a couple on honeymoon, or seeking a solitary wildlife immersion, this yacht offers both community and sanctuary. As your floating base, each day opens with snorkeling in clear waters, hikes among ancient lava flows, or quiet observation of sea turtles and boobies in their natural domain. Post-adventure, relax in the Jacuzzi, browse the library, or enjoy an al fresco dinner under stars. The balance of intimacy, luxury, and deep ecological connection is simply unmatched.

why.body: Evolve offers an intimate, eco-conscious way to explore the Galápagos. Its small size grants access to secluded bays and remote sites while maintaining modern comfort. Perfect for couples, families, and nature lovers, it invites travelers to slow down and connect deeply with each destination.

why.body: On the Origin, travelers experience the Galápagos with intimacy and minimal environmental impact. With exceptional crew and guide ratios, every journey feels personal and enriching. Ideal for couples, small groups, and eco-minded adventurers seeking comfort in harmony with nature.

onlyHere: What sets the Theory apart is its blend of luxurious minimalism and deep ecological integrity. Here, solo travelers, couples, families, and multi generational groups all find harmony. Lightweight design, an intimate 20 guest scale, and the ability to anchor in remote coves that larger ships cannot reach create a deeply personal experience. With onboard technology that reduces fuel use by more than 30 percent compared to conventional yachts in the Galápagos, you explore the archipelago both intimately and responsibly.

why.body: On Theory, it blends boutique comfort with eco-minded adventure. With its low guest count, guests enjoy personalized service and minimal impact on the planet. Perfect for conscious explorers, couples, families, and solo travelers seeking connection and discovery.

stays.tagline: A contemporary sanctuary at the gateway to Machu Picchu.
stays.quote: Travel here to reconnect with wonder, silence, and the sacred energy of the Andes.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months offer the clearest mountain views, lower rainfall, and optimal conditions for exploring Machu Picchu and the surrounding cloud forest. Dry season mornings create especially dramatic sunrise conditions over the Andes.
stays.airport: Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport (CUZ) Inca Manco Cápac International Airport (JUL)
stays.airportDirections: The best arrival airport is Cusco International Airport (CUZ). From Cusco, travelers continue by rail to Machu Picchu Pueblo followed by a short walk to the hotel. Total travel time is approximately 4–5 hours depending on train schedules.

items: Walking access to transport and excursions

onlyHere: There’s a rare kind of energy that exists between the Andes and the Amazon Basin. El MaPi byInkaterra places travelers directly within that transition zone , where mist-covered mountains, rushing rivers, and ancient history create one of South America’s most emotionally powerful destinations.

stays.name: Elephant Pan Khwai

stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October for dry season, best game viewing, and water levels. November to April for green season, birdwatching, and quieter camp.

items: Water and land safari activities year-round
Pool and lounge area with fire pit

onlyHere: Elephant Pan Khwai is perfect for families, couples, solo explorers, and anyone wanting Delta wildlife right outside their tent, adventure on land and water, and a warm, welcoming camp vibe.

why.title: Where the Wild Comes to You
why.body: Ideal for adventure seekers, families, couples, and anyone who wants a front-row seat to Botswana’s wildlife, enjoy mokoro days, elephant moments, and the best of the Khwai Delta.

stays.name: Ellerman House Cape Town
stays.tagline: Where South African soul meets clifftop luxury and unforgettable experiences.
stays.quote: An ocean-view hideaway that feels like home with world-class art, wine, and cuisine at every turn.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Warm sunshine, longer days for outdoor dining and garden strolls, perfect sea views and access to nearby beaches make these prime months for a full Cape Town experience.
stays.airportDirections: ~26 km (~30 minutes) from Cape Town International Airport to Ellerman House via car with complimentary airport transfers offered.
stays.founderNote: A view that makes the rest of Cape Town look like the warm-up act, and white-glove service from a staff that notices before you ask. Make it your base. Stayed May 2026; a founder favourite. , JW

items: Tailored Concierge Access to Cape Town

onlyHere: Perched in Bantry Bay’s prestigious hills, Ellerman House uniquely blends a living art gallery, exceptional wine experiences, and elegant cuisine wrapped in warm South African hospitality and ocean panoramas.

why.body: Ellerman House is a refined boutique retreat for travelers seeking peaceful exclusivity and authentic immersion in Cape Town’s culture. From its significant South African art collection to world-class food and wine experiences. Best for: Honeymooners, Art & Wine Enthusiasts, Couples, Discerning City Explorers, and Luxury Retreat Seekers.

facts.best_months: October to March, for warm sunshine, long days and outdoor dining.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 26 km, around 30 minutes, from Cape Town International Airport (CPT), with complimentary airport transfers.
facts.who_its_for: Honeymooners, couples and art and wine lovers who want a quiet, private base in Cape Town.
facts.signature_experiences: Art tours, wine cellar exploration and BAR ROC sundowners.

faqs.q: Where is Ellerman House?
faqs.a: Ellerman House is at 180 Kloof Road in Bantry Bay, Cape Town, with ocean views.

faqs.q: How do you get to Ellerman House?
faqs.a: It is about 26 km, around 30 minutes, from Cape Town International Airport (CPT). Airport transfers are complimentary.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Ellerman House?
faqs.a: October to March, for warm sunshine, long days, outdoor dining and easy beach access.

faqs.q: What makes Ellerman House different?
faqs.a: A significant South African art collection, a wine archive of more than 9,000 labels, and BAR ROC for champagne and sundowners.

faqs.q: Is Ellerman House good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Honeymooners top its best-for list, alongside art and wine lovers and couples.

items: Game drives (including off-road and night drives)

why.title: Where Big Cats Roam
why.body: Encounter Mara is perfect for those seeking close wildlife encounters, off-road adventure, and the freedom of Mara Naboisho. Best for couples, solo explorers, families, photographers, and big cat fans.

stays.tagline: On the Crater rim, looking into Ngorongoro and out to the Serengeti

paras: Cottages on the wild side of the Crater rim, including two-bedroom family cottages, each with an en-suite bathroom and a private veranda over the Crater.

items: Crater game drives that aim to enter soon after dawn
Highland walks with a Maasai scout and ranger
Visits to a Maasai boma in the next valley
A walk out to the Serengeti Safari Camp

paras: Nomad Tanzania's camp on the Ngorongoro Crater rim. Central lounge with an evening fire. Furnishings sourced locally and inspired by Tanzanian artists. Open all year.

onlyHere: Nomad calls Entamanu the only place where you can see the Ngorongoro Crater and the Serengeti plains from the same spot. Being on the rim means you are often first into the Crater in the morning.

why.title: First Into the Crater
why.body: Best for families, groups of friends and travelers combining Ngorongoro with the Serengeti.

facts.best_months: Entamanu is open all year, with Crater access soon after dawn.
facts.how_to_get_there: Nomad's site does not publish transfer details for Entamanu, so your advisor will confirm the route up to the Crater rim.
facts.signature_experiences: Dawn Crater game drives ahead of the minibuses, highland walks with a Maasai scout, a Maasai boma visit and a walk to Serengeti Safari Camp.
facts.who_its_for: Families and groups of friends in two-bedroom cottages, and travellers who want an early start into the Crater.

faqs.q: Where is Entamanu Ngorongoro?
faqs.a: High on the rim of the Ngorongoro Crater. Nomad describes it as the only place in the world where you can see the Ngorongoro Crater and the Serengeti plains from the same spot.

faqs.q: Is Entamanu open all year?
faqs.a: Yes, Nomad lists Entamanu as open all year.

faqs.q: What are the rooms like at Entamanu?
faqs.a: Cottage-style rooms with en-suite bathrooms, double sinks, a power shower and private verandahs looking into the Crater. Two-bedroom cottages with full-sized bedrooms are available for families or groups of friends.

faqs.q: Why stay on the Crater rim?
faqs.a: Entamanu has access to the Crater soon after dawn, often first in line, which avoids the minibuses that arrive later.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Entamanu?
faqs.a: Early Crater game drives, highland walks with a Maasai scout and an armed ranger, and visits to a Maasai boma in the next valley. Nomad can set up a picnic overlooking the Crater for your return from the morning drive, and guests can walk from Entamanu to Serengeti Safari Camp.

faqs.q: Who is Entamanu best suited to?
faqs.a: Families and groups of friends, who can share Nomad's two-bedroom cottages, and travellers who want to be among the first into the Crater each morning.

stays.name: Entamanu Private
stays.tagline: Four cottages, Ngorongoro's private hideaway

paras: Four cottages raised on wooden platforms on the north-western Crater rim: two family cottages and two standard cottages, each with a private veranda over the Crater.
Early-morning Crater drives soon after dawn, ahead of the minibuses. Highland walks with a Maasai scout. A private visit to a nearby Maasai community.
A separate camp beside Nomad's Entamanu, with its own lounge, dining room and lookout veranda. Raised on platforms to leave no footprint on the site. Open all year. Children over five welcome.

onlyHere: Entamanu Private is the Crater for a family or a small group of friends: four cottages, your own living spaces and the same dawn start into Ngorongoro.

why.title: A Crater Rim to Yourselves
why.body: Best for families and small groups who want privacy at Ngorongoro.

facts.best_months: Entamanu Private is open all year round, with Crater access soon after dawn.
facts.how_to_get_there: Nomad's site does not publish transfer details for Entamanu Private, so your advisor will confirm the route up to the north-western Crater rim.
facts.signature_experiences: Early Crater drives ahead of the minibuses, highland walks with a Maasai scout and a private Maasai boma visit.
facts.who_its_for: Families with children over five and small groups who want four Crater-rim cottages and their own living spaces.

faqs.q: Where is Entamanu Private?
faqs.a: On the remote north-western rim of the Ngorongoro Crater, in the highlands. It is Nomad's exclusive camp on the Crater rim.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Entamanu Private have?
faqs.a: Just four rooms elevated on wooden platforms, two of which are family rooms. Each cottage has a private veranda overlooking the Ngorongoro Crater.

faqs.q: Does Entamanu Private accept children?
faqs.a: Yes, Nomad welcomes children over five at Entamanu Private.

faqs.q: Is Entamanu Private open all year?
faqs.a: Yes, Nomad lists it as open all year round.

faqs.q: What shared spaces does Entamanu Private have?
faqs.a: Its own dining room, a private lounge and a spacious lookout verandah across the Ngorongoro Crater.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Entamanu Private?
faqs.a: Crater drives with access soon after dawn, avoiding the minibuses, and highland walks with your guide and a Maasai scout. Guests can also visit a nearby Maasai boma for insights into pastoral life, from building huts to warrior ceremonies.

faqs.q: Who is Entamanu Private best suited to?
faqs.a: Nomad says the camp is perfect for families, offering your own exclusive Crater experience with private living spaces.

Esirai
Mobile
Migration
Camp
stays.tagline: A nomadic safari crafted to move with Africa’s greatest show.
stays.quote: Esirai reminds you what it feels like to be deeply connected to land, wildlife, and the quiet rhythm of the migrating herds. It’s raw Africa, delivered with soul.
stays.airport: Kogatende Airstrip (north camp) or Seronera Airstrip (south camp)
onlyHere: Only here can you sleep under canvas with the migrating herds passing nearby, hearing the night sounds of the Serengeti move like a living tide. Esirai is crafted for travelers who want closeness to nature without the noise.

why.body: Esirai Camp offers front-row access to one of the world’s last great natural spectacles - the Great Wildebeest Migration.

facts.best_months: Esirai moves between the northern and southern Serengeti with the migration; Entara does not publish fixed months for each location on its site.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Kogatende Airstrip for the north camp or Seronera Airstrip for the south camp, with transfers included in the Adventure and Game Drive packages.
facts.signature_experiences: Migration game drives, guided walks in the north, bush dining, sundowners and hot air balloon flights.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers who want a simple, low-impact mobile camp close to the migration, including families sharing a children's triple.

faqs.q: Where is Esirai Camp?
faqs.a: Esirai is a mobile camp in Tanzania's Serengeti that is set up in the northern or southern Serengeti depending on the season. It moves with the wildebeest and zebra on their journey from the southern plains to the Mara River in the north.

faqs.q: How do I get to Esirai Camp?
faqs.a: Guests fly to Kogatende Airstrip when the camp is in the north and Seronera Airstrip when it is in the south. Return airstrip transfers are included in Entara's Adventure and Game Drive packages.

faqs.q: How many tents does Esirai Camp have?
faqs.a: Esirai has eight mobile tents with en-suite bathrooms, hot safari showers and safari toilets. The heart of camp is a large mess tent with an adjoining library tent and an outdoor fire pit.

faqs.q: Can families stay at Esirai Camp?
faqs.a: Yes. Entara lists a children's triple as available at Esirai, so a family can share.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Esirai Camp?
faqs.a: Game drives, guided walks at the north camp, bush dining, sundowners and hot air balloon flights. The Adventure Package adds a private guide and vehicle with a personal activity plan.

faqs.q: Is Esirai Camp eco-friendly?
faqs.a: Yes. Esirai is a light-footprint camp that is fully solar-powered, uses heated water for showers rather than running water, and has dry pit latrines flushed with sand. The whole camp packs into a single pickup truck when it moves.

faqs.q: Does Esirai Camp have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: No. Esirai has no Wi-Fi, but the camp manager is in contact with Entara's main office and can pass on a message in an emergency.

stays.name: Etosha Mountain Lodge
stays.tagline: Nine chalets in a private reserve on Etosha's southwest border
stays.quote: Perched above the plains, Etosha Mountain Lodge offers breathtaking sunsets, big game safaris, and a peaceful retreat high in Namibia’s wild north
stays.bestMonths: Year-round; May to September for dry-season game viewing
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to September, animals gather at the waterholes; October to April is lush, and wildlife is a little harder to spot.
stays.airportDirections: About a 6 hour drive or a 1 hour flight from Windhoek.

paras: Nine air-conditioned chalets: eight twin or double rooms and one family chalet with a private plunge pool on the veranda. All are en suite with indoor showers and bathtubs, and look out over 180-degree views. Central thatched lapa with restaurant, bar, wine cellar, curio shop and swimming pool.

items: Guided walks with armed guides (ages 12 and up)

paras: Set in the Etosha Heights Private Reserve, which shares a 65-kilometre boundary with Etosha National Park. Waterhole in front of camp. Double-storey photography hide with a livecam. Spa treatments in your room at extra cost. Solar powered. Children of all ages welcome.

onlyHere: Etosha Mountain Lodge is for families, couples, photographers and anyone who wants Etosha's wildlife without the crowds, from a classic Namibian game lodge in a private reserve known for its black and white rhino.

why.title: Namibia's High Safari
why.body: Ideal for wildlife lovers, photographers, couples and families. Look for black and white rhino, lion, cheetah and leopard, then watch the waterhole from the two-level hide.

facts.best_months: Open year round, with May to September the dry season when game gathers at waterholes.
facts.how_to_get_there: About a 6 hour drive or a 1 hour flight from Windhoek.
facts.signature_experiences: Rhino sightings, night drives and a double-storey photography hide on a floodlit waterhole.
facts.who_its_for: Families with children of any age, wildlife photographers and travellers wanting Etosha's game in a private reserve.

faqs.q: Where is Etosha Mountain Lodge?
faqs.a: It is in the Etosha Heights Private Reserve in northern Namibia, on the southwest border of Etosha National Park. The 60,000-hectare reserve shares a 65-kilometre boundary with the park.

faqs.q: How do I get to Etosha Mountain Lodge?
faqs.a: Natural Selection gives two options: about a 6 hour drive or a 1 hour flight from Windhoek.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: The lodge is open year round. In the dry months from May to September animals gather at the remaining waterholes for strong game viewing, while the rainy season from October to April brings lush scenery that makes wildlife a little harder to spot.

faqs.q: How many chalets are there?
faqs.a: Nine air-conditioned chalets: eight twin or double and one family chalet, which has a private plunge pool on its veranda.

faqs.q: Are children welcome?
faqs.a: Yes, children of all ages are welcome. Private vehicles are required on game drives for families with children under 10, and guided walks are for ages 12 and up.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Morning and afternoon game drives, night drives, black and white rhino sightings, a double-storey photography hide over a floodlit waterhole, and guided walks with armed guides.

faqs.q: Who is Etosha Mountain Lodge best for?
faqs.a: Families, photographers and travellers who want Etosha's wildlife in a private reserve, which Natural Selection describes as Etosha without the crowds.

stays.name: Expedition Blue Lagoon
stays.tagline: A seasonal boat, kayak and snorkel expedition to Cap Masoala, run exclusively for two to four guests
stays.bestMonthsNote: A seasonal expedition: it operates from September through to early January because of local weather, and does not run the rest of the year. Departures are on Sundays for the 10-night expedition and Wednesdays for the 11-night expedition. Humpback whales are sometimes seen in season.
stays.airportDirections: A private charter flight of about 90 minutes from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra, then by boat via Nosy Mangabe to Masoala Forest Lodge. Cap Masoala is reached only by boat from Masoala Forest Lodge.

paras: The expedition begins and ends at Masoala Forest Lodge, whose seven tented rooms are raised on stilted decks in the forest canopy above the beach. At Cap Masoala the base camp is Crusoe's Cabin, a timber cabin with running water and a flush toilet, built from 2018. On some expeditions nights are spent camping out on Nosy Behento, Nosy Nepato and other islets in light nylon dome tents with safari showers and short-drop toilets. Simple food, fresh air and midday siestas in shady hammocks set the pace.

Exploring the Blue Lagoon, its beaches, fringing reefs and offshore islets by kayak and outrigger pirogue, snorkelling the coves and a secret spot off Nosy Behento, and walking to old colonial lighthouses for sundowners. At Masoala Forest Lodge the itinerary adds primary rainforest walks for red ruffed lemurs and helmet vangas, night walks for lemurs, kayaking to the sacred island of Nosy Ndraindra, a village walk among rice, cinnamon, clove and vanilla, the Tampolo Cascades, snorkelling at Antalavia and a visit to Nosy Mangabe for leaf-tailed geckos and Brookesia chameleons. Humpback whales are sometimes seen in season.

Cap Masoala is the very tip of the Masoala Peninsula in northeastern Madagascar, beside Masoala National Park. Between some 15km of protective reef and 10km of white beaches lies a lagoon of about 1,500ha. A small rural population lives here largely from the sea, with a coastal trading boat calling every fortnight, and over 20 years has accepted Wild Expeditions and its guests as part of the community. Wild Expeditions bans single-use plastic in its Madagascar operation and uses solar power where possible.

onlyHere: Kilometres of white beaches and a reef-sheltered lagoon where, as Wild Expeditions puts it, the closest fellow tourist is at least 40km away.

why.title: A Lagoon With No One Else There
why.body: Best for adventurous couples and small private groups of up to four who want reef, rainforest and lemurs far from other travellers, and are happy with a cabin and dome tents.

facts.best_months: September to early January only.
facts.how_to_get_there: Charter from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra, then boat only.
facts.signature_experiences: Kayak and pirogue on the Blue Lagoon, reef snorkelling and lemur night walks.
facts.who_its_for: Adventurous couples and private groups of two to four.

faqs.q: Where is Expedition Blue Lagoon?
faqs.a: At Cap Masoala, the tip of the Masoala Peninsula in northeastern Madagascar, reached from Wild Expeditions' Masoala Forest Lodge.

faqs.q: How do you get to Expedition Blue Lagoon?
faqs.a: Fly about 90 minutes by charter from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra, take the boat to Masoala Forest Lodge, then continue by expedition boat to Cap Masoala. Access is only by boat.

faqs.q: Where do you sleep on Expedition Blue Lagoon?
faqs.a: At Masoala Forest Lodge (seven tented rooms on stilted decks) at the start and end, and at Crusoe's Cabin, a timber cabin at Cap Masoala; some expeditions camp on islets in light nylon dome tents. It runs exclusively for 2 to 4 guests.

faqs.q: Can children join Expedition Blue Lagoon?
faqs.a: Child rates apply under 16, but Wild Expeditions says it is not suitable for infants or very young children; ask for age-appropriate advice.

faqs.q: When does Expedition Blue Lagoon run?
faqs.a: September to early January, because of local weather. Departures are Sundays (10 nights) and Wednesdays (11 nights).

faqs.q: What do you do on Expedition Blue Lagoon?
faqs.a: Kayaking, outrigger pirogue trips, snorkelling, beach walks and lighthouse sundowners on the lagoon, with rainforest and night walks for lemurs at Masoala.

stays.name: Explora Uyuni
stays.tagline: Explora's lodge on the Uyuni salt flat, built with local families, at the end of a private crossing from San Pedro de Atacama.

why.title: Place
why.body: The Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat on Earth, high on Bolivia's Altiplano. Explora's lodge is the last base on its private crossing from San Pedro de Atacama, after nights at mountain lodges on the way up.

why.title: People
why.body: Explora, the Chilean house behind Explora Atacama, built the Uyuni lodge in partnership with local families. Each crossing is private: two travellers, an Explora guide and a local driver in a 4x4.

why.title: Impact
why.body: Built in partnership with local families (as Explora reports). Nothing more is claimed until Explora documents it.

why.title: James' note
why.body: I've worked with Explora since 2004. The Atacama-to-Uyuni crossing is the trip I'd put people on when they want the desert and the salt as one journey, and the altitude taken properly, a day at a time.

facts.best_months: May to November for clear, dry days and the best night skies; nights on the Altiplano are very cold.
facts.how_to_get_there: Usually reached on Explora's Travesia Atacama-Uyuni: arrive at Calama (CJC) in Chile, cross the Altiplano by private 4x4 with an Explora guide and a local driver, and fly home from Uyuni (UYU). Itineraries start at seven nights.
facts.signature_experiences: The Uyuni salt flat; the Altiplano lagoons and volcanoes on the way, with vicuñas, flamingos and llamas; nights at Explora's mountain lodges; astronomy under the high-desert sky.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and small private parties who want the Atacama and Uyuni as one journey, with the altitude taken gently.

onlyHere: Feline Fields is not your typical wildlife lodge. It invites you to slow down, read the wind in the grasses, ride into the quiet, and learn from a culture that is ancient yet always present. Come solo and disappear into the desert, arrive with your partner to share moments of quiet wonder, or bring family to explore paths few ever walk. Here you find space, soul, and a connection to a land that whispers.

why.body: Feline Fields Lodge is for the traveler who seeks more than spectacle, where the journey is as internal as it is external. It is ideal for couples and solo travelers who relish solitude, as well as families looking for a meaningful wilderness escape.

onlyHere: At Feline Fields Vintage Camp, you escape into a time when safari was slow, attentive, and deeply felt. Your every moment is threaded with nature: wake to riverside murmurs, end the day in a wooden tub watching stars, and adventure on foot, by canoe, or from a chariot of tracks. The scale is small, the impact is gentle, and every detail is woven to let wilderness lead. Couples will find romance in the solitude; small families can connect in quiet intimacy; solo travelers can travel inward with space and silence; groups can take over the entire camp for a private safari rhythm unlike any other.

why.body: Feline Fields Vintage Camp is perfect for those who long for a safari that whispers rather than shouts. For couples seeking romance under canvas walls, for families wanting meaningful downtime, for solo travelers craving quiet communion, and for groups wanting place and pace of their own. Here you’re not in the wilderness, you are part of it, guided by expert rangers, moved by light, filled with wildlife, and held by an ethos of elegance and gentle footprint.

faqs.q: Where is Gibb's Farm?
faqs.a: In Karatu, between Lake Manyara and the Ngorongoro Crater. The Crater is 56 km, about a two-hour drive, from the front gate, Lake Manyara is a 45-minute drive and Lake Eyasi is 1.5 hours away.

faqs.q: How do you get to Gibb's Farm?
faqs.a: International flights arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, about 45 minutes from Arusha. From Arusha you can drive to the farm, or fly to Lake Manyara Airport for a faster arrival, where Gibb's Farm staff meet guests in private vehicles.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Gibb's Farm have?
faqs.a: Seventeen one-bedroom farm cottages and two two-bedroom farm houses, Bustani and Deutsches. The cottages are known for their outdoor showers, and each farm house bedroom is en-suite.

faqs.q: Is Gibb's Farm good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The two farm houses are designed for bigger families and those travelling together, a limited number of interconnecting rooms are available, and children up to five stay free when sharing.

faqs.q: What is the history of Gibb's Farm?
faqs.a: It was founded in the 1920s as a coffee plantation and still grows about 30 acres of organically cultivated Arabica coffee. Coffee roasted on the farm is served to guests.

faqs.q: What can you do at Gibb's Farm?
faqs.a: The two-hour Elephant Cave and Falls walk through the forested slopes of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, vegetable harvests, coffee processing, cow milking and egg collecting. You can also cycle the farm, walk to neighbouring Tloma village and book half or full day safaris to the Ngorongoro Crater, Lake Eyasi or Lake Manyara.

faqs.q: Is Gibb's Farm good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Gibb's Farm offers honeymoon packages of three nights or more that include a complimentary spa treatment, a romantic dinner and a welcome fruit platter with wine and chocolates.

stays.name: Governors' Camp
stays.tagline: Africa's first permanent luxury tented camp, on its original Mara River site since 1972
stays.bestMonthsNote: Open all year. July to October is the Great Wildebeest Migration and peak safari season. January to March brings strong predator sightings and calving season. April to June is lush and green with fewer crowds, with April and May the green season. November and December bring migratory birds and dramatic skies.
stays.airportDirections: Daily scheduled flights from Nairobi Wilson Airport to Musiara Airstrip with Governors' Aviation, the collection's own airline, and other select airlines; Governors' Aviation flights take approximately 45 minutes. The camp is a short transfer from the airstrip, and local airstrip transfers are included. Strict 15 kg luggage limit per person in soft bags.
stays.founderNote: Stayed with Governors' in 2012. A founder favourite. JW

paras: 24 tents, entirely under canvas: 19 luxury tents overlooking the Mara River and 5 family tents with views across the open plains. Every tent has an en suite bathroom and a private verandah. There is a bar tent with a deck over the Mara River, a dining tent looking out over the plains, a spa tent offering massages with natural products by The Wild Herb Company, a gift shop, and Wifi in camp.

Up to three game drives a day in open-sided 4x4 vehicles, with routes set by the wildlife because the camp is already inside the reserve. Hot-air balloon safaris over the Mara, Masai cultural visits, bush dinners (at extra cost), sundowners and spa treatments. From July to October the Great Migration moves through the Musiara area, with Mara River crossing points near camp.

Set inside the Masai Mara National Reserve beside Musiara Marsh, in a non-fenced, wildlife-dense area where elephants and hippos often move through camp. Governors' Camp runs on 100% solar power and holds a Gold eco-rating from Eco-Tourism Kenya. The nightly rate includes local airstrip transfers, meals, soft drinks, beers, house wines and non-premium spirits, up to three game drives a day and laundry.

onlyHere: Musiara Marsh, right beside camp, is home ground of the Marsh Pride of lions, followed for decades by BBC Earth's Dynasties, Animal Planet's Big Cat Diaries and Big Cat Tales and Nat Geo's LION. The brand describes Governors' Camp as a top choice for the filmmakers behind these productions.

why.title: Where the Mara Safari Began
why.body: Best for first-time safari travellers, families with children of any age, and anyone who wants the Marsh Pride and the migration on the doorstep.

facts.best_months: Open all year; July to October for the Great Migration, January to March for predators and calving.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 45 minutes by Governors' Aviation from Nairobi Wilson to Musiara Airstrip, then a short transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives with the Marsh Pride, migration river crossings and hot-air balloon safaris.
facts.who_its_for: First-time safari travellers, families with children of any age, couples and photographers.

faqs.q: Where is Governors' Camp?
faqs.a: Inside Kenya's Masai Mara National Reserve, on the banks of the Mara River beside Musiara Marsh. It has stood on its original site since 1972.

faqs.q: How do you get to Governors' Camp?
faqs.a: Fly from Nairobi Wilson Airport to Musiara Airstrip with Governors' Aviation (about 45 minutes) or other select airlines. The camp is a short transfer from the airstrip, and airstrip transfers are included.

faqs.q: How many tents does Governors' Camp have?
faqs.a: 24 tents, all under canvas: 19 luxury tents overlooking the Mara River and 5 family tents with views across the plains, each with an en suite bathroom and a private verandah.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Governors' Camp?
faqs.a: Yes. Children of all ages are welcome, including very young children. High chairs, babysitting, special children's meals and early mealtimes are available.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Governors' Camp?
faqs.a: The camp is open all year. July to October brings the Great Migration and Mara River crossings near camp; January to March is known for predator sightings and calving; April and May are green season.

faqs.q: What can you do at Governors' Camp?
faqs.a: Up to three game drives a day, hot-air balloon safaris, Masai cultural visits, bush dinners and spa treatments. The Marsh Pride of lions divides its time between Musiara Marsh, beside camp, and the nearby Bila Shaka area.

faqs.q: Who is Governors' Camp best for?
faqs.a: First-time safari travellers, families, couples and wildlife photographers who want a traditional tented camp focused on wildlife rather than architecture.

stays.name: Governors' Il Moran Camp
stays.tagline: Ten tents under riverine forest on the banks of the Mara River
stays.bestMonthsNote: Open all year. July to October is the Great Wildebeest Migration and peak safari season. January to March brings strong predator sightings and calving season. April to June is lush and green with fewer crowds, with April and May the green season. November and December bring migratory birds and dramatic skies.
stays.airportDirections: Daily scheduled flights from Nairobi Wilson Airport to Musiara Airstrip, the nearest airstrip to camp, with Governors' Aviation and other select airlines; Governors' Aviation flights take approximately 45 minutes. Local airstrip transfers are included. Strict 15 kg luggage limit per person in soft bags.

paras: 10 luxury tents set along the winding banks of the Mara River under a canopy of riverine forest, each with a private veranda and an en suite bathroom with a standalone bathtub, shower, twin basins and running hot and cold water. The main mess tent has dark wooden tables, oversized blue couches, a beaded chandelier, tribal portraits and African artefacts. Meals are served on the raised wooden deck above the river and its resident hippos, and a sunken fire pit is lit each evening. Free Wifi, USB charging and Vortex Diamondback binoculars to borrow at no charge.

Up to three game drives a day in custom-built 4x4 vehicles within the Masai Mara National Reserve and occasionally in the Mara Triangle, with private game drives on request (advance booking required). Hot-air balloon safaris, Masai cultural visits, bush dinners (at extra cost) and, from July to October, the Great Wildebeest Migration and its Mara River crossings.

Fully inside the Masai Mara National Reserve rather than an outside conservancy, so vehicles leave camp straight into wildlife areas without passing through reserve gates. Il Moran holds a Gold eco-rating from Eco-Tourism Kenya, and massages with natural products by The Wild Herb Company can be given in your tent. The nightly rate includes local airstrip transfers, soft drinks, beers, house wines and non-premium spirits, up to three game drives a day and laundry.

onlyHere: Just ten tents inside the reserve, close enough to the Mara River to watch hippos from the dining deck, in the same Musiara country the Governors' guides have known since 1972.

why.title: Ten Tents on the Mara River
why.body: Best for honeymooners, couples, solo travellers and families with children aged 8 and over who want a quiet, private camp inside the reserve.

facts.best_months: Open all year; July to October for the Great Migration, January to March for predators and calving.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 45 minutes by Governors' Aviation from Nairobi Wilson to Musiara Airstrip.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives straight from camp, private game drives on request and hot-air balloon safaris.

faqs.q: How do you get to Il Moran Camp?

faqs.q: How many tents does Il Moran Camp have?

faqs.q: Can children stay at Il Moran Camp?

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Il Moran Camp?

faqs.q: What can you do at Il Moran Camp?

stays.bestMonthsNote: Open all year. December to March is the green season, when rain can turn the rocky landscape green and the dry riverbeds briefly flow, with high temperatures. paras: Ten spacious tents: eight twins and two family units, each on a low wooden deck with a private plunge pool, air-conditioning and an en suite bathroom with double vanities and indoor and outdoor showers. Rammed earth walls and insulated canvas roofs give natural climate control. The main area has a lounge and dining room, an outdoor deck with a swimming pool, a small wellness spa and a fire pit. Wi-Fi is available, hairdryers are provided and laundry is complimentary.

Morning and evening game drives for desert-adapted elephant, giraffe and, with luck, desert lion, plus zebra, klipspringer, kudu, springbok, oryx and steenbok. A waterhole near camp draws desert lion, giraffe, oryx and brown hyena. Rangers lead black rhino tracking, and there are nature walks, scenic sundowners, stargazing with dinner under the stars, and cultural visits with the local Himba. Spa and wellness treatments are available in camp.

Opened in May 2026 on the northern bank of the Hoanib River, 70 km southwest of Sesfontein and 25 km downriver from Hoanib Valley Camp, in the Sesfontein Community Conservancy. The camp is powered entirely by solar energy and has a full water treatment system. Staying supports conservation projects for the desert-adapted elephants, including work on human-wildlife conflict, and the livelihoods of communities living near the conservancy.

onlyHere: A camp shaped around the desert-adapted elephants of the Hoanib Valley, with a private plunge pool on every deck and the Skeleton Coast just beyond the mountains and dunes.

stays.bestMonthsNote: Open all year. December to March is the green season, when rain can turn the rocky landscape green and the dry riverbeds briefly flow, with high temperatures. May to July brings chilly mornings and evenings. By October the land is at its driest and warmest, and desert elephant gather near the last water in the river valleys.
stays.airportDirections: Fly by light aircraft to Orutjandja Airstrip, then take a road transfer to camp. Road access is also possible; Natural Selection reservations quote flights and drives.

paras: Six guest tents: five twins and one family tent, each with an en suite bathroom with an indoor shower and a private veranda. Furniture is made by local Rundu carpenters and Himba carvers, with baskets woven by the Omba Project in Windhoek. The main area has a swimming pool, outdoor dining, a fire pit and a library. Wi-Fi is available and laundry is complimentary.

Morning and evening game drives in search of desert-adapted elephant, giraffe and, with luck, desert lion, along with zebra, klipspringer, kudu, springbok, oryx and steenbok. Rhino rangers lead black rhino tracking, guides share the work of the giraffe conservation programme, and nature walks explore the valley on foot. Cultural visits to the local Himba and Herero communities are offered. Birders look for Monteiro's hornbill, Rüppell's korhaan and Verreaux's eagle.

Set in a hidden valley ringed by jagged mountains in the Sesfontein Community Conservancy, just outside the private 500 square kilometre Palmwag Concession, with views over the ephemeral Hoanib River. The camp is entirely solar powered, and the tents sit on decks made of a wood, bamboo and 70% recycled-material composite. It is a partnership with the Sesfontein Community and the Giraffe Conservation Foundation (GCF): 80% of staff come from Sesfontein, and 8% of turnover is paid as rental to the community, which funds rhino rangers and game guards.

onlyHere: A camp built with the Giraffe Conservation Foundation, where days are spent among desert-adapted giraffe and elephant in the Hoanib River valley, and where every stay supports a black rhino introduction programme.

faqs.a: Ila is a tented lodge on the Kafue River in Kafue National Park, western Zambia, which Green Safaris describes as the largest and oldest park in Zambia.

faqs.q: When is Ila Safari Lodge open?

faqs.q: How many tents does Ila have?

faqs.q: Can children stay at Ila?
faqs.a: Yes. There is no age limit, there are en-suite family rooms, and guides adapt their activities for younger guests.

faqs.q: What makes Ila different?

faqs.q: Who is Ila best for?

faqs.q: Where is Isla Palenque?
faqs.a: Isla Palenque is a 400-acre private island in the Gulf of Chiriquí, off Panama's western Pacific coast near the Costa Rica border, at the edge of the Gulf of Chiriquí National Marine Park. It is a member of the Cayuga Collection.

faqs.q: How do you get to Isla Palenque?
faqs.a: Fly from Panama City (PTY) to David (DAV), about 60 minutes. The team meets you for a 60 minute drive to the port at Boca Chica, then a 15 minute boat ride to the island; from Costa Rica you can fly San José to Golfito and cross at Paso Canoas with the resort's help.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Isla Palenque have?
faqs.a: There are only 8 Beachfront Casitas of 65 m², each steps from Playa Palenque, plus the Beachfront Villa Estate: 6 free-standing rooms and suites above Playa Primera, rented as a whole for 2 to 14 guests. The whole island can be booked for up to 30 guests.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Isla Palenque?
faqs.a: Dry season, mid-December to mid-April, brings near-constant sunshine. Wildlife Season runs May to November, with humpback whales in the Gulf from July and October named as the very best whale-watching month.

faqs.q: Is Isla Palenque good for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Children of all ages are welcome, with gentle swimming beaches, kid-friendly hikes led by Island Hosts, cooking and pastry classes and a 5 km fitness challenge for teens. Casitas sleep 2 adults and 2 children, and the Villa Estate suits multi-generational groups.

faqs.q: What is included and what can you do?
faqs.a: Stays include round-trip boat transfers from Boca Chica, all meals and non-alcoholic drinks, kayaks, paddleboards and more than 10 nature trails and tours. Guests explore seven beaches, snorkel and island hop, forage and take guided wildlife walks.

faqs.q: Where is Islas Secas?
faqs.a: Islas Secas is a private archipelago of 14 volcanic islands in the Gulf of Chiriquí, about 20 miles off Panama's Pacific coast, with 13 of the 14 islands left untouched. Coiba National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is about an hour away by boat.

faqs.q: How do you get to Islas Secas?
faqs.a: From Panama City, the resort's scheduled 16-seat Twin Otter flies just over an hour to the private airstrip on the main island; it is the only aircraft allowed to land there. Guests flying privately use Enrique Malek Airport in David, then a 20 minute flight; the archipelago is reachable only by private plane or boat.

faqs.q: How many casitas are there at Islas Secas?
faqs.a: Seven casitas and one residence, sleeping 28 to 32 guests in total: Tented Casitas and Casita Mirador (1 bedroom), Casita Sombras and Tres Palmas (2 bedrooms), Casita Grande (four casitas, up to 8 guests) and the four-bedroom Casa Cavada residence with a semi-Olympic infinity pool.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Islas Secas?
faqs.a: Islas Secas describes three seasons: January to March for calm seas and the best diving and snorkeling visibility, April to September for whale watching (humpbacks from July to September) and marine safaris, and October to December for glassy seas, sunsets and wellness stays.

faqs.q: Is Islas Secas suitable for children?
faqs.a: Yes, children of all ages are welcome, with watersports suited to children and teens. The resort notes that young children need close supervision, as casita railings have gaps with drops beyond and some paths are too rough for strollers.

faqs.q: What is included at Islas Secas?
faqs.a: Stays are all inclusive, from diving and marine safaris with expert guides to all meals and drinks. Activities include scuba diving at more than 20 sites, whale watching, surfing, kayaking, SUP, e-foiling, catch-and-release fishing, birding and nature trails.

faqs.q: Where is Kichakani Camp?
faqs.a: Kichakani Camp is a mobile camp in Tanzania's Serengeti National Park that moves between two locations to follow the Great Migration. It pitches in the northern Lamai triangle from June to November and in the southern Serengeti from December to March.

faqs.q: How do I get to Kichakani Camp?
faqs.a: By light aircraft to Lamai Airstrip (about 2 hours from Arusha Airport) or Serengeti South Airstrip (about 1 hour 30 minutes), followed by a drive of about 1 hour 15 minutes to camp. The light aircraft luggage limit is 20kg (44lbs) per person in a soft-sided bag, including hand luggage.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kichakani Camp?
faqs.a: June to November in the northern location for the Mara River crossings, which reach a peak from August to October. December to March in the southern location for the wildebeest calving season.

faqs.q: How many tents does Kichakani Camp have?
faqs.a: Kichakani Camp has 10 classic tents for a maximum of 20 guests. Each tent is 42 sq m (452 sq ft) with a king-size bed, a private deck and an en-suite bathroom with a traditional bucket shower.

faqs.q: Is Kichakani Camp suitable for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Children aged 6 and older are welcome, and children aged 15 and younger must share with an adult. A tent sleeps up to 2 adults and 1 child aged 6 to 15.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Kichakani Camp?
faqs.a: Twice-daily game drives focused on the Mara River crossings in the north and the calving season in the south, with full-day drives possible to track the herds. Sundowners, bush breakfasts and a weekly traditional boma night round out the stay.

faqs.q: Is Kichakani Camp good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. Abercrombie & Kent says romance is woven into every A&K Sanctuary, with touches such as a honeymoon cocktail at sundowners and sparkling wine in your tent on the night before departure.

faqs.q: Where is Kokoko Camp?
faqs.a: Kokoko Camp is in a prime wilderness area of Ruaha National Park, Tanzania. It sits on the edge of a forest overlooking the dry Mwagusi Riverbed.

faqs.q: How do I get to Kokoko Camp?
faqs.a: Fly to Msembe airstrip, which is a 45 minute drive from camp.

faqs.q: When is Kokoko Camp open, and when is the best time to go?
faqs.a: Kokoko is open June to November and closed December to May, operating only in Ruaha's dry season. Asilia says October and most of November are the peak of the dry season and offer the best conditions for walking safaris and game drives.

faqs.q: How many tents does Kokoko Camp have?
faqs.a: Just three double or twin tents, and the camp is booked privately for a maximum of six guests. Each tent has an en suite bathroom, a hand basin, an outdoor bucket shower and a retractable roof for stargazing from bed.

faqs.q: Does Kokoko Camp allow children?
faqs.a: Children aged 12 and older are welcome. The minimum age reflects the exposed nature of the camp and its emphasis on walking, in line with park rules for walking safaris.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Kokoko Camp?
faqs.a: Walking safaris, game drives and night drives along the Mwagusi River, hosted by one of Asilia's top guides with a private vehicle. Meals are cooked over an open fire, with secluded dinners in the riverbed.

faqs.q: Who is Kokoko Camp best for?
faqs.a: Small private groups of friends or family who want an exclusive-use camp and an authentic, walking-focused Ruaha safari.

why.title: Hawaii’s Wild Side, Unlocked

onlyHere: At Kudadoo, you discover a rare balance of hyper luxury and a minimal environmental footprint. why.body: Because Kudadoo is not just another luxury escape, it is a statement that you can travel in utter comfort while still honoring the natural world. stays.name: Kura Boutique Hotel
stays.tagline: An adults-only rainforest sanctuary suspended between jungle and ocean.
stays.quote: Luxury feels different when the rainforest is your neighbor and the Pacific is your horizon.
stays.bestMonthsNote: The dry season from December through April offers sunny days, spectacular sunsets, and excellent wildlife viewing. July and August are also exceptional due to the Southern Pacific whale migration season and lush rainforest conditions.

stays.airportDirections: Helicopter from SJO (40 min), or a 20-min flight to XQP then a 60-min transfer. Drive: 4 hrs from SJO to Uvita, last stretch 4x4 only.

onlyHere: Perched high above Costa Rica's Southern Pacific coastline, Kura offers a rare balance of design, intimacy, and immersion in nature. Here, the rainforest stretches endlessly toward the Pacific Ocean, creating a setting where every sunrise, sunset, and wildlife encounter feels extraordinary.

why.title: Where The Rainforest Meets The Horizon
why.body: Kura was created by architect Martin Wells and biologist Alejandra Umaña as an adults-only hotel of just 8 suites, perched above Uvita with rainforest on one side and the Pacific on the other. It pairs intimate, design-led luxury with a strong commitment to sustainability.
Best For:
Honeymoon & Couples
Exclusive Use

facts.best_months: December to April is the dry season, with a mini dry season in late July and early August and whale season from May to November.
facts.how_to_get_there: Helicopter from San José (SJO) in about 40 minutes, or fly 20 minutes from SJO to Quepos (XQP) and transfer about 60 minutes, or drive about 4 hours to Uvita.
facts.signature_experiences: The saltwater infinity pool over the Whale's Tail, Spa Shà, Sky Lounge dinners, whale watching and the Nauyaca Waterfalls hike.
facts.who_its_for: Adults-only (over 18), designed for couples and honeymooners, with whole-hotel exclusive use available.

faqs.q: Where is Kura Boutique Hotel?
faqs.a: Kura sits on a coastal ridge about 1,100 feet above Uvita on Costa Rica's South Pacific coast, overlooking Marino Ballena National Park and the Whale's Tail sandbar. It is about 60 minutes south of Manuel Antonio.

faqs.q: How do you get to Kura?
faqs.a: The quickest way is a helicopter charter from San José (SJO), about 40 minutes, to a helipad 5 minutes from the hotel. Or fly 20 minutes from SJO to the Quepos airstrip (XQP) and transfer about 60 minutes to Kura. By road it is about 4 hours from SJO to Uvita; the final climb is 4x4 only, so the hotel meets self-drivers in Uvita.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kura?
faqs.a: The dry season runs December to April, with a short mini dry season in late July and early August. Kura calls May to November Wildlife Season, when humpback whales visit and turtles nest; September and October are the rainiest months.

faqs.q: How many suites does Kura have?
faqs.a: Kura has 8 suites: Master Suites, Deluxe Suites, Suites and Junior Suites, four of them with private Kura-style infinity plunge pools. Two separate BlackHouse Villas by Kura sit three minutes away by car.

faqs.q: Is Kura adults-only?
faqs.a: Yes. Guests must be over 18, and younger guests are welcome only when a single party books the whole hotel.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Kura?
faqs.a: The saltwater infinity pool with Whale's Tail views, Spa Shà treatments, private candlelit dinners in the rooftop Sky Lounge, whale watching from Uvita, the Nauyaca Waterfalls hike and tours to Corcovado National Park.

faqs.q: Who is Kura best for?
faqs.a: Couples and honeymooners who want privacy and design; the hotel says its suites were designed with couples in mind. Groups can also book the whole hotel for exclusive use.

stays.name: Kwando 4 Rivers Camp
stays.tagline: Exclusive, game-rich wilderness in the northern Delta.
stays.quote: Tucked away in a remote corner of the Kwara Reserve, 4 Rivers offers an exclusive, classic Okavango tented safari experience.
stays.airportDirections: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
stays.founderNote: First stayed with Kwando in 2012. Struck by the warmth of the service and by how intimate the locations are: fewer rooms, far fewer vehicles, and more wildlife, especially predators. That density of sightings for the price makes Kwando better value for the money than the larger branded safari circuits.

paras: At 4 Rivers, you will experience the true essence of the Okavango Delta in a setting that feels both remote and deeply comfortable. Your accommodation consists of classic, well-appointed tented suites that overlook a beautiful, permanent lagoon. These suites are designed to provide you with a peaceful sanctuary, allowing you to wake up to the sounds of the bush and the sight of the floodplains. The camp is intimate, ensuring that your stay is personal and quiet. You will spend your time between the comfortable main lodge area and your private tent, where the design emphasizes a connection to the surrounding wilderness. Whether you are watching the sunset over the water or enjoying a quiet moment on your deck, the camp provides a perfect, understated luxury that allows the natural beauty of the northern Delta to take center stage.

Enjoy an exclusive traversing area focusing on walking, game drives (off-road and night drives), and seasonal mokoro excursions. Off-road on-foot with specialist walking guide and explore Maboa Island to learn about the Okavango ecosystem. Look for Cape clawless otters, elephants splashing about in the Tsum Tsum River, and sable antelope in the ancient woodlands.

4 Rivers features classic, comfortable tented suites situated on the banks of the Tsum Tsum River. The camp is designed for intimacy, with a focus on high-quality guiding and tracking. Each open 4x4 vehicle is staffed by both a guide and a tracker, doubling your chances of spotting elusive wildlife. The camp’s main area overlooks a permanent lagoon, providing a stunning backdrop for meals and relaxation. It is a modern, yet authentic, base for exploring one of the most game-rich areas in Botswana.

onlyHere: 4 Rivers is located in a remote, exclusive corner of the Kwara Reserve, where no other camp has access. This ensures that your wildlife sightings are private and undisturbed. The camp’s name is inspired by the four deep crossings that once provided the only access to these floodplains, highlighting the rugged, untouched nature of this specific part of the northern Okavango Delta.

why.body: You should stay at 4 Rivers if you are looking for an exclusive, game-rich safari in a remote part of the Okavango Delta. The camp’s location in a vast, private reserve means you will experience the wilderness without the crowds found in other areas. The focus on expert-led game drives, combined with the opportunity for walking safaris and seasonal water activities, makes it a versatile choice for any safari enthusiast. The camp’s intimate size and classic tented design offer a perfect balance of comfort and authenticity. By choosing 4 Rivers, you are choosing a unique, high-quality safari experience that prioritizes the natural environment and the thrill of discovery in one of Botswana’s most pristine landscapes.

facts.best_months: May to October
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
facts.who_its_for: Adventurous travelers and wildlife enthusiasts seeking exclusivity and high-quality game viewing.
facts.signature_experiences: Off-road game drives with expert trackers and seasonal mokoro excursions.

faqs.q: What makes the location of 4 Rivers special?
faqs.a: 4 Rivers is located in a remote, exclusive section of the Kwara Reserve. No other camp has access to this specific part of the concession, which means you will enjoy private, uncrowded wildlife sightings. The camp overlooks the Tsum Tsum River, a region known for its incredible game density.

faqs.q: Are the game drives at 4 Rivers different from other camps?
faqs.a: Yes, each open 4x4 game vehicle at 4 Rivers features both a guide and a tracker. This 'two-person' team approach significantly enhances your ability to spot wildlife, as the tracker focuses on signs and tracks while the guide navigates and provides information, leading to a more successful and rewarding safari.

faqs.q: Is 4 Rivers suitable for a first-time safari visitor?
faqs.a: Absolutely. 4 Rivers offers a classic, comfortable, and highly professional safari experience. With its focus on expert guiding and the abundance of wildlife in the Kwara Reserve, it provides a fantastic introduction to the Okavango Delta for those who want a high-quality, authentic, and exciting safari.

stays.name: Kwando Kwara Camp
stays.tagline: The complete Delta experience in prime wilderness.
stays.quote: Kwara Camp is one of the oldest and most beloved camps in the Delta, offering an authentic, high-density safari experience.
stays.airportDirections: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
stays.founderNote: First stayed with Kwando in 2012. Struck by the warmth of the service and by how intimate the locations are: fewer rooms, far fewer vehicles, and more wildlife, especially predators. That density of sightings for the price makes Kwando better value for the money than the larger branded safari circuits.

paras: At Kwara, you will find yourself immersed in the heart of the Okavango Delta on a secluded, forested island. Your accommodation consists of nine expansive suites elevated on wooden platforms, designed to blend seamlessly into the surrounding landscape. Each suite features a distinct living area, a raised bedroom, and a luxurious bathroom equipped with a double washbasin, a bathtub, and both indoor and outdoor showers. You can relax on your private deck, which offers serene views over the lagoon, providing a perfect vantage point to watch the Delta's rhythms. The camp is connected by sandy paths that lead you to the main lodge, where you can enjoy premium drinks and exceptional dining. Whether you are unwinding after a day of exploration or waking up to the sounds of the bush, your stay here is crafted to be both comfortable and deeply connected to the wild environment.

Kwara is renowned for its comprehensive range of activities, ensuring you experience the Delta from every angle. You can embark on both land and water-based adventures throughout the year. Expert guides and trackers lead you on game drives to spot the region's famous big cats, while seasonal water activities allow you to explore the winding channels by boat or traditional mokoro. The camp's strategic location in the private Kwara Concession guarantees uncrowded sightings and the opportunity for off-road tracking, providing you with an intimate and thrilling encounter with Botswana’s diverse wildlife.

The camp features nine large, luxury suites elevated on raised platforms, each offering a private deck with lagoon views. Guests benefit from a high-end main lodge area, premium beverage selections, and gourmet dining. The camp is designed to be an authentic, 'real-deal' safari stay, emphasizing comfort without sacrificing the raw, natural beauty of the Okavango. With a focus on expert-led game viewing, the camp maintains a high standard of service and hospitality, ensuring your stay is both seamless and memorable.

onlyHere: Kwara is uniquely positioned on a forested island within the heart of the Okavango Delta, offering a rare combination of permanent water access and high-density game viewing. As one of the most established camps in the region, it provides an authentic, cult-favorite safari experience that remains true to its origins while offering modern, elevated luxury. The exclusivity of the private Kwara Concession ensures that your wildlife encounters are intimate and undisturbed.

why.body: You should choose Kwara if you seek a complete, year-round Delta experience that balances high-octane wildlife viewing with refined, laid-back luxury. The camp’s reputation for big cat sightings is legendary, making it a premier destination for those who prioritize predator interaction. By staying here, you benefit from the expertise of seasoned guides and trackers who utilize the private concession to provide an uncrowded, bespoke safari. The combination of land and water activities ensures that no two days are the same, while the camp’s thoughtful design allows you to feel completely at one with the Okavango’s unique ecosystem. It is the perfect choice for travelers who value authenticity, exclusivity, and the thrill of the wild.

facts.best_months: May to October
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
facts.who_its_for: Safari enthusiasts, wildlife photographers, and those seeking an authentic, high-density big cat experience.
facts.signature_experiences: Year-round land and water activities, including mokoro excursions and big cat tracking.

faqs.q: What kind of wildlife can I expect to see at Kwara?
faqs.a: Kwara is world-renowned for its high density of predators, particularly big cats. You can expect to see lions, leopards, and cheetahs, as well as large herds of elephants and buffalo. The diverse landscape of the private concession supports a wide variety of species, ensuring excellent game viewing throughout the year.

faqs.q: Are the activities at Kwara seasonal?
faqs.a: While game drives are available year-round, water-based activities such as mokoro excursions and boating are seasonal and depend on the water levels of the Okavango Delta. However, because of its strategic location, Kwara offers a mix of land and water experiences that provide a well-rounded safari regardless of the season.

faqs.q: Is Kwara suitable for families?
faqs.a: Kwara is generally an adult-oriented camp, often catering to those seeking a quiet, immersive, and authentic safari experience. It is best suited for couples, solo travelers, or small groups of adults who appreciate the focus on high-quality guiding and the exclusive nature of the private concession.

stays.name: Kwando Lagoon Camp
stays.tagline: A legendary predator paradise on the river.
stays.quote: If Botswana’s safari scene had a secret handshake, Lagoon Camp would be in on it.
stays.airportDirections: Light aircraft transfer from Maun or Kasane to the local airstrip.
stays.founderNote: First stayed with Kwando in 2012. Struck by the warmth of the service and by how intimate the locations are: fewer rooms, far fewer vehicles, and more wildlife, especially predators. That density of sightings for the price makes Kwando better value for the money than the larger branded safari circuits.

paras: Tucked along the shady banks of the Kwando River, Lagoon Camp offers a low-key luxury hideout with serious safari credentials. As you settle into your tent, you will find a private deck that serves as your personal viewing platform for the wilderness. The interiors are designed for comfort, featuring an indoor ball-and-claw bathtub for relaxing after a day in the bush, complemented by an invigorating outdoor shower. The camp is set within a vast, remote wilderness where elephants frequently wander past your accommodation. You will feel the history of this location, as it was one of the first camps established in this pristine region. The atmosphere is intimate and authentic, ensuring that your stay is defined by the sounds of the river and the distant calls of the wild, providing a perfect sanctuary in the heart of the Linyanti region.

At Lagoon, the focus is on the raw, untamed power of the Kwando-Linyanti ecosystem. You will head out on game drives to track the region's famous predator populations, including lions known for their hunting prowess. The camp also offers boat cruises on a double-decker boat, allowing you to navigate the winding waterways and observe wildlife from a unique perspective. With the freedom of a private concession, you can enjoy flexible game viewing, including night drives that reveal the nocturnal secrets of the bush. Whether you are watching massive herds of elephants or tracking elusive predators, every excursion is designed to immerse you in the heart of this predator paradise.

Your tent at Lagoon is a private retreat featuring a spacious deck overlooking the river. Inside, you will enjoy the luxury of an indoor ball-and-claw bathtub, perfect for unwinding. The addition of an outdoor shower allows you to bathe under the African sky. The camp provides all essential amenities for a comfortable stay, ensuring you are well-rested for your daily adventures. With a focus on low-impact, high-value tourism, the camp maintains an intimate atmosphere while providing all the necessary comforts for a remote, luxury safari experience.

onlyHere: Lagoon is renowned as one of Botswana’s premier spots for predators, particularly lions that have mastered the art of hunting the region's thirsty megafauna. As one of the original camps in this remote wilderness, it offers an authentic, uncrowded experience that is increasingly rare. The combination of tangled woodlands and winding waterways creates a unique habitat where you can witness the raw, natural drama of the African bush in complete seclusion.

why.body: You should choose Lagoon if you are seeking a deep, immersive connection with one of Africa’s most predator-rich environments. The camp’s long-standing reputation for excellence and its strategic location on the Kwando River make it a bucket-list destination for serious safari enthusiasts. By staying here, you support a pioneer of photographic tourism in Botswana, ensuring your visit contributes to the conservation of this pristine wilderness. The intimate scale of the camp, combined with the expertise of local Batswana guides, guarantees a personalized and transformative experience. Whether you are watching elephants from your deck or tracking lions across the floodplains, Lagoon offers a rare, authentic encounter with the wild that stays with you long after you depart.

facts.best_months: May to October
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft transfer from Maun or Kasane to the local airstrip.
facts.who_its_for: Serious wildlife enthusiasts and photographers seeking predator action.
facts.signature_experiences: Boat cruises on the Kwando River and predator-focused game drives.

faqs.q: What makes the wildlife viewing at Lagoon so special?
faqs.a: Lagoon is located in a remote, predator-rich wilderness. It is famous for its lion prides that have developed unique hunting techniques to take down large prey. Because it is a private concession, you benefit from uncrowded sightings and the ability to go off-road, providing a much more intimate and flexible wildlife experience than in national parks.

faqs.q: Is the camp suitable for families?
faqs.a: While Lagoon is a premier destination for wildlife enthusiasts, its remote location and focus on predator activity make it better suited for adults or families with older children who are interested in a serious safari experience. The camp provides a comfortable, luxury environment, but the primary draw remains the raw, untamed nature of the surrounding bush.

faqs.q: What activities are available besides game drives?
faqs.a: In addition to game drives, you can enjoy boat cruises on the Kwando River using the camp's double-decker boat. These cruises offer a relaxing way to view wildlife, such as elephants and hippos, from the water. Night drives are also available, allowing you to explore the nocturnal world of the Linyanti region with your expert guide.

stays.name: Kwando Lebala Camp
stays.tagline: Expansive floodplains teeming with life.
stays.quote: Watch out for the moving reeds which can reveal all sorts of animals as they move in and out.
stays.airportDirections: Light aircraft transfer from Maun or Kasane to the local airstrip.
stays.founderNote: First stayed with Kwando in 2012. Struck by the warmth of the service and by how intimate the locations are: fewer rooms, far fewer vehicles, and more wildlife, especially predators. That density of sightings for the price makes Kwando better value for the money than the larger branded safari circuits.

paras: Lebala Camp is situated in the vast, open floodplains of the Kwando River, offering you a front-row seat to the Linyanti marshes. Each of the eight tents is designed to provide an immersive experience, with views that stretch across the lush, shifting landscape. As you relax on your private deck, you can watch the reeds sway, often signaling the movement of elephants, lechwe, reedbuck, and hippos. The camp’s design emphasizes a connection to the environment, ensuring that you feel part of the wilderness even while resting in your room. The atmosphere is one of quiet observation, where the rhythm of the marsh dictates the pace of your day. With its remote location and limited number of tents, Lebala provides a peaceful, exclusive retreat where you can truly disconnect and appreciate the natural beauty of Botswana.

At Lebala, your adventures are defined by the dynamic nature of the floodplains. You will head out on game drives to explore the marshes, where the high density of wildlife ensures constant action. The area is famous for its large herds of elephants and buffalo, as well as the predators that follow them. Your guides are experts at navigating the changing terrain, allowing you to get close to the action. Whether you are tracking wild dogs or watching a herd of lechwe splash through the shallows, every activity is an opportunity to witness the raw, untamed beauty of the Linyanti ecosystem in a truly private setting.

Your tent at Lebala is a spacious, comfortable sanctuary designed to blend seamlessly with the surrounding floodplains. Each unit features a private deck where you can enjoy the views of the Linyanti marshes. The interiors are thoughtfully appointed with all the amenities you need for a luxury stay in the bush. The camp’s layout ensures privacy and tranquility, allowing you to enjoy the sounds of the marsh from the comfort of your room. It is the perfect base for your daily explorations of this unique and vibrant ecosystem.

onlyHere: Lebala is unique for its location on the expansive floodplains of the Kwando River. The shifting marshes create a constantly changing landscape that supports an incredible diversity of wildlife, including rare species like the lechwe. Because the reserve is shared between only two camps, you are guaranteed an uncrowded experience, allowing you to observe the natural behavior of animals in a pristine, undisturbed environment that feels like your own private wilderness.

why.body: You should stay at Lebala if you are looking for a remote, high-value safari experience that focuses on the beauty of the floodplains. The camp’s intimate size and expert guiding make it an ideal choice for those who want to get away from the crowds and immerse themselves in the wild. By staying here, you are supporting a commitment to low-impact, photographic tourism that protects this fragile ecosystem. The combination of stunning views, abundant wildlife, and the peace of the Linyanti marshes creates a truly memorable safari. Whether you are a seasoned traveler or on your first safari, Lebala offers a unique perspective on the natural world that is both humbling and deeply rewarding.

facts.best_months: May to October
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft transfer from Maun or Kasane to the local airstrip.
facts.who_its_for: Wildlife enthusiasts and those seeking a remote, peaceful safari.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives through the Linyanti marshes and tracking large elephant herds.

faqs.q: What kind of wildlife can I expect to see at Lebala?
faqs.a: Lebala is located in the Linyanti marshes, which are home to large herds of elephants and buffalo. You will also frequently see lechwe, reedbuck, and hippos. The area is also known for its predator populations, including lions and wild dogs, which are often spotted moving through the floodplains.

faqs.q: Is the camp accessible year-round?
faqs.a: The camp is generally accessible, but the best time to visit is during the dry season from May to October. During this time, the floodplains are more accessible, and wildlife congregates around the remaining water sources, making for excellent game viewing. Always check with your travel planner for the most current conditions.

faqs.q: How does the camp ensure a private experience?
faqs.a: Lebala is one of only two camps in a massive 2,300km² private reserve. This limited access ensures that you will rarely encounter other vehicles, allowing for a truly exclusive and undisturbed safari experience. Your guides have the flexibility to go off-road, ensuring you get the best possible views of the wildlife.

stays.name: Kwando Mma Dinare Camp
stays.tagline: Warm hospitality and big game on the Gomoti.
stays.quote: Mma Dinare, meaning Mother Buffalo, offers a warm, authentic safari experience overlooking the wildlife-rich Gomoti River floodplains.
stays.airportDirections: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
stays.founderNote: First stayed with Kwando in 2012. Struck by the warmth of the service and by how intimate the locations are: fewer rooms, far fewer vehicles, and more wildlife, especially predators. That density of sightings for the price makes Kwando better value for the money than the larger branded safari circuits.

paras: At Mma Dinare, you will be welcomed with the warmth of the Botswana sun and the genuine hospitality of our local staff. Your stay is set in a beautiful, private concession bordering the Moremi Game Reserve, where your tented suite overlooks the vast, wildlife-magnet floodplains of the Gomoti River. The camp is designed for 'laidback luxury,' with raised canvas tents that provide wide-open views of the Delta. You will spend your time relaxing in the comfortable main area, listening to stories from our people, or watching the buffalo and elephants that frequently visit the river. The camp’s design is both elegant and unpretentious, ensuring you feel at home in the heart of the wilderness. Whether you are enjoying a sundowner on the deck or waking up to the sounds of the bush, your stay at Mma Dinare is crafted to be a deeply personal and memorable experience.

Mma Dinare offers a well-rounded safari experience with a mix of land and water activities. You can enjoy day and night game drives, which are excellent for spotting the area's high concentration of predators, including lions and leopards. Seasonal boating and mokoro excursions allow you to explore the Gomoti River’s ebbing waterways, providing a different perspective of the Delta. The area is particularly famous for its buffalo herds and the predators that follow them, ensuring that every game drive is filled with the potential for exciting wildlife interactions.

The camp features raised canvas tented suites that offer wide-open views of the Gomoti River. Mma Dinare is known for its warm, Batswana-led hospitality and its focus on big game viewing. The camp is located in a private 27,000-hectare concession, ensuring an exclusive and uncrowded experience. With a mix of land and water activities, including night drives, the camp provides a comprehensive and exciting safari that is perfect for those who want to see the best of the southern Okavango.

onlyHere: Mma Dinare, meaning 'Mother Buffalo' in Setswana, is uniquely situated on the Gomoti River, a critical dry-season watering point that attracts massive herds of buffalo and elephants. This concentration of prey makes it a predator paradise, offering you some of the most exciting wildlife interactions in the southern Okavango Delta. The camp’s warm, community-focused atmosphere is a hallmark of the Kwando experience.

why.body: You should stay at Mma Dinare if you are looking for a warm, authentic, and game-rich safari experience in the southern Okavango Delta. The camp’s location on the Gomoti River makes it a magnet for wildlife, ensuring that you are always close to the action. The mix of land and water activities, combined with the expertise of our local guides, provides a well-rounded and exciting safari. By choosing Mma Dinare, you are choosing a camp that values hospitality, community, and the raw beauty of the Delta. It is the perfect choice for those who want to see big game in an exclusive, private setting while enjoying the comfort and warmth of a truly special safari home. Whether you are a photographer or a first-time visitor, Mma Dinare offers an unforgettable experience.

facts.best_months: May to October
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft transfer from Maun Airport to the local airstrip.
facts.who_its_for: Families, couples, and wildlife enthusiasts seeking big game and warm hospitality.
facts.signature_experiences: Day and night game drives along the Gomoti River and seasonal mokoro excursions.

faqs.q: What is the significance of the name Mma Dinare?
faqs.a: Mma Dinare means 'Mother Buffalo' in Setswana. The name reflects the camp's location on the Gomoti River, which is a favorite haunt for large bachelor buffalo herds. The presence of these herds attracts a high concentration of predators, making the area a prime spot for exciting wildlife viewing.

stays.name: Loldia House

paras: Rooms in the original main house, built in 1943, and in garden cottages across the estate: a master bedroom in the original house, six country-style en suite rooms in three guest cottages set in lush gardens, and two luxury suites near the lakeshore with views over the lake. The main house has a dining room, a sitting room and a verandah looking over Lake Naivasha and Mount Longonot. An infinity pool sits on an outcrop between two old fig trees, with a poolside spa using natural products by The Wild Herb Company, a gift shop, and Wifi in the main areas.

Guided boat safaris on Lake Naivasha for birdlife and hippos, day and night game drives on the conservancy, gentle walks on the fenced farming side of Loldia, and sundowners over the lake. Day excursions reach Lake Nakuru National Park, known for its rhino and flamingos, Eburu Forest, Hell's Gate National Park and other Rift Valley lakes such as Lake Elementeita.

On the north western shores of Lake Naivasha in Kenya's Great Rift Valley, on a privately owned 6,500-acre conservancy about two hours from Nairobi. Because Loldia is private land rather than a national park, day and night game drives, walks and boat excursions run without park entry restrictions. Loldia House holds a Gold eco-rating from Eco-Tourism Kenya. The nightly rate includes local airstrip transfers, meals, soft drinks, beers, house wines and non-premium spirits, laundry and game vehicle transfers to activities on Loldia ranch.

onlyHere: A 1943 farmhouse that keeps its wide verandas and period detail, with a set lunch served under an ancient fig tree looking out over Lake Naivasha.

faqs.q: Who is Loldia House best for?

faqs.q: Who is Lolebezi best for?
