Londolozi
Reserve
stays.tagline: "Londolozi: Where Wild Africa Awakens the Soul"
stays.quote: The camps & villas of the Londolozi Reserve offers an harmonious blend of heritage and luxury, providing guests with an authentic safari experience deeply rooted in family tradition and a profound connection to the land.
stays.bestMonthsNote:
May to October - Dry Season / Prime Safari Time These cooler, drier months are widely considered the best time to visit Londolozi for exceptional wildlife viewing. Here's why:
Unmatched Wildlife Sightings. Vegetation is sparse, and animals gather around waterholes, making them easier to spot. Leopard sightings are more frequent.
stays.airportDirections: In short there are three major airport serving the Sabi Sands: Kruger Mpumalanga International Airport (for lodges in the western sector) Skukuza Airport (for lodges in the southern sector) Hoedspruit Eastgate Airport (for lodges in the northern sector) We are happy to assist with road transfers from any of these airports to your lodge (only in combination with a confirmed reservation).

paras: Twice-daily game drives in open Land Rovers with a ranger and tracker. Guided walks. Private vehicles for photographers. Daily yoga, private meditation and Healing House treatments. Photographic tuition in the studio. Wellness retreats with Boyd Varty and Martha Beck on published dates. Conservation through the Ripple Fund, from Sand River restoration to rhino protection.

Four camps, the Private Granite Suites and private villas on 15,000 hectares in the Sabi Sand, with private heated plunge pools, open-air baths and interleading family suites. The Healing House at Varty Camp is a dedicated wellness space with treatment rooms, a heat cabin over the Sand River, sound and energy work and the signature Biophony Treatment. Complimentary daily yoga on a deck built into a 500-year-old ebony tree near Founders Camp, with private yoga and meditation on request. A photographic studio with Lightroom tuition, post-production for printing and Canon and Nikon camera and lens hire. A gym at Varty Camp.

onlyHere: Londolozi has followed the same leopard dynasty since 1979, when John Varty and Elmon Mhlongo first earned the trust of the Mother Leopard, and more than four decades of sightings now trace the River, Saseka and Sunsetbend lineages. Add twelve years of wellness safaris at the Healing House, retreats led by Boyd Varty and Martha Beck, and a studio where you can edit and print your leopard photographs before you leave.

why.title: A Spiritual Return to the Wild - An Original
why.body: Londolozi is not just a safari destination. It’s a spiritual return to the wild, a sanctuary where nature, luxury, and legacy converge to offer something truly rare: deep, personal transformation. You're not just witnessing the wild. You’re becoming part of it.

stays.name: Marataba
stays.tagline: A malaria-free Big Five safari in the Waterberg, with three ways to stay
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to September is cool and dry with sparse bush, the best for game viewing and the season for rhino interventions. October to April is green, with afternoon storms, baby animals and the best birding. The wildlife does not migrate, so game viewing is good all year.
stays.airport: Thabazimbi Airstrip; OR Tambo International Airport (JNB), Johannesburg
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Thabazimbi Airstrip, then a road transfer: 40 minutes to Marataba Villa, 1 hour to Safari Lodge, 90 minutes to Mountain Lodge. Or drive from Johannesburg in about 3.5 hours.

paras: Three ways to stay in Marakele National Park. Safari Lodge has fifteen canvas-and-stone tents on the plains, Family Tents with a kids' room among them, and welcomes all ages. Mountain Lodge has five rooms above Waterfall Valley, solar-powered and Scandinavian in feel, for guests 16 and over. Marataba Villa has four luxury tents on the banks of the Matlabas River, booked whole for one family or group, with its own team, chef and private vehicle.

Two game drives a day with a FGASA-accredited field guide, bush walks, morning and sunset water safaris on the Matlabas River, stargazing, and a night in the two-level Thabametsi Treehouse at the foot of the Waterberg. From April to September guests can join specialist vets on a rhino conservation intervention, photographed by the Creative Lab team at no extra cost.

Malaria-free, so it suits young children and anyone avoiding malaria tablets. The Big Five plus brown hyena, aardwolf, pangolin and more than 380 bird species, with black rhino the signature species. Marakele holds one of the world's largest colonies of endangered Cape vultures, more than 800 breeding pairs. Kosher cuisine at Safari Lodge from a dedicated kitchen. Wi-Fi at every lodge.

onlyHere: A Big Five safari a short hop from Johannesburg with no malaria, where a boat carries you up the Matlabas River to elephants drinking at the bank and a treehouse lets you sleep out under the Waterberg stars.

why.title: Three Lodges, One Wilderness
why.body: Best for families with young children, couples who want the adults-only Mountain Lodge, and multigenerational groups who want a villa and vehicle of their own.

facts.best_months: May to September for game viewing and rhino interventions; October to April for green bush, baby animals and birding.

faqs.q: Is Marataba malaria-free?
faqs.a: Yes. Marataba is in the malaria-free Waterberg, so it suits young children and anyone who would rather not take malaria tablets.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Marataba?
faqs.a: Yes at Safari Lodge and Marataba Villa, which welcome all ages. Mountain Lodge is for guests 16 and over.

faqs.q: How do you get to Marataba from Johannesburg?
faqs.a: Fly to Thabazimbi Airstrip and transfer by road (40 minutes to the Villa, 1 hour to Safari Lodge, 90 minutes to Mountain Lodge), or drive from Johannesburg in about 3.5 hours.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Safari Lodge, Mountain Lodge and Marataba Villa?
faqs.a: Safari Lodge has 15 tents on the plains, welcomes families and runs scheduled game drives. Mountain Lodge has 5 rooms above a valley for guests 16 and over. Marataba Villa has 4 tents on the river for private use, with its own team and vehicle.

faqs.q: Can you book a single tent at Marataba Villa?
faqs.a: No. The Villa is booked whole, all four tents with a private team, for one family or group.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Marataba?
faqs.a: May to September for the best game viewing and rhino interventions; October to April for green bush, baby animals and birding. The wildlife does not migrate, so it is good all year.

faqs.q: What wildlife will you see at Marataba?
faqs.a: The Big Five, plus giraffe, zebra, hippo, crocodile and more than 380 bird species. Black rhino is the signature species, and brown hyena, aardwolf and pangolin are possible.

stays.name: Masoala Forest Lodge
stays.tagline: Canopy treehouses where primary rainforest yields directly to coral-shelved ocean
stays.quote: Wake to birdsong in the treetops, fall asleep to the sound of surf on a deserted beach.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Open late April to early January. October to December is driest; humpback whales July to September; closed early January to mid-April.
stays.airport: Maroantsetra Airport (WMN), Ivato International Airport, Antananarivo (TNR)
stays.airportDirections: Scheduled charter from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra on Sundays and Wednesdays (about 90 minutes), then 40 km by lodge boat via Nosy Mangabe.

paras: Primary lowland rainforest meets a sheltered, coral-rich bay on the Masoala Peninsula
Seven palm-thatched treehouses on stilted wooden platforms, with a few metres of beach between each and the sea
A maximum of 14 guests, reached only on foot or by boat
A central beach house for lunch and dinner, and a sea deck for breakfast and afternoon tea

Your journey begins with a domestic flight to Maroantsetra followed by a motorboat crossing of Antongil Bay, a World Heritage area and important humpback whale breeding ground. The crossing sets the tone: ocean travel, the sense of arriving somewhere uncompromised, and immediate access to water-based exploration.

On site, guided rainforest walks trace game trails for birds, endemic lemurs and other canopy species. Night walks reveal nocturnal frogs and chameleons. Offshore, snorkeling and short kayak outings put coral gardens and reef fish within easy reach, and seasonal whale-watching trips leave directly from the lodge’s bay. Guides tailor each day to sightings and conditions, so activities feel handcrafted rather than prepackaged.
An 85 hectare private rainforest reserve bordering Masoala National Park, with seven marked trails
Solar power and low-impact design, with single-use plastic banned in the Madagascar operation
Natural history library, sea deck and massage tent
Small-group naturalist guiding

onlyHere: Wake in a treehouse with your feet almost in the water, snorkel the reef in front of camp
Explore the private reserve's marked trails on your own, a privilege not found in Madagascar's national parks
Nightly walks for nocturnal lemurs, with the aye-aye seen regularly
Boat arrival across Antongil Bay, a World Heritage Site and humpback whale breeding ground

why.title: Rainforest meets ocean
why.body: The Masoala Peninsula holds Madagascar's largest remaining tract of lowland rainforest, and at the lodge the forest comes down to a sheltered beach on the Tampolo Marine Reserve. A morning in the canopy with red ruffed lemurs and helmet vangas can end snorkelling right in front of camp.

why.title: Barefoot seclusion
why.body: Seven palm-thatched treehouses, a maximum of 14 guests and access only on foot or by boat keep the lodge quiet and unhurried.

why.title: Kayak roots, naturalist guiding
why.body: The founders discovered Masoala on kayak expeditions in the late 1990s, and kayaking, pirogue sailing, forest walks and night walks remain at the heart of each stay.

why.title: Wild sea access
why.body: Snorkelling, kayaking and, from July to September, humpback whales in Antongil Bay are part of everyday life here rather than separate day trips.

facts.best_months: Open late April to early January. October to December is driest; humpback whales visit Antongil Bay July to September.
facts.how_to_get_there: Scheduled charter from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra on Sundays and Wednesdays, then 40 km by lodge boat across Antongil Bay via Nosy Mangabe.
facts.signature_experiences: Guided canopy and lowland rainforest walks, night walks for nocturnal species, snorkeling and kayaking in a coral-rich bay, seasonal humpback whale-watching in Antongil Bay, and visits with conservation teams working on the Masoala Peninsula.
facts.who_its_for: Travelers seeking intimate, nature-led stays: couples and honeymooners after seclusion and romance; active, adventurous guests who want rainforest trekking and snorkeling; lone travelers who value safety and small-group guiding; and wildlife photographers targeting endemic forest species and seasonal whales.

faqs.q: What is Masoala Forest Lodge known for?
faqs.a: Masoala Forest Lodge is known for its unique location where intact primary rainforest meets coral-rich ocean, its elevated palm-thatched treehouses, and close links to conservation and research on the Masoala Peninsula.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Masoala Forest Lodge have?
faqs.a: The lodge has seven palm-thatched treehouses on stilted wooden platforms, each a few metres from the sea, and takes a maximum of 14 guests, keeping it intentionally small-scale.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Masoala Forest Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge is open from late April to early January. October to December is the driest period, humpback whales visit Antongil Bay from July to September, and the lodge closes from early January to mid-April.

faqs.q: Is Masoala Forest Lodge good for families?
faqs.a: The lodge can work well for families who are comfortable with elevated walkways, boat transfers and simple, nature-focused accommodation. Check with the lodge about minimum age limits and options for private guiding or family arrangements.

faqs.q: How do you get to Masoala Forest Lodge?
faqs.a: By scheduled charter flight from Antananarivo to Maroantsetra on Sundays and Wednesdays (about 90 minutes), then 40 km by lodge boat across Antongil Bay via Nosy Mangabe, landing directly on the lodge's beach.

faqs.q: What wildlife might I see at Masoala Forest Lodge?
faqs.a: Expect to encounter endemic lemurs, a rich array of forest birds and reptiles, and seasonally, humpback whales in Antongil Bay; reef snorkeling reveals coral and reef fish close to shore.

faqs.q: How sustainability-minded is the lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge operates with solar-based systems, sources food locally and organically where possible, and sits within a private conservation reserve that supports research and community initiatives.

Its thatched-roof casitas and villas sit among gardens, giving the resort a relaxed, individual feel rather than the scale of a conventional beach hotel. Spend unhurried hours by the water, then head out to snorkel or dive the reef, or return for a spa treatment and dinner. It suits travelers drawn to Caribbean simplicity with thoughtful comforts.

facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Philip S. W. Goldson International Airport, connect to San Pedro on Ambergris Caye by domestic flight or water taxi, then arrange a resort transfer.

facts.signature_experiences: Snorkeling and diving excursions to the Belize Barrier Reef, time on Ambergris Caye’s shoreline, and spa treatments at the resort.

faqs.q: What is Matachica Resort & Spa known for?
faqs.a: Matachica is known for its thatched-roof casitas and villas, beachfront setting on Ambergris Caye, and access to Belize Barrier Reef activities. The resort also has an on-site spa.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Matachica Resort & Spa have?
faqs.a: Matachica has 32 casitas and villas. Confirm current accommodation counts and categories directly with the resort, as inventory may change.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Matachica Resort & Spa?
faqs.a: Belize’s drier season, generally December through May, is a popular time to visit. Conditions vary, so check seasonal weather and sea conditions when planning reef activities.

faqs.q: Is Matachica Resort & Spa good for families?

faqs.q: How do you get to Matachica Resort & Spa?

faqs.q: Can guests snorkel or dive from Matachica Resort & Spa?
faqs.a: The resort provides access to excursions on the Belize Barrier Reef, including snorkeling and diving opportunities. Availability and conditions depend on the day and should be confirmed with the property.

stays.name: Matetsi Victoria Falls

Game drives, including night drives, and walking safaris in Matetsi Private Game Reserve. Sunrise and sunset boat cruises on the Zambezi. Fishing. Birdwatching. Guided Victoria Falls tours. Boma dining. Africology spa treatments.

136,000-acre (55,000-hectare) Matetsi Private Game Reserve. 15 km of private Zambezi River frontage. Private plunge pool and river views from every suite. Interiors by a Zimbabwean architectural designer on a 'Life on the River' theme. Private wine cellar. Africology spa treatments in the massage sala. Private airstrip and helipad.

why.title: River. Falls. Safari. All Yours.

facts.signature_experiences: Game drives and walks in a 136,000-acre private reserve, Zambezi boat cruises and fishing, and Victoria Falls tours.
facts.who_its_for: Families, couples and groups who want safari, river and Victoria Falls in one stay.

faqs.q: Where is Matetsi Victoria Falls?
faqs.a: Matetsi sits on a private 15 km (9-mile) stretch of the Zambezi River, about 40 km upriver from Victoria Falls, within the 136,000-acre Matetsi Private Game Reserve in Zimbabwe.

faqs.q: How do you get to Matetsi Victoria Falls?
faqs.a: It is about an hour (60 km) by road from Victoria Falls International Airport, and about 40 minutes from Victoria Falls town, with complimentary road transfers within the Victoria Falls area. Livingstone and Kasane are about 1.5 hours away including the border crossing, and helicopters and charter flights can land at the lodge's own helipad and airstrip.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Matetsi?
faqs.a: Matetsi says the dry season, July to November, gives the best chance of large elephant and buffalo herds. From November the rains bring calving season, and the green season is good for birding.

faqs.q: How many suites does Matetsi have?
faqs.a: There are 16 River Suites and two River Family Suites, each with a private plunge pool, plus the exclusive-use four-bedroom River House.

faqs.q: Is Matetsi good for children?
faqs.a: Children of all ages are welcome. Family suites pair a main bedroom with a children's room for children up to 16, and walking safaris are for ages 16 and over, or 13 to 15 at the manager's or head guide's discretion.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Matetsi?
faqs.a: Game drives, including night drives, and walking safaris in the private reserve, sunrise and sunset boat cruises and fishing on the Zambezi, and guided visits to Victoria Falls.

faqs.q: Can Matetsi be booked for exclusive use?
faqs.a: Yes. The whole lodge can be booked with private access to the reserve and river frontage, or the western guest area with up to seven suites, as well as the four-bedroom River House.

why.title: A small hotel inside Tulum's protected Jaguar Park
why.body: Mezzanine is a boutique hotel with three room categories, set above the sea in a protected stretch of Tulum near the ruins. Days centre on the view, the beach below and the Thai restaurant, with packages to cenotes, canals and Sian Ka'an. The hotel welcomes guests aged 16 and over.

facts.best_months: November to April, the dry season as Mezzanine describes it; May to October is the wet season.

facts.signature_experiences: Thai dining on the cliffside terrace; packages to cenotes, ancient canals, the Mayan ruins and Sian Ka'an; the sister property Hotel Mi Amor, 3 minutes away, with its restaurant and infinity pool.
facts.who_its_for: Guests 16 and over looking for a small hotel in a protected area near the Tulum ruins, with Thai cuisine and sea views.

faqs.q: Where is Mezzanine Tulum?
faqs.a: Mezzanine sits inside Jaguar Park, a protected area of Tulum, at Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila Km 4.4. The hotel says it is framed between the jungle and the Caribbean, steps from the ancient Mayan ruins.

faqs.q: How do I get to Mezzanine Tulum?
faqs.a: Fly into Tulum International Airport (TQO) or Cancún International Airport (CUN). The concierge books round-trip airport transfers by email with your flight details and number of guests, with payment taken in advance.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Mezzanine Tulum?
faqs.a: Mezzanine describes Tulum's dry season as November to April and the wet season as May to October. January to March days usually sit around 23 to 26C with cooler evenings.

faqs.q: What rooms does Mezzanine Tulum have?
faqs.a: There are three room categories: the Penthouse with Plunge Pool (two penthouses), the Sea View Room and the Interior Room. Every guest room has air conditioning.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Mezzanine Tulum?
faqs.a: No. Children under 16 are not permitted to stay at the hotel, though children are welcome in the restaurant.

faqs.q: What is special about dining at Mezzanine?
faqs.a: The restaurant serves Thai cuisine on a cliffside terrace over the Caribbean, from a menu by Thai Chef Jakkree Putaruk and Executive Chef Liliana López. Breakfast and the beach menu also include Mexican staples.

faqs.q: Who is Mezzanine Tulum best for?
faqs.a: Adults and older teens who want a small hotel in a protected stretch of Tulum with sea views and Thai food. It is not wheelchair accessible because of the landscape.

facts.best_months: Open all year, with peak season mid-June to October and elephants in reception from late October to mid-December.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport (MFU), then a 45-minute game-viewing transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Elephants walking through reception in mango season, game drives, walking safaris and the Bush-Spa.
facts.who_its_for: Families and safari guests starting or ending a South Luangwa bushcamp circuit.

faqs.q: Where is Mfuwe Lodge?
faqs.a: Mfuwe Lodge is set between two lagoons just inside the entrance to South Luangwa National Park, Zambia. It is The Bushcamp Company's gateway lodge and the usual start or end of its bushcamp circuit.

faqs.q: How do you get to Mfuwe Lodge?
faqs.a: Fly to Mfuwe International Airport (MFU), which has daily scheduled Proflight Zambia flights from Lusaka. From there it is a 45-minute transfer in an open game-viewing vehicle.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Mfuwe Lodge?
faqs.a: Mfuwe Lodge is open all year. Peak season runs from mid-June to October, the green season from December to April, and elephant families walk through reception between late October and mid-December.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Mfuwe Lodge have?
faqs.a: There are 18 air-conditioned thatched chalets: two suites, three family rooms and thirteen rooms. The Family House at Mfuwe Lodge is a separate option for families and friends.

faqs.q: Where is Miavana?
faqs.a: Miavana is on Nosy Ankao, the largest of five islands in a remote archipelago off the northeastern coast of Madagascar. The private island is around 10 square kilometres and is run by Time + Tide.

faqs.q: How do you get to Miavana?
faqs.a: By helicopter only: a helicopter transfer from Diego Suarez or Nosy Be is the only way onto the island. Time + Tide also offers a seven-night Private Jet Package with return private jet flights from Johannesburg to Diego Suarez (minimum five adults).

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Miavana?
faqs.a: Miavana is open year round. Humpback whales pass from July to September, kiteboarding is best from May to October, diving is best from November to April, and turtles nest in December with hatchlings in April.

faqs.q: What villas does Miavana have?
faqs.a: Miavana has 13 ocean-front villas: 7 one-bedroom, 4 two-bedroom and 2 three-bedroom, each with a private pool, direct beach access and private butler service. The whole island can be booked for exclusive use by up to 42 guests.

faqs.q: Is Miavana good for children?
faqs.a: Yes, all ages are welcome. Each villa has a study that converts to a children's bedroom, and the team builds a personalised adventure programme for children, from lemur tracking and turtle walks to crafts and guided quad biking.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Miavana?
faqs.a: Scuba diving with a PADI-certified dive centre, kiteboarding, lemur trekking for the island's crowned lemurs, blue safaris for dolphins and whales, fishing, turtle monitoring and helicopter excursions to places such as Ankarana and the Tsingy Rouge.

faqs.q: Who is Miavana best for?
faqs.a: Families, honeymooners and couples, active travelers drawn to the sea, and groups who want a private island entirely to themselves.

faqs.a: A 90-minute drive from Zanzibar Airport or Stone Town to the departure point, then a 10 to 15 minute boat ride onto the beach. There are no jetties, so guests wade through shallow water, and a private helicopter option to the Matemwe landing site is also available.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Mnemba Island?

faqs.a: Big cats. Lion and cheetah are frequently seen, with leopard, caracal and serval often making an appearance, alongside abundant plains game.

faqs.q: What else is there to do at Namiri Plains?
faqs.a: Dawn to dusk game drives, specialised photographic safaris in custom-designed vehicles, a swimming pool, a library and massages at the Asilia spa.

onlyHere: Only here can you wake up in a valley carved by time, spend your day crossing Mars-like terrain, and return to candle-lit silence beneath the Milky Way.

facts.best_months: March to May and September to November: clear skies, mild days and cold, dark nights for the stars. The desert is dry all year; December to February is warmest and busiest.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly Santiago to Calama, El Loa Airport (CJC), about 2 hours, then around 1½ hours by road to the hotel outside San Pedro de Atacama. The house arranges the transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Stargazing from the hotel's own observatory under some of the clearest skies on Earth; the salt mountains and the salt lake; the altiplano lagoons and geyser fields on guided excursions; the gardens and villas finished by local artisans; silence.
facts.who_its_for: Couples after remote luxury, adventure travellers, wellness-minded guests, and anyone who comes for the night sky.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nayara Alto Atacama?
faqs.a: March to May and September to November, for mild days, cold clear nights and the best stargazing. The Atacama is dry all year; December to February is warmest and busiest.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Alto Atacama?
faqs.a: Fly from Santiago to Calama (CJC), about two hours, then about an hour and a half by road to the hotel on the edge of San Pedro de Atacama. The house arranges the transfer.

faqs.q: How big is Nayara Alto Atacama?
faqs.a: A 42-room hotel set into a valley of salt mountains outside San Pedro de Atacama, with gardens, villas and an observatory, run by Nayara Resorts since 2020.

faqs.q: Can you combine the Atacama with Easter Island or Patagonia?
faqs.a: Yes. Every route runs through Santiago, so the Atacama pairs with Rapa Nui or with Patagonia. Allow around two weeks for two of the three.

facts.signature_experiences: Overwater villas with glass floor inlays, bamboo treehouses, snorkeling, mangrove kayaking and bioluminescence.

faqs.q: Where is Nayara Bocas del Toro?
faqs.a: Nayara Bocas del Toro is on a private island in the Bocas del Toro archipelago on Panama's Caribbean coast, a short boat ride from Isla Colón.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Bocas del Toro?
faqs.a: Fly from Panama City's Albrook Airport (PAC) to Bocas del Toro Airport (BOC); SANSA also flies from San José (SJO) to BOC a few times a week. The team meets you for a brief drive to the dock and a complimentary 20 minute boat transfer to the island.

faqs.q: Is Nayara Bocas del Toro adults only?
faqs.a: Yes. It is an adults-only resort for guests 16 and over, designed for couples and friends.

faqs.q: What villas does Nayara Bocas del Toro have?
faqs.a: Overwater Pool Villas and Overwater Pool Villa Deluxe (102 m²) with private plunge pools and swim-up staircases, IBUKU-designed bamboo Treehouses about fifty feet above the ground, and a 191 m² Presidential Overwater Villa with its own saltwater infinity pool.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nayara Bocas del Toro?
faqs.a: Nayara recommends February to April or September to October, when seas are typically calm and sunny. The main green season runs May to August, with another rainy spell from November to December.

faqs.q: What is included and what can you do?
faqs.a: The stay is all inclusive, covering dining, premium drinks, non-motorized water sports and round-trip boat transfers from BOC. Snorkeling, kayaking through mangroves and paddleboarding are complimentary; diving, fishing and private boat trips to the Zapatilla Islands and Dolphin Bay can be arranged.

stays.tagline: Luxury rainforest living beneath Costa Rica’s iconic Arenal Volcano.
stays.quote: Where tropical gardens, volcano views, and wildlife surround every moment.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Costa Rica’s dry season delivers ideal weather for volcano exploration, wildlife encounters, rainforest hiking, outdoor wellness experiences, and enjoying clear views of Arenal Volcano with lower rainfall and comfortable tropical conditions.

onlyHere: Nayara Gardens sits in tropical gardens below Arenal Volcano, where thousands of planted Cecropia trees draw resident sloths. Guests move between private plunge pools, seven rainforest hot spring pools and the restaurants of the wider Nayara campus.

facts.best_months: Open all year; Nayara describes January to May as very warm with mostly afternoon rain, and June to December as hot with rain at any time.
facts.how_to_get_there: Private plane to La Fortuna airstrip then 15 to 20 minutes by road, or about 3 hours by private transfer from SJO or LIR.
facts.signature_experiences: Private plunge pools, the seven Termas hot spring pools, sloth spotting, daily yoga and the award-winning spa.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and families, with children of all ages welcome.

faqs.q: Where is Nayara Gardens?
faqs.a: Nayara Gardens is in the Arenal Volcano National Park area of Costa Rica, near La Fortuna. It is the original resort on Nayara's Arenal campus, alongside Nayara Springs and Nayara Tented Camp.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Gardens?
faqs.a: The quickest route is a private plane to the La Fortuna airstrip, then a 15 to 20 minute drive, which the resort can coordinate. Private road transfers from San José (SJO) or Liberia (LIR) take about 3 hours, driven by local naturalists.

faqs.q: What rooms does Nayara Gardens have?
faqs.a: Freestanding casitas in two styles: the Arenal Pool Casita (97 m²) with a garden deck and private plunge pool, and the octagonal Rainforest Pool Villa (105.4 m²) with a plunge pool on a wraparound balcony. Both have indoor and outdoor rain showers.

faqs.q: Is Nayara Gardens good for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Nayara Gardens is family friendly and welcomes children of all ages. Arenal Pool Casitas sleep two adults and two children under 18, Rainforest Pool Villas two adults and one child; there is no kids' club, but babysitting can be booked in advance.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nayara Gardens?
faqs.a: The resort is open all year. Nayara describes January to May as very warm with rain usually in the afternoons, and June to December as hot with rain possible at any time of day.

faqs.q: Are there sloths and hot springs at Nayara Gardens?
faqs.a: Yes. Nayara has planted thousands of Cecropia (Guarumo) trees that sloths love, and guides help guests spot them. The Termas are seven mineral hot spring pools set in the rainforest.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Nayara Gardens, Springs and Tented Camp?
faqs.a: All three share one Arenal campus. Gardens is the family-friendly original with casitas and villas, Springs is the adults-only villa retreat with hot spring plunge pools, and Tented Camp offers stilted tents with hot spring fed pools for couples and families.

stays.name: Nayara Hangaroa
stays.tagline: A luxury sanctuary at the edge of the Pacific where ancient culture meets volcanic wilderness.
stays.quote: Some journeys are vacations. Others become part of your story forever.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months provide the warmest temperatures, calmer ocean conditions, vibrant cultural activity, and ideal weather for exploring archaeological sites, coastal landscapes, and Pacific sunsets across Rapa Nui.
stays.airportDirections: Mataveri International Airport is located approximately 10 minutes by vehicle from Nayara Hangaroa. Private transfers are the preferred arrival option.
onlyHere: Nayara Hangaroa offers one of the world’s rarest luxury experiences , staying on the remote island of Rapa Nui surrounded by sacred history, volcanic cliffs, and the endless Pacific Ocean. Here, luxury feels deeply connected to culture, ancestry, and the rhythms of island life.

why.title: Place
why.body: Rapa Nui is about 3,700 km out in the Pacific, one flight from Santiago and nothing else for days of sailing in any direction. Nayara Hangaroa sits on the ocean a few minutes from the island's one town, in stone buildings roofed with the thick mauku grass the Rapanui used for shelter, with terraces that look straight at the Pacific. It is the island's address for seeing the quarry at Rano Raraku, the platforms, Orongo on the crater rim and the stars, and still being back by the water for sunset.

why.title: People
why.body: Nayara Hangaroa is part of Nayara Resorts, the Costa Rican house that took on the former Hangaroa Eco Village in 2020. The house has not yet confirmed a named host; the island's Rapanui guides are the people who make the days here.

why.title: Impact
why.body: Not yet documented by the house. Nothing is claimed until the property states it.

why.title: James' note
why.body: I haven't stood on Rapa Nui yet; it's on my own list for the reason it's on this one. An island that far out, with a culture that is still spoken and danced rather than fenced off, is the kind of place you give five nights and don't try to rush. Nayara is where I'd put the bags down.

facts.best_months: October to March, when the island is warmest and the sea calmest; January to March is the dry season and February brings the Tapati festival.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly Santiago to Mataveri (IPC), about 5½ hours, the only way in. The hotel is around ten minutes from the airport by road and collects you.
facts.signature_experiences: Rano Raraku, where the moai were carved; Ahu Tongariki's fifteen statues at first light; Orongo on the rim of Rano Kau; a walk up Terevaka; an afternoon at Anakena; the southern night sky from the terrace.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and honeymooners after distance and quiet, solo travellers, walkers, and anyone who wants the archaeology with the living Rapanui culture around it.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at Nayara Hangaroa?
faqs.a: October to March, for the warmest weather and calmest sea; January to March is the dry season and February is the Tapati festival. The island is subtropical and warm all year, so the quieter southern winter still works.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Hangaroa?
faqs.a: By air from Santiago to Mataveri International Airport (IPC), about five and a half hours, the only route to the island. The hotel is around ten minutes from the airport and arranges the transfer.

faqs.q: How many nights should you stay on Rapa Nui?
faqs.a: Four or five. That covers the quarry at Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki at dawn, Orongo and Rano Kau, a walk up Terevaka, an afternoon at Anakena and an evening of stargazing without rushing any of it.

faqs.q: Is Nayara Hangaroa near the town?
faqs.a: Yes. It sits on the ocean a few minutes from Hanga Roa, the island's only town, close enough to walk in for the evening and still be on the water for sunset.

faqs.q: Can you combine Rapa Nui with the rest of Chile?
faqs.a: Yes. Every route runs through Santiago, so Rapa Nui pairs with the Atacama desert in the north or Patagonia in the south. Allow around two weeks for two of the three.

facts.who_its_for: Adults only (18 and over), designed for couples seeking a romantic, secluded rainforest retreat.

faqs.q: Where is Nayara Springs?
faqs.a: Nayara Springs is in the Arenal Volcano National Park area of Costa Rica, about 7 km from the town of La Fortuna. It shares one rainforest campus with its sister resorts, Nayara Gardens and Nayara Tented Camp.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Springs?
faqs.a: The quickest way is a private plane to the La Fortuna airstrip, then a 15 to 20 minute drive, which the resort can coordinate. By road, private transfers from San José (SJO) or Liberia (LIR) take about 3 hours and are driven by local naturalists.

faqs.q: Is Nayara Springs adults only?
faqs.a: Yes. All guests must be at least 18. Families with children are directed to the sister properties, Nayara Gardens and Nayara Tented Camp.

faqs.q: What are the villas like at Nayara Springs?
faqs.a: Guests stay in Springs Villas of 139 m² (1,500 sq ft), each with a private plunge pool fed by natural mineral hot springs, a four-poster king bed, a private garden with dual rain showers and indoor and outdoor sitting areas. Every Springs Villa comes with a private host.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nayara Springs?
faqs.a: The resort is open all year. Nayara describes January to May as very warm with rain usually in the afternoons, and June to December as hot with rain possible at any time of day.

faqs.q: What is there to do at Nayara Springs?
faqs.a: Soak in your villa's hot spring pool, join the daily instructor-led yoga, walk the Perezoso Trail to look for resident sloths and take the naturalist-led frog night tour. Private guides arrange hanging bridges, volcano hikes, coffee and cacao visits, zip lining, rappelling and rafting.

faqs.q: Who is Nayara Springs best for?
faqs.a: Couples and adults wanting a romantic, secluded stay. Guests also have full access to the restaurants and facilities of Nayara Gardens and Nayara Tented Camp, including the adults-only Amor Loco and Mis Amores.

faqs.q: Where is Nayara Tented Camp?
faqs.a: Nayara Tented Camp sits high above the rainforest in the Arenal Volcano National Park area of Costa Rica, on reforested land that is part of Nayara's Arenal campus with Nayara Gardens and Nayara Springs.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nayara Tented Camp?
faqs.a: The fastest option is a private plane to the La Fortuna airstrip followed by a 15 to 20 minute drive, which the resort can coordinate. Private road transfers from San José (SJO) or Liberia (LIR) take about 3 hours, driven by local naturalists.

faqs.q: What accommodation does Nayara Tented Camp have?
faqs.a: Stilted tents in four styles: the Nayara Tent (2 adults, 2 children) and the Family Tent (two tents sharing an outdoor living space and pool) each have a pool fed by mineral hot springs; the Grand Tent adds a kitchen and an oversized infinity pool; and two Private Residences, Casa Paloma and Casa Dana, sleep up to 12 adults with a hot spring fed infinity pool.

faqs.q: Is Nayara Tented Camp good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The camp is family friendly, with Family Tents, Grand Tents and two Private Residences designed for families, small groups and multi-generational travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nayara Tented Camp?
faqs.a: The camp is open all year. Nayara describes January to May as very warm with rain usually in the afternoons, and June to December as hot with rain possible at any time of day.

faqs.q: What wildlife and experiences are there at Nayara Tented Camp?
faqs.a: Guests often see sloths, toucans and tropical birds from their clifftop decks, as the tents sit in a reforestation corridor. Naturalist guides lead hanging bridges, volcano hikes, coffee and cacao visits and other Arenal adventures.
