stays.quote: Find your island, One-Bedroom Beach House. Two-Bedroom Beach House. Three-Bedroom Beach House. Whole Island Exclusive Use.wake to the sound of waves, walk sandy paths, and rediscover time with people you love. Nikoi is wild, simple, and simply unforgettable.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dry season is best for swimming, snorkeling, and beach life, calm seas, clear skies, and warm temperatures year-round.
stays.airport: Raja Haji Fisabilillah International Airport (TNJ), Singapore Changi Airport (SIN)
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Singapore or Bintan, fast ferry to Bintan, then a 1-hour private car and speedboat transfer to Nikoi Island (arranged by lodge).

paras: Beautiful driftwood beach houses, each steps from the sea with open-air living and private decks. White sand beaches. Coral reefs. Award-winning eco-design. Family-friendly and safe. Organic food. Solar-powered. Complimentary water sports equipment.

onlyHere: Nikoi is perfect for couples, families, groups, or solo travelers seeking privacy, barefoot luxury, and connection to nature. Swim, explore, or just be, in a place that’s both wild and welcoming.

why.title: Wild Beauty, Pure Simplicity
why.body: Stay for total privacy, stunning natural beauty, laid-back luxury, and the sense that time slows down. Ideal for couples, families, honeymooners, and anyone who wants their own private island paradise with a positive impact.

stays.name: Nimali Mara
stays.tagline: Ten tented suites in the kopjes above the Mara River crossings

paras: Eight tented suites and two honeymoon suites, each with a private deck looking out over the Serengeti and a bath with a view of the plains. Interiors mix contemporary lines with earthy textures and fabrics.
Morning and afternoon game drives to the Mara River crossings, at their peak from July to October. Elephants and predators year round. Hot-air balloon flights over the northern plains and the river.

In the far north of the Serengeti near the Kenyan border, tucked into a kopje close to the Mara River. An infinity pool set into the rock and a campfire under the stars. A four-hour game drive from its sister camp, Nimali Serengeti.

onlyHere: A camp built into the rocks within reach of the Mara River, where the wildebeest migration makes its most dramatic crossings between July and October.

why.title: Front Row for the Crossings
why.body: Best for couples, honeymooners, photographers and migration seekers.

facts.best_months: July to October, when the wildebeest migration crossings of the Mara River are at their peak.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Kogatende Airstrip, then a 35-minute road transfer, or a four-hour game drive from Nimali Serengeti.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives to the Mara River crossings, hot-air balloon flights over the northern plains, spa treatments, bush dinners and sundowners.
facts.who_its_for: Honeymooners and couples, migration seekers, and families who are happy with Nimali's age guidelines for game drives and walks.

faqs.q: Where is Nimali Mara?
faqs.a: Nimali Mara is in the far north of Tanzania's Serengeti, close to the Kenyan border, tucked into the kopjes near the Mara River. This is where the wildebeest migration crosses the Mara River.

faqs.q: How do I get to Nimali Mara?
faqs.a: Fly to Kogatende Airstrip, then take a 35-minute road transfer to the lodge. By road, Nimali Mara is a four-hour game drive from its sister camp, Nimali Serengeti.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nimali Mara?
faqs.a: July to October, when the migration crossings of the Mara River reach their peak. The area is also known for its elephants and predators.

faqs.q: How many suites does Nimali Mara have?
faqs.a: There are eight tented suites and two honeymoon suites, each with a private deck looking out over the Serengeti and a bath with a view of the plains. An infinity pool is set into the natural rock formations.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Nimali Mara?
faqs.a: Yes, Nimali welcomes families. Children under 6 are not allowed on game drives in open vehicles, and children under 12 cannot join walking safaris or bush camping.

faqs.q: What activities does Nimali Mara offer?
faqs.a: Morning and afternoon game drives to see the river crossings, plus spa treatments, bush dinners and sundowners. Nimali also highly recommends a hot-air balloon flight over the northern plains and the Mara River.

stays.name: Nimali Serengeti
stays.tagline: Twelve tented suites in the heart of the Serengeti

paras: Twelve tented suites, two of them linked by a shared walkway for families, each with a private verandah and an en-suite bathroom with bathtub and outdoor shower. Interiors take their cue from the migration.
Morning and afternoon game drives for lion, cheetah and leopard. The migration moves through from April to June and October to December. Hot-air balloon flights. Dinner under the stars.

In the central Serengeti, in a new position near Makoma Hill with uninterrupted views over kopje-dotted plains. A central lounge, dining area and pool deck. Four hours by road from the Ngorongoro Crater gate and a four-hour game drive from its sister camp, Nimali Mara.

onlyHere: A central Serengeti base on one of the migration's main routes, with strong big cat sightings in every season.

why.title: Big Cats All Year
why.body: Best for first-time safari-goers, families and photographers.

facts.best_months: Year-round for game viewing, with the migration passing through from April to June and from October to December.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Seronera Airstrip, then a 40-minute road transfer, or drive four hours from the Ngorongoro Crater main gate.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives for lion, cheetah and leopard, hot-air balloon flights, spa treatments, bush lunches and dinner under the stars.
facts.who_its_for: Families, big cat enthusiasts and travellers wanting a central Serengeti base with strong game viewing in every season.

faqs.q: Where is Nimali Serengeti?
faqs.a: Nimali Serengeti is in the heart of Tanzania's Serengeti National Park, in a new position close to Makoma Hill with uninterrupted views over kopje-dotted plains.

faqs.q: How do I get to Nimali Serengeti?
faqs.a: Fly to Seronera Airstrip, then take a 40-minute road transfer. By road, the lodge is four hours from the Ngorongoro Crater main gate and about two hours from Naabi Hill gate; the eight-hour drive from Arusha is not recommended.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nimali Serengeti?
faqs.a: Game viewing is outstanding all year round. The lodge sits on a wildebeest migration route, with the herds moving through from April to June and from October to December.

faqs.q: How many suites does Nimali Serengeti have?
faqs.a: There are 12 tented suites, two of them connected by a shared walkway for families. Each has a private verandah and an en-suite bathroom with a bathtub and outdoor shower.

faqs.q: Is Nimali Serengeti good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Two suites are linked for families, and Nimali welcomes children. Children under 6 are not allowed on game drives in open vehicles, and children under 12 cannot join walking safaris or bush camping.

faqs.q: What activities does Nimali Serengeti offer?
faqs.a: Morning and afternoon game drives in an area known for lion, cheetah and leopard, plus spa treatments, bush lunches, sundowners and dining under the stars. Nimali also highly recommends a hot-air balloon flight.

stays.name:
Niyama Private Islands 
 Maldives
stays.tagline: Family Tides & Island Vibes – Bond, Explore, Renew.
stays.quote: Here, every sunrise restores, every splash connects, and every moment together transforms.
stays.bestMonths: November–April (dry season); June–September (surf season & lower rates)
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dry season offers calm seas, clear skies, and ideal snorkeling. June–Sept brings Pacific swells, perfect for surf-loving families with quieter islands and cost savings.
stays.airport: Velana International Airport (MLE); domestic seaplane landing on island.
stays.airportDirections: Seaplane from MLE (~40 min) lands directly. Best for families and scenic transfers.
onlyHere: Niyama instead of separating families splits the island: Play is full of active fun, treetop adventures and surf breaks, while Chill offers quiet spa moments and underwater lounges. Ideal for families, multi-gen groups, couples, or solo travelers craving connection in a mindful way. Kids and parents find joy here together, each day seamlessly blending discovery with comfort, laughter with renewal, all within a conservation-minded sanctuary.

why.body: Island Life for Every Generation – Together, Apart, and Across

Niyama’s split-island concept uniquely caters to both family adventure and adult relaxation without compromise. Families can bond over surf lessons, scavenger hunts, and pool parties in Play, while adults retreat to Chill’s spa, yoga, and underwater dining. With a villa host, eco-conscious practices, and seamless services, this stay brings multi-generational groups, active families, honeymooners, and solo travelers into a shared island tapestry, refreshed, connected, and inspired.

stays.name:
No.1 Pery Square 
 Limerick
stays.tagline: Your country house in the city.
stays.quote: Come for the history. Stay for the feeling.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Spring and summer bring some of the property's most evocative experiences to life, from terrace time and spa escapes to the Picnic & Pampering Break. The seasonal experiences are designed around slowing down, enjoying the outdoors and making the most of Limerick's Georgian Quarter.
stays.airportDirections:
Shannon Airport, SNN
Approximately 25 minutes by car.
Limerick Station
Approximately 5 minutes on foot from the hotel.
onlyHere: No. 1 Pery Square is where a city stay takes on the feeling of a country house escape. Georgian architecture, warm hospitality, local produce, fireside afternoons and restorative spa time come together in a house full of personality.

why.title: Find the Soul of Limerick Behind a Georgian Door
why.body: Choose No. 1 Pery Square when you want your Limerick experience to feel intimate, elegant and deeply connected to place.
This is a stay for travelers who appreciate heritage without sacrificing comfort, memorable food rather than anonymous dining, and the freedom to slow down rather than rush through a destination.
Best traveler types:
Family & Generational

pathway.classifiedBy: Claude, delegated by James (Ireland pilot shortlist, 31 Oct 2026)

stays.name: Noah's Forest by Tifakara
stays.tagline: Reconnect with yourself in the rainforest, where river sounds, wildlife and Arenal Volcano create the backdrop.
stays.quote: Reconnect with Yourself!
stays.bestMonthsNote: December through April brings some of the best conditions for discovering La Fortuna, with sunnier days inviting you into the rainforest, toward Arenal Volcano, across hanging bridges and onto the river. It’s an ideal season for balancing adventure with slower moments, soaking in hot springs, wandering through the gardens, or simply listening to the forest come alive around Noah’s Forest.
stays.airport: La Fortuna Airport / Arenal Airport , FON
stays.airportDirections: La Fortuna Airport: about 14 minutes.

items: Adventure Combo: ziplining plus hanging bridges walk
Swimming pool with Arenal Volcano view
Free parking with electric vehicle chargers

onlyHere: At Noah's Forest you can fall asleep to the sounds of the jungle, soak in a private spa overlooking the forest, take a yoga or meditation session by the river and swim with a view of Arenal Volcano, all a short distance from La Fortuna.

why.title: Where the rainforest becomes your retreat
why.body: Noah's Forest is for travellers who want a peaceful rainforest base close to La Fortuna, with adventure by day and a massage, a soak or a quiet dinner at Acacia by night.
Best suited for:
Honeymoon & Couples
Adventure & Nature

facts.best_months: Noah's Forest does not name a best season on its own site; ask James Wild & Co for Arenal timing.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 14 minutes from La Fortuna Airport and 1.3 km north of La Fortuna's park, with free parking and EV chargers.
facts.signature_experiences: Private spa tubs overlooking the forest, riverside yoga, ziplining and hanging bridges, Balsa River rafting and in-room massages.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and adventure-minded travellers wanting a rainforest stay minutes from La Fortuna.

faqs.q: Where is Noah's Forest by Tifakara?
faqs.a: Noah's Forest is 1.3 km north of La Fortuna's park in Alajuela, Costa Rica, about 5 minutes from La Fortuna centre and 20 minutes from Arenal Volcano National Park. The hotel describes itself as an oasis of peace that mixes a central location with rainforest.

faqs.q: How do you get to Noah's Forest by Tifakara?
faqs.a: The nearest airstrip is La Fortuna Airport, about 14 minutes away according to the hotel. Free on-site parking, including electric vehicle chargers, makes arriving by car straightforward.

faqs.q: What rooms does Noah's Forest have?
faqs.a: Riverside Rooms, Garden View Rooms, Quadruple Rooms, Hideaway Villas and a Riverside Family Villa, with deluxe rooms that include a private spa tub overlooking the forest.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Noah's Forest?
faqs.a: The hotel does not name a best season on its own site. Ask James Wild & Co for timing around Arenal's drier and greener months.

faqs.q: What experiences does Noah's Forest offer?
faqs.a: The hotel arranges an Adventure Combo of ziplining with volcano and lake views plus a hanging bridges rainforest walk, a hot springs pass and rafting on the Balsa River. In-room hot stone, deep tissue and couple massages are also available.

faqs.q: Who is Noah's Forest best for?
faqs.a: Couples and active travellers who want a riverside rainforest base close to La Fortuna, with yoga or meditation by the river, a pool with Arenal Volcano views and the Acacia restaurant on site.

stays.name:
Nomad Tanzania 
 Lamai Serengeti
stays.tagline: Where ancient kopjes, endless horizons, and Africa's greatest wildlife spectacle become your front yard.
stays.quote: Some places change how you see the world. Lamai changes how you feel within it.

items: Infinity-style swimming pool overlooking the Serengeti

onlyHere: Built directly into the giant granite boulders of Kogakuria Kopje, Lamai feels inseparable from its surroundings. From your veranda, lions, elephants, wildebeest, and cheetahs move across the plains below. Few camps in Africa combine dramatic scenery, migration access, and authentic safari atmosphere quite like this.

facts.best_months: July to October for Mara River crossings, or December to May for the green season Nomad calls its favourite.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly into the Serengeti to a bush airstrip and transfer to camp, or arrive on a guided driving safari through Northern Tanzania.
facts.signature_experiences: Mara River migration crossings, walking safaris from camp and open-fronted rooms set among the boulders of Kogakuria Kopje.
facts.who_its_for: Families, with dedicated kids' rooms, and groups of friends or large families who want Lamai Private to themselves.

faqs.q: Where is Nomad's Lamai Serengeti?
faqs.a: On Kogakuria Kopje in the northern Serengeti, a rocky outcrop with views for miles. The Mara River is just down the track.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Lamai?
faqs.a: July to October brings the Mara River crossings, when large herds of wildebeest and zebra cross the river. Nomad calls the December to May green season its favourite time of year, and lion, leopard and buffalo are present all year.

faqs.q: How do you get to Lamai?
faqs.a: Fly into the Serengeti and land at a bush airstrip, then transfer to camp. Lamai can also be reached on a guided driving safari through Northern Tanzania.

faqs.q: Is Lamai good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Lamai's kids' rooms have two single beds and an interconnecting bathroom, and Nomad describes Lamai Private as small, intimate and well suited to families.

faqs.q: What is Lamai Private?
faqs.a: Lamai's little sister, a private camp for exclusive use by groups of friends or large families. It has four open-fronted rooms with Serengeti views, its own lounge, a private pool and dedicated staff.

faqs.q: What activities are offered at Lamai?
faqs.a: Game drives, including full-day drives, and bush walks out from the lodge when the grass is short, which Nomad notes is a rare allowance inside a national park. Evenings bring sundowners and dinner under the stars, and there is a pool overlooking the Serengeti.

stays.name: Nômade Temple Holbox
stays.tagline: A wellness retreat on Holbox Island, surrounded by the Yum Balam Nature Reserve.
stays.quote: Beyond a destination, it’s a doorway to slow journeys, whispered rituals, and the unfolding of your own wild heart.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months bring drier weather, lower humidity, gentler seas, and calmer conditions for ocean rituals, kayaking, and bioluminescence viewing. Rainfall is lowest, making outdoor experiences more reliable.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Cancún (CUN), drive 2 to 2.5 hours to Chiquilá port, then about 30 minutes across to Holbox.

items: Jungle Treehouse (7 metres above the ground)
30 rooms across three levels, from earth to sky
Surrounded by the Yum Balam Nature Reserve
Wellness events free for hotel guests
Beach club and pools for guests
La Popular restaurant, fresh Caribbean fish

onlyHere: Nômade Temple Holbox sits on an island where the Caribbean meets the Gulf of Mexico, inside the Yum Balam Nature Reserve. Its 30 rooms climb through three levels of jungle, from canvas-walled Moon Temple rooms to treehouses raised above the ground, and the weekly programme leans into wellness, water and island nature.

why.body: Nômade describes its journey as travel outward and inward: exploring new places and cultures, and making time for self-discovery and healing. On Holbox that means a weekly wellness calendar, water activities and island excursions in a reserve setting, with the hotel welcoming adults only.

facts.how_to_get_there: Fly into Cancún (CUN), drive 2 to 2.5 hours to Chiquilá port, then about 30 minutes across to Holbox. The brand's Path to Holbox offer (4 nights or more) includes one-way transfer for two from CUN, covering the drive to Chiquilá, ferry access and a taxi to the hotel.
facts.signature_experiences: Weekly wellness calendar, sound journeys and massage, water activities, island nature excursions, shared local food experiences, and dining at La Popular.
facts.who_its_for: Adults (18+) seeking wellness programming and island nature.

faqs.q: Where is Nômade Temple Holbox?
faqs.a: On Holbox Island, Mexico, where the Caribbean meets the Gulf of Mexico, surrounded by the Yum Balam Nature Reserve. The address is Calle Caguama, corner of Calle Caracol, Holbox.

faqs.q: How do I get to Nômade Temple Holbox?
faqs.a: Fly into Cancún International Airport (CUN), drive 2 to 2.5 hours to the port of Chiquilá, then allow about 30 minutes to cross to the island. Public parking is available at Chiquilá port.

faqs.q: What rooms does Nômade Temple Holbox have?
faqs.a: There are 30 rooms across three levels: the Moon Temple Room with canvas walls, the Jungle Treehouse raised 7 metres above the ground, the Beachfront Treehouse and the Oceanfront Suite.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Nômade Temple Holbox?
faqs.a: Nômade's FAQ describes Holbox as adults-only, for guests aged 18 and over. The Holbox rooms page also notes that children are not allowed in the Moon Temple Room or the Jungle Treehouse.

faqs.q: What experiences does Nômade Temple Holbox offer?
faqs.a: Wellness programmes, water activities, island nature excursions and shared local food experiences, on a weekly calendar. Wellness events are free for hotel guests, and there is a personal session menu that includes massage and a Lucid Dreaming Sound Journey.

faqs.q: Where do you eat at Nômade Temple Holbox?
faqs.a: La Popular serves fresh fish from the Caribbean. Vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free dishes are on the menus, and most dishes can be adapted for allergies.

faqs.q: Who is Nômade Temple Holbox best for?
faqs.a: Adults looking for a wellness-led island stay in nature. The hotel does not recommend it for wheelchair users or guests with limited mobility because of its wood, sand and concrete construction.

stays.name:
Nomade 
 Temple Ibiza
stays.tagline: “Where the wild heart finds sanctuary on Ibiza’s north shore.”
stays.quote: Step into an experience that dissolves boundaries. Between place and self and leave more alive than when you arrived.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months offer Mediterranean warmth, sunny skies, and open access to the outdoor pool, ritual programming, sea excursions, and cliff hiking. The island is most alive then, but not overly crowded in the shoulder months. The pool is seasonal (open typically April to November)
stays.airportDirections: From Ibiza Airport (IBZ), drive north across the island to Sant Joan de Labritja. It’s approximately a 45–60 minute drive (depending on traffic and route). The drive is scenic: you travel the island’s interior, cross the hills, and descend toward the rugged northern coastline. For travelers seeking smoother logistics, Ibiza Airport is by far the best arrival hub.
onlyHere: At Nômade Temple Ibiza you don’t just stay. You become part of a living, breathing rhythm. Whether you’re a solo traveler seeking creative renewal, a couple longing for deeper connection, or a small group designing a meaningful retreat, here you’ll feel held and invited to explore. The architecture, the programming, and the local engagements are all crafted so that your journey is not just about seeing new lands, but about meeting new parts of yourself.

why.body: You should stay here because it’s rare to find a hotel that balances luxurious comfort, cultural depth, and transformational design. Nômade Temple Ibiza is particularly well suited for creative souls, wellness seekers, couples yearning for soulful escapes, and small groups or retreat organizers. It’s not a mass‑tourism beach resort. It’s a place to slow your tempo, reclaim your senses, and gather in unforgettable rhythms.

stays.name:
Nomade Temple Madrid
Coming 2025
stays.tagline: A sanctuary in the beating heart of Madrid
stays.quote: Lose your map. Let your curiosity lead you through the temple of the city.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months offer milder weather, long daylight hours and vibrant street life. Roof terraces are fully usable, outdoor social programming can run, and art festivals abound across Madrid.
stays.airportDirections:
Drive or taxi: ~25 minutes (approx 8–10 km) depending on traffic.
Public transport: take the metro (Line 8) + transfer(s) or use airport express bus to central stops, then walk or transfer to Gran Vía station , hotel is ~5 minutes walk from Gran Vía metro.
Best option: use MAD → airport metro (Line 8) → transfer to central lines, or airport express bus → central hub → walking.

items: Rooftop sunset views overlooking Gran Vía
Wandering on foot through literary quarters

onlyHere: Step into a refuge of calm just above Madrid’s pulse. Here, guests can spend dawn lingering over coffee, afternoons discovering hidden alley museums, and evenings restored in the spa or rooftop lounge. This is no mere hotel , it’s a creative node in the city’s fabric. For solo wanderers, couples seeking intimacy, or small groups wanting the energy of Madrid as their living room , this is your base to go deeper, slower, and more richly.

why.body: Nomade Temple Madrid is made for travelers who no longer wish to merely visit cities, but to feel them. It’s best for culture‑hungry solo travelers, couples craving quiet luxury steps from the buzz, creative friends plotting their next art walk, and small groups who value both design and awe. Here, you’re not just in Madrid , you’re woven into its stories.

stays.name: Nômade Temple Tulum
stays.tagline: Where the Mayan jungle meets the Caribbean, with wellness at the centre of every day.
stays.quote: In the space between jungle and sea, your spirit finds its compass.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months fall in the dry season, offering more consistent sunshine, lower rainfall, calmer seas, and cooler nights ideal for beach, jungle walks, outdoor wellness, and uninterrupted programming.
stays.airportDirections: Cancún (CUN) is 130 km away, approximately 2 hours by road; the hotel arranges private transport, booked and paid at least 48 hours before arrival.

items: Family rooms and Double Up rooms
Weekly wellbeing programme and spa menu

onlyHere: Nômade Temple Tulum pairs a beachfront setting with a full weekly programme of workshops, ceremonies and gatherings meant to get guests away from their phones and into their bodies. Rooms, suites, treehouses and bungalows sit among the gardens, three restaurants cover seafood, Middle Eastern and omakase, and the hotel welcomes all ages.

why.body: Nômade Temple Tulum suits travellers who want more than a beach bed: breathwork, ice baths, stargazing and yoga, live music through the week and three very different restaurants. Families are welcome, with family rooms and a two-bedroom villa with its own pool.

facts.how_to_get_there: Cancún (CUN) is 130 km, approximately 2 hours by road; private transport can be arranged, requested and paid at least 48 hours before arrival. Address: Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila Km 10.5.
facts.signature_experiences: Clarity Breathwork, Ice Bath, Stargazing and Yogasanas classes; weekly workshops, ceremonies and gatherings; spa; weekly music calendar; La Popular, Macondo and Kuu Jū omakase.
facts.who_its_for: All ages: couples, friends and families who want wellness programming, music and three restaurants on the beach.

faqs.q: Where is Nômade Temple Tulum?
faqs.a: On Tulum Beach in the hotel zone, at Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila Km 10.5. Nômade describes it as blending with the Mayan jungle, near archaeological sites, cenotes and the Sian Ka'an Biosphere.

faqs.q: How do I get to Nômade Temple Tulum?
faqs.a: Cancún International Airport (CUN) is 130 km away, approximately 2 hours by road. The hotel can arrange one-way or round-trip private transport, which must be requested, confirmed and paid at least 48 hours before arrival.

faqs.q: What rooms does Nômade Temple Tulum have?
faqs.a: 38 intimate rooms, 20 exclusive suites, 5 treehouses and 36 bungalows. Room types include the Beachfront Room, Oceanfront Room, Standard, Jungle and Arena rooms, the Double Up room, family rooms and a Two Bedroom Villa with Pool.

faqs.q: Is Nômade Temple Tulum family friendly?
faqs.a: Yes. Nômade says the Tulum hotel welcomes all ages, and it offers family rooms and a Double Up room with two beds.

faqs.q: Where do you eat at Nômade Temple Tulum?
faqs.a: There are three restaurants: La Popular for fresh seafood with a sea view, Macondo for Middle Eastern dishes with a twist, and Kuu Jū, a Japanese omakase restaurant. Vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free dishes are available.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Nômade Temple Tulum?
faqs.a: Signature classes include Clarity Breathwork, Ice Bath, Stargazing and Yogasanas, alongside a weekly programme of workshops, ceremonies and gatherings, a spa menu and a weekly music calendar.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nômade Temple Tulum?
faqs.a: Nômade does not name a best season on its site. Ask James for timing around weather and the hotel's events calendar.

stays.name: North Island Okavango
stays.tagline: Delta island magic, wild and exclusive
stays.quote: Wake to lechwe splashing through water, float down secret channels, and end the day with elephants drinking at sunset. North Island Okavango is where the real Delta spirit lives
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to October for peak flood season, best water safaris, and wildlife concentration. November to April for green season, birds, and fewer guests.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Maun, connect by light aircraft (30 minutes) to North Island airstrip, then short transfer to camp.

paras: Eight spacious tented suites, each with en suite bathroom, outdoor shower, private deck, and endless water or bush views. Main camp with lounge, bar, dining area, fire pit, and a floating plunge pool.
Game drives, mokoro and motorboat excursions, guided island walks, birdwatching, catch-and-release fishing, photographic safaris, and sundowners on the water.
True private island experience in the heart of the Okavango. Abundant wildlife and birdlife. Flexible safaris by water and land. Family-friendly tents. Solar power and eco-sensitive design.

onlyHere: North Island Okavango is perfect for couples, families, honeymooners, and adventurous solo travelers who want wild, private, and water-rich safaris deep in the heart of the Delta.

why.title: Your Private Island in the Delta
why.body: Best for wildlife lovers, water adventure seekers, couples, and families wanting classic Okavango magic, privacy, and close encounters with elephants, hippos, and rare birds.

stays.name: Nyamatusi Camp
stays.tagline: Six tented suites with plunge pools on the Zambezi in Mana Pools
stays.bestMonthsNote: December to April is the green season, with wildflowers, full water sources and newborn wildlife. May to September is the cool, clear Diamond Season. October brings intense heat, drying waterholes and dramatic predator action.

paras: Six luxury tented suites, each with air conditioning, an indoor and outdoor shower, a mini bar, a viewing deck with outdoor seating and a private plunge pool, all looking over the Zambezi River. The main camp has a plunge pool and firepit, a lounge, a dining area and a wine cellar for private dinners.

Walking safaris are the highlight here, tracking wildlife on foot in Mana Pools National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Game drives, canoeing safaris and fishing on the Zambezi, and birding fill the rest of the day, ending with sunset over the river.

Powered entirely by solar energy and built from thatch and indigenous materials, with handwoven lighting and furniture by local artisans. Mana Pools takes its name, meaning four pools, from its four permanent waterholes.

onlyHere: Tracking wildlife on foot along the Zambezi floodplain, then returning to your own plunge pool above the river.

why.title: Mana Pools on Foot
why.body: Best for travellers who want an authentic, uncrowded safari with expert walking guides, including first-time safari-goers who prefer authenticity over crowds.

facts.best_months: May to September for cool, clear dry-season days; October for dramatic predator action.
facts.signature_experiences: Walking safaris, canoeing on the Zambezi and sunsets over the river from camp.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers who want an uncrowded Mana Pools safari with walking at its heart.

faqs.q: Where is Nyamatusi Camp?
faqs.a: In Mana Pools National Park in northern Zimbabwe, a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Zambezi River.

faqs.q: How many suites does Nyamatusi Camp have?
faqs.a: Six luxury tented suites, each with a private plunge pool, air conditioning and views over the Zambezi.

faqs.q: What is Nyamatusi Camp known for?
faqs.a: Walking safaris in Mana Pools, plus game drives, canoeing and fishing on the Zambezi and birding.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Nyamatusi Camp?
faqs.a: May to September is the cool, clear dry season, and October brings the most dramatic predator action as waterholes dry. December to April is green, with newborn wildlife.

faqs.q: Is Nyamatusi Camp good for a first safari?
faqs.a: Yes. African Bush Camps describes it as a strong introduction for travellers who want authenticity over crowds, with expert guiding.

pathway.classifiedBy: James Papagno (Off the Map rule, 1 Nov 2026)

stays.name: Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort
stays.tagline: Canopy villas in a working tea estate on the edge of Nyungwe Forest
stays.airportDirections: Helicopter from Kigali to the resort's helipad (recommended), 35 minutes from One&Only Gorilla's Nest; or a domestic flight, or about 230 km by road.

paras: Canopy villas and treehouses with the forest at eye level: two-bedroom Canopy Villas with wood-burning stoves and forest balconies, and Canopy Treehouses with deep soaking tubs.

Chimpanzee treks. Canopy walks. Guided tea estate walks and a Rwandan tea ceremony. Twilight forest hikes. Birdwatching. Sunrise yoga. Archery above the tea fields. Umuganda community morning on the last Saturday of the month.

In the Gisakura Tea Estate on the edge of Nyungwe National Park, where one of Africa's oldest rainforests meets the tea fields. Dining Room among the tea fields. Tea Lounge and Tea Bar. Forest-view spa with two treatment rooms. Open-air yoga deck over the rainforest. Two experiences a day included.

onlyHere: Formerly One&Only Nyungwe House. Chimpanzees in the rainforest by morning and tea on the estate by afternoon, and the natural second half of a Rwanda journey after the gorillas.

why.title: Primates and Tea
why.body: Best for returning Africa travelers, birders, hikers and couples pairing Nyungwe with Volcanoes National Park.

facts.best_months: The resort does not name a best season; two experiences a day are included and shaped around the weather.
facts.how_to_get_there: By helicopter to the resort's helipad (recommended), 35 minutes from One&Only Gorilla's Nest; or by domestic flight, or about 230 km by road from Kigali International Airport.
facts.signature_experiences: Chimpanzee treks and canopy walks in Nyungwe Forest, with tea ceremonies and walks on the Gisakura Tea Estate.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and travelers aged 15 and over pairing Nyungwe's chimpanzees with Rwanda's gorillas.

faqs.q: Where is Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort?
faqs.a: Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort is in the Gisakura Tea Estate on the edge of Nyungwe National Park, Rwanda, where one of Africa's oldest rainforests meets the tea fields. It is approximately 230 kilometres from Kigali International Airport.

faqs.q: How do you get to Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort?
faqs.a: The recommended way is by helicopter, direct to the resort's own helipad; from One&Only Gorilla's Nest it is 35 minutes by helicopter. The resort can also be reached by domestic flight or by road, and it arranges the journey for you.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: The resort does not name a best season on its own site, so James Wild & Co confirms timing for chimpanzee treks when planning your dates. Every stay includes two experiences a day, chosen by you or shaped around the weather.

faqs.q: What kind of rooms does it have?
faqs.a: Villas and treehouses held in the canopy: Two-Bedroom Canopy Villas with two ensuite bedrooms for up to four, and Canopy Treehouses for two with a deep soaking tub. The resort does not publish a room count.

faqs.q: Are children welcome?
faqs.a: The resort has a minimum age of 15 years, and the spa welcomes guests aged 16 and over. At least one guest aged 18 or over must be present at check-in.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Chimpanzee treks with expert guides, canopy walks, guided walks and a Rwandan tea ceremony on the Gisakura estate, birdwatching for endemic species, archery, sunrise yoga and twilight forest hikes. Two experiences a day are included in every stay.

faqs.q: Who is Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort best for?
faqs.a: Couples and adult travelers pairing chimpanzees and the rainforest with gorilla trekking in Volcanoes National Park, and anyone who wants a forest-view spa and tea estate between treks.

stays.name: Ol Jogi Conservancy - Kenya
stays.tagline: Where privacy, wildlife, and conservation converge in luxury.
stays.quote: Ol Jogi Conservancy: Kenya’s Ultimate Private Safari for Every Generation: "Immerse yourself in a sanctuary where luxury lifestyle, rare wildlife, and meaningful conservation flow together, creating a journey that enriches both traveler and terrain.
stays.bestMonthsNote: June–October offers dry‑season game viewing and rhino spotting; January–March brings lush landscapes, migratory birdlife, and pleasant weather.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Nairobi–Jomo Kenyatta (NBO), then take a private charter or helicopter to Ol Jogi (~60 mi/1 hr). Wilson (WIL) also offers regional flights to Nanyuki airstrip. Charter option delivers dramatic aerial views of Laikipia plains.

items: br/>Lavish communal lounge, bar & dining areas
br/>Spa, gym, steam room and tennis pavilion
br/>Waterhole viewing tunnel right at your doorstep
Morning & evening game drives across 58,000 acres
br/>Guided bush walks and wildlife tracking
br/>Visit to the on‑site vet rescue & rhino sanctuary
br/>Walks with baboons and cheetah enclosures
br/>Helicopter scenic flights over Laikipia plateau
br/>World‑class conservation with rhino & Grevy’s zebra breeding
br/>Tranquil waterhole hide with wildlife viewing
Solar power + electric safari vehicles for low impact
br/>Direct support for local community & conservation projects

onlyHere: Ol Jogi offers an intimate, one‑group‑at‑a‑time retreat that blends flamboyant design and world‑class facilities with purposeful conservation. From sipping sundowners in a sunken waterhole hide to watching orphaned rhino in the veterinary clinic, every moment here is meaningful. This sanctuary is ideal for multi‑gen families, couples seeking romance or solo travelers passionate about wildlife and eco‑impact.

why.title: Privacy & Purpose in the Heart of Laikipia
why.body: Ol Jogi is a haven for conservation‑minded travelers who value exclusivity. Whether you’re a family wanting a wild retreat, a couple celebrating a milestone, or an adventurer craving safari immersion, this is a journey that goes beyond luxury. It leaves a legacy. Best for: Family & Generational, Honeymoon & Couples, Adventure & Nature, Conservation & Eco‑Mindfulness, Solo travelers.

stays.name: Ol Pejeta Bush Camp by Asilia
stays.tagline: Home of the last northern white rhinos, wild Laikipia adventure
stays.quote: Wake to rhinos grazing by the river, track the Big Five, and experience conservation in action at the heart of Ol Pejeta
stays.bestMonths: June to October, January to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October and January to March are dry seasons for easy wildlife viewing and rhino tracking. April, May, and November are green, with fewer visitors and good birding.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Nanyuki Airstrip, 60 to 90 minute road transfer to camp. Charter flights available from Nairobi or Mara.

paras: Seven classic tents, all with en suite bathrooms, hot showers, and private decks overlooking the Ewaso Nyiro River. Family tent available. Main mess tent with lounge, dining, and riverside fire pit.

onlyHere: Ol Pejeta Bush Camp is for wildlife lovers, families, couples, and conservationists seeking immersive safari with rhinos and authentic bush living in a working conservancy.

why.title: Rhinos, Rivers, and Real Safari
why.body: Ol Pejeta Bush Camp is perfect for travelers passionate about wildlife conservation, rhino tracking, and hands-on safari experiences. Best for families, couples, solo travelers, and photographers.

stays.name: Olas Tulum
stays.tagline: An intimate beachfront guesthouse on the edge of Sian Ka'an.
stays.quote: Wake to the sound of the waves and discover a slower way to travel.
stays.bestMonthsNote: The ideal time to visit Olas Tulum is during the dry season from November through May, when warm temperatures, gentle Caribbean breezes and abundant sunshine create perfect conditions for beach relaxation, swimming, cycling, outdoor dining and exploring Tulum's nearby cenotes and archaeological sites.
stays.airport: Tulum International Airport (TQO) Cancún International Airport (CUN)
stays.airportDirections:
Tulum International Airport (TQO)
Approximately 47 km
Around 50 minutes by car
Closest international airport
Cancún International Airport (CUN)
Approximately 122 km
Around 2 hours by car
Largest international gateway to the Riviera Maya
Recommended Arrival Airport: Tulum International Airport (TQO)

items: Intimate boutique hotel and guesthouse on the beach

onlyHere: Olas is a small guesthouse in the dunes at the edge of the jungle, run entirely on solar power and cooled by the sea breeze rather than air conditioning. Breakfast is shared around one table in the sand, and Sian Ka'an begins next door.

why.title: A solar-powered guesthouse beside Sian Ka'an
why.body: Olas suits travellers who want a quiet beach, a small number of suites and a team that has lived in the area for 20 years. Mornings start in the Sky Yoga Shala or on the sand, and the team can arrange Sian Ka'an, cenotes and turtle nesting. The whole property can also be rented for a group.

facts.best_months: Year-round warmth around 26C; rainy season June to October; turtle nesting May to October.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly into Tulum (TQO, about 1 hour) or Cancún (CUN, about 1.75 hours). Private transfers with 72 hours' notice, or rent a car. Address: 10.6 Boca Paila Road.
facts.signature_experiences: Sunset rooftop lounge, Sky Yoga Shala, massage, Sian Ka'an by kayak or birdwatching tour, cenotes, turtle nesting May to October.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, friends and families with children over five who want a small, solar-powered beachfront guesthouse next to Sian Ka'an; the whole property can be rented by a large party.

faqs.q: Where is Olas Tulum?
faqs.a: On the beach at 10.6 Boca Paila Road, Tulum, 14 km from the centre of Tulum Pueblo. It neighbours the Sian Ka'an reserve, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

faqs.q: How do I get to Olas Tulum?
faqs.a: Fly into Tulum (TQO) or Cancún (CUN). Olas says the drive is about 1 hour from TQO and 1.75 hours from Cancún; its team arranges private transfers with 72 hours' notice, and renting a car is also recommended.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Olas Tulum?
faqs.a: Olas gives a year-round temperature of around 26C, up to 32C in summer, with the rainy season from June to October. Turtle nesting season runs May to October.

faqs.q: What suites does Olas Tulum have?
faqs.a: The Oceanfront Villa holds the Oceanfront Master Suite, Oceanfront Junior Suite, Oceanfront Suite and Oceanfront Balcony Suite. The Oceanview Villa, about 20 metres back, has three suites including the Oceanview Deluxe Balcony and the Oceanview Balcony Suites.

faqs.q: Are children welcome at Olas Tulum?
faqs.a: Yes, children over five years old are welcome.

faqs.q: Does Olas Tulum have air conditioning?
faqs.a: No. Olas is 100% solar powered and its suites are designed for the sea breeze, with palapa roofs, ocean-facing rooms and floor fans.

faqs.q: What experiences does Olas Tulum offer?
faqs.a: A rooftop lounge above the jungle canopy, the Sky Yoga Shala with private classes, and massage in your suite or under the palms. The team arranges Sian Ka'an kayak or birdwatching trips, cenote visits with guides, and turtle nesting in season.

stays.name: Oliver’s Camp by Asilia
stays.tagline: Tarangire’s walking safari camp, wild and authentic
stays.quote: Wake to elephant herds passing by, explore on foot with expert guides, and experience classic adventure in the wild heart of Tarangire
stays.bestMonthsNote: Best in the dry season; the camp closes from mid-March to mid-May.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Kuro Airstrip, about 1 hour drive to camp.

paras: Fifteen tents in two wings of five and ten, including two family tents and a honeymoon tent, each with en suite bathroom, indoor and outdoor showers, and private deck with sweeping bush views. Each wing has a lounge and dining room overlooking the Tarangire River floodplains, with a cocktail bar and pool deck between them. Evening campfire.

onlyHere: Oliver’s Camp is for real adventurers, couples, families, and solo travelers looking for wild landscapes, elephants, and exciting walking safaris in a secluded, untamed corner of Tarangire.

why.title: Walk on the Wild Side
why.body: Oliver’s is perfect for travelers wanting classic safari, walking adventures, and Tarangire’s large elephant herds. Best for couples, families, solo explorers, and anyone who loves nature up close.

facts.best_months: Open mid-May to mid-March, with September and October best for wildlife with fewer visitors and November to February for photography and birding.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Kuro airstrip in Tarangire, then drive about an hour to camp.
facts.signature_experiences: Walking safaris, night game drives, sunrise balloon safaris and game viewing around the Silale Swamp's elephant and buffalo herds.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers wanting walking safaris away from day-trip traffic, including honeymooners and families with children over five.

faqs.q: Where is Oliver's Camp?
faqs.a: Oliver's Camp is in a remote southeastern area of Tarangire National Park, Tanzania, about 3 hours south of the entrance gate. It sits close to the Silale Swamp, which Asilia calls the park's best game viewing area.

faqs.q: How do I get to Oliver's Camp?
faqs.a: Fly to Kuro airstrip, approximately an hour's drive from camp.

faqs.q: When is Oliver's Camp open, and when should I go?
faqs.a: The camp is open mid-May to mid-March and closes for the rains from mid-March to mid-May. Asilia recommends September and October for great wildlife with fewer visitors, and November to February for photography and birding.

faqs.q: How many tents does Oliver's Camp have?
faqs.a: There are 15 tents in two wings of five and ten, including 2 family tents and 1 honeymoon tent. Each tent has an en suite bathroom with indoor and outdoor showers and a private deck.

faqs.q: Does Oliver's Camp allow children?
faqs.a: Yes, children over the age of five are welcome, and there are two family tents. The minimum age for walking safaris is 12.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Oliver's Camp?
faqs.a: Walking safaris with an armed ranger, night game drives and twice daily game drives, with the option of a sunrise hot-air balloon safari over the Tarangire plains. Walking runs 1 June to 15 February, subject to weather.

stays.name: One&Only Gorilla's Nest
stays.tagline: Treehouses in the eucalyptus on the edge of Volcanoes National Park
stays.airportDirections: A 25-minute helicopter flight from Kigali International Airport (recommended), or about 2.5 hours by road.

paras: Treehouses and suites suspended amid the eucalyptus: Forest Treehouses with a fireplace, soaking tub, outdoor shower and private deck; two-bedroom Susa Treehouses with a fireplace; the Virunga Suite with an open-air bathtub; the Ingagi Suite with an alfresco bath and spacious deck; and the Silverback Suite with its own private pool and firepit.

Gorilla treks in Volcanoes National Park. Stories of Your Ancestors, a fireside briefing on the 12 gorilla families. The Secrets of Rwandan Coffee. Iby'iwacu Cultural Village. Rhythms of Rwanda drumming and dance at the boma. Handspun Hope, a working farm supporting local women. Archery. Guided nature walks for birds and butterflies.

In the Virunga foothills near Kinigi, on the edge of Volcanoes National Park. The Nest restaurant. One&Only Spa. Heated infinity pool. Club One open-air fitness centre and yoga pavilion. Boma and coffee garden. Jack Hanna Cottage with games room and library.

onlyHere: Gorilla's Nest puts you on the edge of Volcanoes National Park, with a forest treehouse, a fire and a deep bath waiting when you come down from the mountain.

why.title: Gorillas in Comfort
why.body: Best for couples and travelers aged 15 and over pairing gorilla trekking with a Rwanda or East Africa safari.

facts.best_months: One&Only does not name a best season; James Wild & Co confirms gorilla trekking dates when planning.
facts.how_to_get_there: A 25-minute helicopter flight from Kigali International Airport (recommended), or a 2.5-hour drive.
facts.signature_experiences: Guided gorilla treks after a fireside briefing on the park's 12 gorilla families, plus Rwandan coffee tastings and the One&Only Spa.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and travelers aged 15 and over who want gorilla trekking with spa, culture and treehouse comfort.

faqs.q: Where is One&Only Gorilla's Nest?
faqs.a: One&Only Gorilla's Nest is in the foothills of Volcanoes National Park near Kinigi and Musanze, Rwanda, with individual treehouses and suites among eucalyptus trees on the edge of the park.

faqs.q: How do you get to One&Only Gorilla's Nest?
faqs.a: The recommended way is a 25-minute chartered helicopter flight from Kigali International Airport; by road it is a 2.5-hour drive by SUV. Nyungwe Tea Forest Resort is 35 minutes away by helicopter.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: One&Only does not name a best season on its own site, so James Wild & Co confirms trekking dates when planning your stay. Volcanoes National Park is home to 12 families of endangered mountain gorillas.

faqs.q: What rooms does One&Only Gorilla's Nest have?
faqs.a: Treehouses and suites: Forest Treehouses for two, two-bedroom Susa Treehouses for up to three, and the Virunga, Ingagi and Silverback Suites for two, the Silverback with its own private pool. One&Only does not publish a total room count.

faqs.q: Are children welcome?
faqs.a: The resort has a minimum age of 15 years, and at least one guest aged 18 or over must be present at check-in. Rollaway beds are not available.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Guided gorilla treks, prepared for at Stories of Your Ancestors, a fireside gathering on the park's 12 gorilla families. Guests can also join The Secrets of Rwandan Coffee, visit Iby'iwacu Cultural Village and Handspun Hope, and unwind at the One&Only Spa and heated infinity pool.

faqs.q: Who is One&Only Gorilla's Nest best for?
faqs.a: Couples and adult travelers aged 15 and over who want gorilla trekking with spa time, cultural experiences and a treehouse to return to, and those pairing it with Nyungwe by helicopter.

stays.name: Open Sky Zion
stays.tagline: Luxury beneath the vast desert sky.
stays.quote: The greatest luxury is having enough space to hear yourself think.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Spring and fall provide ideal temperatures for hiking, outdoor wellness experiences, photography, and exploring Zion National Park. Cooler weather enhances comfort while preserving the dramatic beauty of the surrounding desert landscapes.
stays.airport: St. George Regional Airport (SGU) Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC)
stays.airportDirections:
Nearest Airport: St. George Regional Airport (SGU)
Approximate Travel Times:
SGU → Open Sky: 45–60 minutes drive
LAS → Open Sky: approximately 2.5 hours drive
SLC → Open Sky: approximately 4.5 hours drive
onlyHere: Open Sky offers something increasingly rare in modern travel, silence, space, and perspective. Surrounded by Utah's vast desert landscapes, guests experience luxury not through excess, but through meaningful connection with nature and the rhythms of the Southwest.

stays.name: Pacuare Lodge
stays.tagline: Wild Luxury by the River
stays.quote: Float in by raft, wake to toucans, and discover adventure, romance, and rainforest magic along Costa Rica’s legendary river.
stays.bestMonths: December to April and June to August
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dry season is ideal for rafting, wildlife, and hiking; green season is quieter with lush forest and higher river flows.
stays.airportDirections: 2.5 to 3 hrs from San José to the river, then raft or 4x4 (about 45 min).

paras: Twenty bungalows within a 340-hectare protected area, spring-fed stone plunge pools in the Linda Vista and Canopy Villas and a private pool at the Jaguar Villa, open-air heated showers, river or rainforest views, a la carte meals, a spa, a private suspension bridge to a treetop platform at the Canopy Villa, and bilingual guides certified in swiftwater rescue.

onlyHere: Pacuare Lodge suits adventurous couples, families with children 7 and over and anyone who wants deep rainforest. Arriving by whitewater raft on the Pacuare River is part of the stay, and the lodge supports rainforest conservation and the local Cabecar community.

why.title: Costa Rica's Hidden River Paradise
why.body: Stay for whitewater rafting, rainforest immersion, eco-elegant suites and villas, and eight included experiences, ideal for couples, families with children 7 and over, groups and travelers with a spirit for adventure.

facts.best_months: December to April and June to August are peak seasons, with higher river levels from September to November.
facts.how_to_get_there: Transfer 2.5 to 3 hours from San José to the Pacuare River, then arrive by whitewater raft or a 45-minute 4x4 ride.
facts.signature_experiences: Whitewater rafting plus eight included experiences such as the Canopy Tour, Tropical Canyoning and the Cabecar Indigenous Hike.
facts.who_its_for: Adventurous couples, honeymooners and families with children 7 and over.

faqs.q: Where is Pacuare Lodge?
faqs.a: Pacuare Lodge sits beside the Pacuare River near Siquirres, on the Caribbean slope of Costa Rica's Talamanca range, with 20 bungalows inside a 340-hectare protected area. It is not directly accessible by car or public transport.

faqs.q: How do you get to Pacuare Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge collects guests from San José hotels around 6 am for a 2.5 to 3 hour drive to the river, then guests arrive by whitewater raft or by 4x4 (about 45 minutes). Self-drivers can meet the team at its warehouse in Siquirres; the nearest international airport is San José (SJO).

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Pacuare Lodge?
faqs.a: The lodge is open year round; peak seasons are December to April (dry season) and June to August. River levels are higher in the rainy season, especially September to November, and late April to early June or September to late November offer more availability.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Pacuare Lodge have?
faqs.a: There are 20 bungalows: seven Garden Suites, River View Suites, Linda Vista Villas and Canopy Villas with spring-fed stone plunge pools, and the Jaguar Villa, the most luxurious, with a private spring-fed pool beside the river.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Pacuare Lodge?
faqs.a: Yes, from age 7. Rafting has its own minimums (9 to raft in and 12 to raft out), so younger children reach the lodge by ground transport.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Pacuare Lodge?
faqs.a: Arriving by whitewater raft, plus eight included experiences: Canopy Tour, Tropical Canyoning, Bird-Watching, Cabecar Indigenous Hike, Ancient Trail and Hidden Waterfall Hike, Rural Experience, The Loop and the Sustainability Tour.

faqs.q: Who is Pacuare Lodge best for?
faqs.a: Adventurous couples, honeymooners and families with children 7 and over. The lodge also offers honeymoon and exclusive-use packages.

stays.name: Paws Up Resort
stays.tagline: “Where Big Sky Meets Bespoke Wilderness”
stays.quote: Step off the map. Breathe deep. Let the land guide you home.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Summer (June–September) delivers long daylight, warm weather, river and hiking adventures, and full activity menus. In winter months (Dec–Feb), the land becomes a snowy playground. Cross‑country skiing, snowshoeing, sleigh rides, and cozy fireside rituals. Shoulder seasons may see limited services or weather variability.
stays.airportDirections: The resort is about a 35‑minute drive (or ≈ 35 mi northeast) from Missoula International Airport. Transfers to/from MSO are included in most home or tent bookings.

paras: Luxury Homes: Meadow Homes, Big Timber, Wilderness Estates, Historic Homes.  Safari‑Style Tents: multiple camps (Creekside, Cliffside, River Camp, etc.).  Green O Housings: modern forest hauses in adults-only enclave.

items: Fly fishing & river excursions on the Blackfoot
Guided hikes, wildlife tracking, mountain biking
Spa & wellness, forest bathing, sound healing
Winter sports: snowshoeing, sledding, cross‑country skiing
Cultural excursions: ghost town tours, ranch immersion
On‑property transport and vehicles per home
100+ miles of trails and 10 miles of Blackfoot River
Family & kids programs (Kids Corps of Discovery)

onlyHere: This is for travelers who want more than a place to stay. They want to live a rich, slow moment in the land. Whether you’re traveling with family, as a couple, solo, or in a small group, Paws Up offers sanctuary to disconnect, roam, and be wholly present.

why.body: Paws Up is a working ranch turned immersive retreat, where your stay becomes part of the landscape. Ideal for couples, families, solo travelers, or small groups, every experience is tailored and rooted in nature.

stays.name:
Pearl Resort 
 Le Borabora
stays.tagline: An iconic Bora Bora escape where Polynesian authenticity meets legendary lagoon luxury.
stays.quote: Some destinations exceed expectations. Bora Bora redefines them.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months typically provide sunny days, lower humidity, calm lagoon conditions, and exceptional visibility for snorkeling, boating, and exploring Bora Bora's natural beauty.
stays.airport: Bora Bora Airport (BOB) Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT)
stays.airportDirections: Guests arrive via Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT), connect to Bora Bora Airport (BOB), and then take a short resort boat transfer directly to Motu Tevairoa.
onlyHere: Le Bora Bora occupies one of the most spectacular settings in the South Pacific. Positioned on a secluded private motu and surrounded by Bora Bora's famous turquoise lagoon, the resort combines luxury, culture, and nature into one of the world's most sought-after island experiences. Every moment here is framed by water, mountains, and endless horizons.

stays.name:
Pearl Resort 
 Le Nuku Hiva
stays.tagline: Discover the untamed heart of French Polynesia in the legendary Marquesas Islands.
stays.quote: Adventure begins where the familiar ends.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months generally provide warm temperatures, comfortable humidity, ideal hiking conditions, and excellent opportunities for cultural exploration and outdoor adventures throughout the Marquesas.
stays.airport: Nuku Hiva Airport (NHV) Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT)
stays.airportDirections: Guests typically arrive via PPT (Tahiti) and connect to NHV (Nuku Hiva Airport). The resort is located approximately 40–50 minutes by vehicle from the airport overlooking Taiohae Bay.
onlyHere: Le Nuku Hiva offers an experience unlike anywhere else in French Polynesia. Far removed from the overwater resorts of the Society Islands, this destination reveals a landscape of towering cliffs, deep valleys, ancient traditions, and untamed beauty. It is a place where adventure and culture are inseparable.

stays.name:
Pearl Resort 
 Le Tahiti
stays.tagline: Discover the island where authentic Tahitian culture meets oceanfront luxury.
stays.quote: Sometimes the most unforgettable island experience begins before the journey even continues.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months generally offer pleasant temperatures, lower rainfall, excellent sightseeing conditions, comfortable beach weather, and ideal opportunities for exploring Tahiti's cultural and natural attractions.
stays.airportDirections: Approximately 20 minutes by vehicle from Tahiti Faa'a International Airport. The resort is also located approximately 10 minutes from downtown Papeete.

items: Ocean View Room with Hot Tub
Views across Matavai Bay to Moorea

onlyHere: Le Tahiti offers something few South Pacific resorts can claim: a dramatic black sand beach framed by lush mountains and endless ocean views. Here, travelers experience authentic Tahiti rather than simply passing through it. Every day begins with sunrise over Matavai Bay and ends with the colors of Moorea fading into the horizon.

stays.name:
Pearl Resort 
 Le Tikehau
stays.tagline: Discover one of French Polynesia's most secluded island escapes, surrounded by a world-famous lagoon.
stays.quote: The further you travel, the more extraordinary simplicity becomes.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months generally provide warm temperatures, lower humidity, calmer seas, excellent snorkeling visibility, and ideal conditions for exploring the atoll and marine ecosystem.
stays.airport: Tikehau Airport (TIH) Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT)
stays.airportDirections: Guests typically arrive via PPT (Tahiti) before connecting to TIH (Tikehau Airport). The resort is then reached by a short boat transfer from the airport to the private motu.
onlyHere: Few destinations in the world feel as remote and untouched as Tikehau. Set on a tiny private motu surrounded by a vast turquoise lagoon, Le Tikehau delivers an authentic castaway experience elevated by luxury hospitality. Here, nature remains the main attraction, and every day is shaped by the rhythm of the ocean.

stays.name:
Pearl Resort 
 Vahine Private Island
stays.tagline: A hidden private island sanctuary where simplicity and luxury exist in perfect balance.
stays.quote: Luxury isn't about having more. It's about needing less.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months generally offer calm lagoon conditions, warm temperatures, excellent snorkeling visibility, lower rainfall, and ideal weather for enjoying the private island environment and outdoor activities.
stays.airport: Raiatea Airport (RFP) Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT)
stays.airportDirections: Guests arrive via Tahiti Faa'a International Airport (PPT), connect to Raiatea Airport (RFP), and continue by boat transfer to Vahine Island. Total transfer from Raiatea typically takes approximately 35–45 minutes depending on sea conditions.

items: Coral reef access directly from the island

stays.bestMonthsNote: Description: Cool, dry season best for wildlife, walks, cheetah tracking, and clear Karoo skies; summer is green and beautiful, ideal for birding.
stays.airportDirections: Scheduled flights to Port Elizabeth, then 3-hour road transfer; private charter to Graaff-Reinet Airstrip, 40-minute transfer to lodge.

paras: Intimate lodges and villas set on a vast, restored wilderness. Cheetah tracking and hands-on conservation. Pools and outdoor dining. Flexible family-friendly accommodation. All-inclusive, locally sourced cuisine. Solar-powered and rewilding-focused.

onlyHere: Samara is ideal for families, couples, friends, conservationists, and solo adventurers seeking something beyond a typical safari, rewilded landscapes, personal service, and experiences that restore soul and land.

why.title: Rediscover Wild Karoo Magic
why.body: Stay at Samara for close-up cheetah tracking, epic landscapes, meaningful conservation, and the warmth of a family-owned reserve. Perfect for families, couples, and anyone passionate about rewilding and new African adventures.

facts.best_months: April to October, the cool, dry season, for wildlife, walks and cheetah tracking.
facts.how_to_get_there: Scheduled flights to Port Elizabeth (PLZ), then a 3-hour road transfer, or a private charter to Graaff-Reinet Airstrip and a 40-minute transfer.
facts.who_its_for: Families, couples, friends, conservationists and solo adventurers who want something beyond a typical safari.
facts.signature_experiences: Cheetah tracking on foot, star beds and conservation activities.

faqs.q: Where is Samara Karoo Reserve?
faqs.a: Samara is near Graaff-Reinet in the Eastern Cape, on a vast, restored Karoo wilderness.

faqs.q: What makes Samara different?
faqs.a: You can track cheetah on foot and take part in hands-on conservation on rewilded land. The reserve is family-owned and solar-powered.

faqs.q: How do you get to Samara Karoo Reserve?
faqs.a: Fly to Port Elizabeth International (PLZ), then a 3-hour road transfer. Or take a private charter to Graaff-Reinet Airstrip, 40 minutes from the lodge.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Samara?
faqs.a: April to October. The cool, dry season is best for wildlife, walks, cheetah tracking and clear Karoo skies. Summer is green and good for birding.

faqs.q: Is Samara good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. It offers family safaris, kids' activities and flexible family-friendly accommodation.

stays.name: San Camp
stays.tagline: Seven white tents on the edge of Ntwetwe Pan

paras: Seven classic white tents with four-poster beds, Persian rugs, mahogany writing desks and leather armchairs, each with a day bed outside and views across the salt pans.

Time with a habituated meerkat colony. Quad biking across the pans. Walks with Zu/'hoasi Bushmen. Horseback riding, helicopter flights, game drives and night drives. Flamingos on the pans in March and April.

On the edge of Ntwetwe Pan in the Makgadikgadi, adjoining Makgadikgadi National Park, and one of only three camps in a 400,000-hectare concession. Open-sided pavilions, a tea tent, a pool tent and communal dining. Solar powered. Open mid-April to mid-October.

onlyHere: Lying out on the salt pans to count the stars from one horizon to the other, with meerkats for company in the morning.

why.title: Desert Space and Silence
why.body: Best for couples, solo travellers, photographers and returning safari-goers.

stays.name: Saruni Eagle View
stays.tagline: Panoramic views, wild adventure, Naboisho at its wildest
stays.quote: Watch herds from above, walk with Maasai guides, and sleep to the music of the Mara at a true eagle’s nest above the plains
stays.bestMonths: June to October, January to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October for the Great Migration and high wildlife density. January to March for quiet bush, abundant predators, and birding.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Ol Seki Airstrip, 20-minute game drive to camp, Saruni Eagle View team will greet you.

paras: Nine elevated tented suites with panoramic private verandas, full en suite bathrooms, open-air showers, and breathtaking savannah views. Main area with dining deck, lounge, fire pit, and an observation terrace for epic wildlife watching.

items: Elevated tents with wide open views
Intimate, wildlife-rich setting in Naboisho Conservancy

onlyHere: Saruni Eagle View is for couples, solo travelers, families, and anyone who wants stunning views, close-up wildlife action, and immersive Maasai-guided adventure. Perfect for photographers, birders, and true nature lovers.

why.title: See the Mara from Above
why.body: Best for wildlife enthusiasts, couples, families, and solo explorers who want amazing views, active safaris, and real connection to local culture and conservation.

stays.name: Saruni Leopard Hill
stays.tagline: Sleep under the sky, live among leopards, wild Naboisho calls
stays.quote: Watch the sunrise through your tent’s open roof, walk wild with Maasai, and relax in the heart of big cat country
stays.bestMonths: June to October, January to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October for big cats, migration, and cool dry weather. January to March for green plains, birdlife, and fewer crowds.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Ol Seki Airstrip, 25-minute game drive to camp, Saruni Leopard Hill team will greet you.

paras: Six luxury “star” tents including four double tents, one honeymoon tent, and one family tent, each with retractable roof, private deck, en suite bathroom, outdoor shower, and dramatic views of the savannah. Main area with fire pit, lounge, dining deck, yoga platform, and library.

items: Innovative star tents with open roof and sky views
Direct access to wildlife-rich plains and waterholes

onlyHere: Saruni Leopard Hill is for couples, honeymooners, families, and solo travelers who want a unique safari with a blend of luxury, wilderness, and wellness. Perfect for big cat fans, adventure seekers, and those craving connection to nature and culture.

why.title: Sleep Beneath the Stars
why.body: Ideal for couples, solo explorers, and families who want comfort, wildlife, wellness, and cultural connection in one of Africa’s wildest landscapes.

stays.name: Saruni Samburu Lodge
stays.tagline: Wild luxury atop the rocks, Samburu’s untamed beauty in every direction
stays.quote: Rise above the plains in a spectacular cliff-top villa, explore Samburu with expert guides, and experience true freedom with breathtaking views
stays.bestMonths: June to October, December to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October and December to March for dry weather, best wildlife sightings, and clear views.
stays.airport: Samburu Kalama Airstrip (KLB) or Samburu Oryx Airstrip (ORX)
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Samburu Kalama Airstrip, 30-minute scenic drive to lodge, Saruni Samburu team will greet you.

paras: Six open-fronted villas including family, single, and honeymoon villas, all with panoramic views, private verandas, outdoor showers, and spacious lounge areas. Main lodge offers infinity pools, open dining, lounge, library, and spa.

items: Private game drives in Samburu and Kalama Conservancies

paras: Spectacular villas with cliff-top views. Private guide and vehicle for each booking. Infinity pools. Samburu Wellbeing Space spa. Outdoor dining and sundowners. Family-friendly, exclusive, and deeply connected to local culture.

onlyHere: Saruni Samburu is for couples, honeymooners, families, and solo travelers who want next-level privacy, dramatic scenery, and deep cultural immersion in northern Kenya’s wildest region. Every stay supports conservation and local communities.

why.title: Luxury Among the Rocks
why.body: Ideal for adventurous couples, families, and solo travelers who want space, dramatic scenery, and a personal safari experience with a strong focus on conservation and community.

stays.name: Saruni Wild Lodge
stays.tagline: Remote, intimate, wild. Masai Mara as it should be
stays.quote: Wake to the sounds of the bush, track wildlife on foot or by vehicle, and fall asleep to the night chorus in a truly wild setting
stays.bestMonths: June to October, January to March
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October for Great Migration and wildlife action, January to March for fewer crowds, lush scenery, and baby animals.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Mara North Airstrip, 45-minute drive to camp, Saruni Wild team will greet you.

paras: Three elegant tented suites, including one family tent and two double tents, all with en suite bathrooms, hot showers, open views, and a blend of classic safari style and modern comfort. Shared dining, lounge, and fire pit in an intimate bush camp setting.

items: Ultra-intimate camp with only three tents

onlyHere: Saruni Wild Lodge is ideal for couples, solo explorers, small families, and true safari lovers who want an exclusive, authentic, and adventurous stay in the heart of the Mara North Conservancy. Unplugged luxury and a deep connection to nature.

why.title: Intimate Wilderness, Wild Adventure
why.body: Perfect for couples, honeymooners, and families seeking privacy, adventure, and deep immersion in untamed nature. Amazing for solo travelers wanting authentic safari and meaningful local connection.

stays.name:
Sasaab Lodge 
 Northern Kenya

stays.quote: Where the wild Samburu lands meet Moroccan-inspired design, Sasaab offers a soulful blend of adventure, luxury, and total relaxation.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dry season is best for wildlife and clear skies; the green season offers dramatic scenery and fewer guests.
