stays.airportDirections: Fly to Samburu or Sasaab Airstrip (private charter), 20–40 minute road transfer to lodge.

items: Sweeping views over the Ewaso Nyiro River
Private plunge pools in every suite
On-site cultural experiences with Samburu warriors

onlyHere: Sasaab is ideal for couples, families, groups, and anyone who wants big sky safari and desert style in one of Kenya’s wildest landscapes. Find rest, adventure, and real connection in a lodge built for both luxury and soul.

why.title: Desert Dreams, River Life
why.body: Sasaab is where Moroccan-inspired comfort meets Samburu adventure. From game drives to camel rides, river views to wellness retreats, it’s perfect for families, couples, solo travelers, and anyone seeking an unforgettable, restorative safari.

stays.name: Saseka Tented Camp
stays.bestMonthsNote: Thornybush's dry winter: thinner bush and animals at permanent water.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Hoedspruit from Johannesburg or Cape Town, then about 45 minutes by road.

stays.name: Sashwa River of Stars
stays.tagline: Twelve suites on the banks of the Olifants River in the Greater Kruger, with plant-based food and holistic wellness.
stays.bestMonthsNote: The dry season in the Greater Kruger: thinner bush and animals drawn to the Olifants River. October to April is the green, wet season.
stays.airportDirections: Fly into Hoedspruit Eastgate (HDS) from Johannesburg or Cape Town, then a pre-arranged road transfer of about 1 hour 15 to 1 hour 20 minutes.

why.title: Place
why.body: The Olifants River cuts through the Greater Kruger, and Sashwa's twelve suites sit on its upper bank, looking down at the water where elephants and hippos come to drink.

why.title: People
why.body: A safari lodge built around holistic wellness: yoga on the riverbank, meditation, and a kitchen that cooks only plants.

why.title: Impact
why.body: The lodge describes a philanthropy-led model; nothing is claimed here until we have read the detail.

why.title: James' note
why.body: I haven't been yet. A plant-based safari sounds like a contradiction until you remember the elephants have been doing it for millions of years. Give it five nights, not three.

facts.best_months: May to September, the dry season; October to April is the green, wet season.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Hoedspruit Eastgate (HDS), then about 1 hour 15 minutes by road to the lodge on the Olifants River. Minimum stay three nights; five or more is better.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives and dawn bush walks; elephants, hippos and lions from the decks; yoga on the riverbank; three plant-based meals a day; the Milky Way at night.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, solo travellers and small groups who want a safari with yoga, meditation and a plant-based kitchen. Children over 16, or any age on an exclusive booking.

pathway.classifiedBy: James Papagno (batch 3, drafted by Iggi; PATH-05 added in Stage 4, 1 Nov 2026)

stays.name: Sausage Tree Camp
stays.tagline: Private guiding and plunge pools on the Lower Zambezi
stays.bestMonthsNote: Fishing is best September to December.
stays.airportDirections: Light-aircraft transfer flights into the Lower Zambezi.

paras: Seven tented suites and the Kigelia House for four, each with its own plunge pool and Zambezi view. The whole camp can be booked privately.

items: Private game drives day and night
Boat safaris and canoeing through Zambezi channels

paras: Established in 1996 in Lower Zambezi National Park as a luxury bush camp. Guaranteed private guiding with private vehicles, boats and canoes. Butlers, known as Muchindas.

onlyHere: Sausage Tree is privacy as a promise: your own guide, vehicle and boat, a plunge pool on the Zambezi and a camp founded in 1996 and rebuilt in its entirety in 2018.

why.title: Privately Guided
why.body: Best for couples, families with children over eight and groups who want the whole experience to themselves.

facts.best_months: Open 1 April to 30 November, with fishing best September to December.
facts.how_to_get_there: A transfer flight into Lower Zambezi National Park.
facts.signature_experiences: Guaranteed private guiding by vehicle, boat and canoe, with a plunge pool at every suite.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, families with children over eight and private groups.

faqs.q: Where is Sausage Tree Camp?
faqs.a: Sausage Tree is on the banks of the Zambezi River inside Lower Zambezi National Park, Zambia, a protected area of 4,092 km2.

faqs.q: How do you get to Sausage Tree Camp?
faqs.a: Guests take a transfer flight into the Lower Zambezi; ask your travel designer for routing. The camp sits on the river, and activities run by vehicle, on foot, by boat and by canoe.

faqs.q: When is Sausage Tree Camp open?
faqs.a: The camp is open from 1 April to 30 November. Green Safaris says fishing is good all year, with September to December the best time.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Sausage Tree have?
faqs.a: Seven tented luxury suites and the Kigelia House for four guests, each with its own plunge pool and Zambezi view. The whole camp can be booked privately.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Sausage Tree?
faqs.a: Yes, for families with children above eight years old.

faqs.q: What makes Sausage Tree different?
faqs.a: Every stay includes guaranteed private guiding, meaning your own vehicle, boat and canoe trips, plus butlers known as Muchindas. Day and night drives, walking safaris, canoeing, catch-and-release fishing and river lunches are included.

faqs.q: Who is Sausage Tree best for?
faqs.a: Couples, families with children over eight and groups who want the whole camp to themselves.

stays.name: Sayari Camp by Asilia
stays.tagline: Front row for river crossings, contemporary Serengeti luxury
stays.quote: Wake to the sound of wildebeest at the Mara River, enjoy contemporary comfort, and experience the best of the northern Serengeti
stays.bestMonthsNote: The camp closes in April and May.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Kogatende Airstrip, 20 minute drive to camp.

paras: Fifteen tented suites, including two family tents and a honeymoon tent, each with en suite bathroom, walk-in shower, free standing tub, private outdoor shower, and wraparound veranda overlooking the plains. Main area with pool, spa, and bar. Two Retreats with a dedicated chef, guide, and private vehicle for families and groups.

items: Closest permanent camp to the Mara River

onlyHere: Sayari is for discerning travelers, couples, families, and migration chasers seeking the perfect blend of wild drama and modern luxury in the northern Serengeti.

why.title: River, Crossing, and Comfort
why.body: Sayari is ideal for those who want to see river crossings, enjoy experienced guiding, and relax in luxury after wild days. Best for couples, solo explorers, families, and photographers.

facts.best_months: July to September for the Great Migration with crossings into October, and November to March for quiet resident wildlife; open June to March.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Kogatende airstrip in the northern Serengeti, then drive 20 minutes to camp.
facts.signature_experiences: Mara River crossings, twice daily game drives, walking safaris, the rim-flow pool and spa.
facts.who_its_for: Migration seekers, couples and honeymooners, and families or groups who want a private Retreat.

faqs.q: Where is Sayari Camp?
faqs.a: Sayari Camp is in the northern Serengeti, Tanzania. Asilia describes it as the closest permanent camp to the Mara River, giving the quickest access to the migration river crossings.

faqs.q: How do I get to Sayari Camp?
faqs.a: Fly to Kogatende airstrip, a 20 minute drive from camp.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Sayari Camp?
faqs.a: July, August and September are usually best for the Great Migration, and river crossings still occur in October. From November to March the area offers resident wildlife including black rhino, lion, leopard and cheetah, with few other guests. The camp is open June to March.

faqs.q: How many tents does Sayari Camp have?
faqs.a: There are 15 tented suites, including 2 family tents and 1 honeymoon tent, plus two Retreats that opened in 2023. The Retreats come with a dedicated chef, guide and private safari vehicle.

faqs.q: Does Sayari Camp allow children?
faqs.a: Yes, children aged five and older are welcome, with a family tent and two Retreats designed for families and small groups. Walking safaris have a minimum age of 12.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Sayari Camp?
faqs.a: Watching the wildebeest river crossings from July to October, twice daily game drives and walking safaris, which run 1 June to 15 January subject to weather. Between activities there is a rim-flow pool and massages.

stays.name: Segera Retreat
stays.tagline: Where Conservation, Art, and Wild Africa Meet
stays.quote: At Segera, nature, creativity, and community unite, each stay is a step toward a more beautiful, sustainable world.
stays.bestMonthsNote: June to October is dry season with clear skies and wildlife at its peak; December to March offers green landscapes and fewer visitors.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Nanyuki or directly to Segera’s private airstrip. 45-minute road transfer from Nanyuki or 10 minutes from Segera Airstrip.

paras: Award-winning villas set in lush botanical gardens. Outdoor and indoor showers, private decks, and unique architecture. Contemporary African art collection. Organic gardens, saltwater pool, and spa. Personalized service, curated adventures, and focus on sustainability.

onlyHere: Segera is perfect for multigenerational families, romantic couples, solo adventurers, and art lovers. Every guest is part of a living story, conservation, creativity, and real connection in the wild heart of Kenya.

why.title: Wild Luxury, Inspired Living
why.body: Stay at Segera for bold architecture, private villas, cutting-edge conservation, and art at every turn. Best for those seeking rare wildlife, bespoke safaris, and a retreat that’s as creative as it is restorative.

stays.name: Selinda Main Camp by Great Plains
stays.tagline: Wild comfort, private waterways, Selinda adventure
stays.quote: Wake to elephants on the floodplain, unwind in barefoot luxury, and experience Botswana’s wild heart in Selinda.
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to October is the dry season, ideal for peak wildlife and the best game viewing. November to April brings lush landscapes, dramatic scenery, excellent birding, and fewer visitors.
stays.airportDirections: Fly by charter to Selinda Airstrip, followed by a 45-minute road transfer to camp. Charter flights are available from Maun, Kasane, or other Delta camps.

paras: Three spacious guest suites, each with a private deck, plunge pool, lounge, copper bathtub, and indoor and outdoor showers. A two-bedroom Selinda Suite accommodates families or private groups with its own staff and vehicle. The main lodge features a fire deck, library, and stunning lagoon views.
Morning and afternoon game drives, night drives, private boating when in season, guided bush walks, birding, photographic safaris, seasonal fishing, sundowners, and in-suite spa treatments.

Spacious tented suites with private plunge pools and copper bathtubs overlooking the lagoon. Private safari vehicles, big cat and elephant encounters, eco-friendly solar-powered design, and exclusive access to the reserve.

onlyHere: Selinda Main Camp is ideal for couples, families, photographers, and adventure seekers seeking classic luxury, abundant wildlife, and the quiet drama of Selinda’s private wilderness.

why.title: Lagoon Luxury, Selinda Spirit
why.body: Selinda Main Camp is ideal for travelers who want a blend of comfort, exclusivity, and high wildlife density, with bespoke service and private guiding. Best for couples, families, solo adventurers, and photographers.

stays.name: Senda Monteverde
stays.tagline: A luxury cloud forest sanctuary immersed in Costa Rica's most magical ecosystem.
stays.quote: Some forests are explored. Others completely transform the way you see the world.
stays.bestMonthsNote: The dry season provides excellent hiking conditions, exceptional wildlife viewing, and clearer opportunities for observing Monteverde's famous cloud forest landscapes. Birdwatching is particularly rewarding during these months, especially for sightings of the resplendent quetzal.
stays.airport: Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport (LIR)
stays.airportDirections: Drive 2h30m from SJO (paved) or 2.5 hrs from LIR (last 18 km gravel).

items: 24 suites and rooms in contemporary mountain bungalows
Small network of on-property nature trails
El Sapo Restaurant & Bar with hyper-local ingredients
Two heated Jacuzzis and a dry sauna
Minutes from the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve

onlyHere: Senda sits at the foot of the Monteverde cloud forest, high on the Continental Divide, with views across the highlands to the Gulf of Nicoya on clear days. Guests cross a hanging bridge straight into the neighboring Aguti Wildlife Reserve, with its old-growth trees and wildlife, and can still stroll 15 minutes into Monteverde town.

facts.best_months: January to mid May is Monteverde's dry season; late May to mid December is the green season.
facts.how_to_get_there: Drive about 2 hours 30 minutes from San José (SJO) or about 2.5 hours from Liberia (LIR), or book the lodge's private driver.
facts.signature_experiences: Free access to the neighboring Aguti Wildlife Reserve, naturalist-led cloud forest hikes and night tours, and coffee experiences.
facts.who_its_for: Families, couples and adventurous travelers who want the cloud forest with town a short walk away.

faqs.q: Where is Senda Monteverde?
faqs.a: Senda Monteverde is in Cerro Plano, Monteverde, in Costa Rica's northwestern highlands at about 4,660 feet above sea level. It is minutes from the Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve and a 15-minute walk from Monteverde town.

faqs.q: How do you get to Senda Monteverde?
faqs.a: Drive about 2 hours 30 minutes from San José (SJO) on a road paved all the way, or about 2.5 hours from Liberia (LIR), where the final 18 km is gravel. The lodge can arrange a private driver or a shared shuttle from either airport.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Senda Monteverde?
faqs.a: Senda gives Monteverde's dry season as January to mid May and its green season as late May to mid December. Daytime temperatures stay around 20 to 25°C (68 to 77°F) all year.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Senda Monteverde have?
faqs.a: Senda has 24 suites and rooms in stand-alone mountain bungalows: Superior Rooms, Junior Suites, Premium Suites and the two-bedroom Senda Suites.

faqs.q: Is Senda Monteverde good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Senda welcomes children of all ages, with cribs, a kids' menu, small rubber boots and walking sticks, and Senda Suites that sleep up to 4 adults and 2 children.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Senda Monteverde?
faqs.a: Complimentary self-guided access to the neighboring Aguti Wildlife Reserve across the lodge's hanging bridge, cloud forest hikes and night tours with in-house naturalist guides, coffee experiences, and two heated Jacuzzis and a dry sauna.

faqs.q: Who is Senda Monteverde best for?
faqs.a: Families, couples and adventurous travelers. The lodge calls itself a luxury eco-hotel for adventurous travelers who seek a peaceful, down-to-earth stay.

stays.name:
Serengeti Lamai Camp 
 By Serian
stays.tagline: “Where the Mara River whispers, and the wildebeest roam free.”
stays.quote: Freedom to roam, under open skies - this is the wild you came for.
stays.bestMonthsNote: These months coincide with peak river-crossing season of the Great Migration, giving you the highest chance of witnessing herds crossing the Mara River, dramatic predator action, and prime safari conditions with dry weather and easy game-spotting.
stays.airport: Nearest airstrip: Lamai Airstrip (for small charter flights).
stays.airportDirections: From Lamai Airstrip, It's a short transfer by 4WD to the camp (time depends on flight arrival schedule). Best arrival is via charter flight into Lamai Airstrip, then ground transfer to camp.
stays.founderNote: James has worked with Alex Walker since 2017; Serian's camps are vetted and Founder Favorites. Serian is our preferred fly-camping partner.

items: Witnessing the Great Migration river crossings
En-suite bathrooms with flushing toilets and showers
Dedicated 4WD safari vehicle per group with private guide & spotter

onlyHere: Serengeti Lamai places you at the edge of wild travel & far from the crowds, in the thick of the savannah and the Mara River’s pulse. It’s a rare chance to observe the Great Migration, predators, plains game, and sweeping landscapes all from a camp designed for intimacy, presence, and respect for nature.

why.body: With just 8 elegant safari tents and 2 family suites, the camp offers an intimate and private atmosphere. Its secluded setting makes it ideal for exclusive bookings, private groups, or those traveling with specialist safari guides.

facts.best_months: July to October for the Mara River crossings; the camp is open all year except April and May.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly in to Lamai Airstrip, the camp's preferred airstrip in the northern Serengeti.
facts.signature_experiences: Mara River crossings, private open-top game drives with a guide and spotter, walking safaris and fly camping.
facts.who_its_for: Families, privately guided groups and exclusive-use bookings wanting front-row access to the river crossings.

faqs.q: Where is Serian's Serengeti Lamai?
faqs.a: In the Lamai Wedge of the northern Serengeti National Park, about a kilometre from the Mara River above Crossing Point 4. Serian says the camp sits midway among the crossing points along the river.

faqs.q: How do I get to Serengeti Lamai?
faqs.a: Fly in to Lamai Airstrip, which Serian names as the camp's preferred airstrip. Each group then has its own 4WD vehicle with a dedicated guide and spotter.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Serengeti Lamai?
faqs.a: July to October, when the river crossings take centre stage from camp. The camp is open all year except April and May, and outside crossing season the Lamai Wedge has four resident lion prides and large herds of elephant, buffalo and plains game.

faqs.q: How many tents does Serengeti Lamai have?
faqs.a: There are 8 tents and 2 family suites, each with an en-suite bathroom, flushing toilet and plumbed shower. The camp has 24-hour electricity and no Wi-Fi.

faqs.q: Is Serengeti Lamai good for families or private groups?
faqs.a: Yes. Serian says the camp's intimacy makes it perfect for families or privately guided groups, and it can be booked on an exclusive basis.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Serengeti Lamai?
faqs.a: Watching the wildebeest cross the Mara River, game drives in your own open-top vehicle, walking safaris and fly camping. The camp also gives access to the Lamai Wedge and Wogakuria Kopjes.

faqs.q: How long should I stay at Serengeti Lamai?
faqs.a: Serian recommends a minimum of 4 nights to take in all that the northern Serengeti has to offer.

stays.name: Shawa Luangwa Camp
stays.tagline: Silent safaris in the Valley of the Leopard
stays.bestMonthsNote: Lush in May; dry-season game viewing June to October.
stays.airportDirections: About a 1 hour flight from Lusaka, then a 45-minute road transfer.

paras: Five Safari Suites under canvas on the Luangwa River: Couples Suites, a Family Suite and Premium Suites, each raised on stilts with a 270-degree view and an en-suite bathtub.

items: Game drives in silent electric vehicles
Conservation and community projects in the Luangwa

paras: A small eco-friendly bush camp in the Nsefu Sector of South Luangwa National Park. Named after the legendary Zambian guide Jacob Shawa. Silent Safari vehicles. Can be booked exclusively.

onlyHere: Shawa Luangwa brings electric, silent safaris to the Valley of the Leopard, in the Nsefu Sector, one of the park's most untouched areas and ideal for safaris on foot and by vehicle.

why.body: The Valley of the Leopard
Best for couples, families taking the camp and keen walkers.

facts.best_months: May to October, within a camp season of 1 May to 30 November.
facts.how_to_get_there: A flight of about 1 hour from Lusaka to Mfuwe, then a 45-minute road transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Silent electric game drives and walking safaris in the Nsefu Sector, the Valley of the Leopard.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, families with children 9 and over, private groups and wildlife photographers.

faqs.q: Where is Shawa Luangwa Camp?
faqs.a: Shawa is a small bush camp on the eastern bank of the Luangwa River in the Nsefu Sector of South Luangwa National Park, Zambia.

faqs.q: How do you get to Shawa Luangwa Camp?
faqs.a: Fly from Lusaka to Mfuwe (usually about 1 hour with Proflight), then take a road transfer of about 45 minutes to camp.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Shawa Luangwa?

faqs.q: How many suites does Shawa have?
faqs.a: Five raised canvas Safari Suites: Couples Suites, a Family Suite that sleeps four, and Premium Suites. The whole camp can be booked exclusively.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Shawa Luangwa?
faqs.a: Yes, from 9 years old, and the team is experienced with families with older children.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Shawa?
faqs.a: Silent safaris in solar-powered electric e-Cruisers, walking safaris with a guide and armed scout, birding and bush meals. Green Safaris says it is the only operator offering Silent Safaris in Luangwa.

faqs.q: Who is Shawa Luangwa best for?
faqs.a: Couples, families with children 9 and over, groups taking the whole camp and photographers; Green Safaris calls the Nsefu Sector ideal for photographic safaris.

The only lodge in Skeleton Coast National Park, in the Skeleton Coast Central Concession Area. Central lounge and restaurant with a wraparound deck facing the Atlantic. Fireplace and library. Solar powered. Two Michelin Keys. Children of all ages welcome.

faqs.q: Where is Shipwreck Lodge?
faqs.a: It is in the Skeleton Coast Central Concession Area of Skeleton Coast National Park in north-western Namibia, strung along a dune facing the Atlantic. Natural Selection says it is the only lodge in the whole of the park.

faqs.q: How do I get to Shipwreck Lodge?
faqs.a: Natural Selection does not publish transfer details on its Shipwreck Lodge page, so flights or road transfers are confirmed with its reservations team at booking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: The lodge is open year round. May to October is winter, with pleasant days, chilly mornings and evenings and little to no rain; November to April is summer, with clearer, less foggy mornings that suit birdwatching.

faqs.q: How many rooms are there?
faqs.a: Ten rooms built to resemble shipwrecks: eight twin or double and two family rooms (triples on request), all en suite and solar powered, with wood-burning stoves.

faqs.q: Are children welcome?
faqs.a: Yes, children of all ages are welcome. Private vehicles are required on drives and walks for families with children under 10, and quad biking and sandboarding have their own age guidance.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Nature drives along the Hoarusib River, a day excursion to the Mowe Bay Cape fur seal colony past old wrecks, the Clay Castles excursion, guided quad biking, sandboarding and beach walks.

faqs.q: Who is Shipwreck Lodge best for?
faqs.a: Travellers drawn to raw, remote coastline and desert, including families and photographers. Natural Selection notes that wildlife sightings here are rare but special.

faqs.q: Where is Sindabezi Island Camp?
faqs.a: Sindabezi is a small island in the Zambezi River, 12 km upstream of Victoria Falls in Zambia, looking over the river floodplain and Victoria Falls National Park. It is the sister camp to Tongabezi.

faqs.q: How do you get to Sindabezi Island?
faqs.a: Fly into Livingstone Airport, drive about 25 minutes to Tongabezi, then take a short boat ride to the island. Green Safaris says the island is about 15 minutes from Tongabezi by boat.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Sindabezi?
faqs.a: Sindabezi is open year-round. Devil's Pool usually opens mid-August to mid-January, and April to August tends to be best for lunar rainbows over the Falls.

faqs.q: How many chalets are on Sindabezi?
faqs.a: There are five open-fronted thatched Chalets, including the Honeymoon Chalet, and small groups can book the whole island.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Sindabezi?
faqs.a: Yes, from 9 years old. Green Safaris recommends it for families who have been on safari before.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Sindabezi?
faqs.a: Boat transfers to the island, sunrise and sunset cruises, sampan dinners on the river, sand bar picnics and visits to Victoria Falls. All Tongabezi activities are open to Sindabezi guests.

faqs.q: Who is Sindabezi best for?
faqs.a: Couples and honeymooners, solo travellers, families with children 9 and over, and small groups taking the island privately.

faqs.q: How do you get to Six Senses Zil Pasyon?
faqs.a: The quickest way is the Zil Air helicopter: a 20-minute flight from Seychelles International Airport (SEZ) on Mahé to the resort's own jetty helipad, flying between sunrise and sunset only and reserved in advance. Alternatively, take a speedboat or private yacht from Praslin or La Digue, or a seasonal private boat or yacht crossing from Mahé.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Six Senses Zil Pasyon?

Diving is best from March to May and September to November, hiking from May to September, turtle nesting runs from mid-October to mid-January and hatchlings appear from mid-December to mid-March.

faqs.q: How many villas does Six Senses Zil Pasyon have?

The spa has five spa villas, and PADI certified dive excursions run with dive centres from Praslin and La Digue.

faqs.q: Where is The Hide Safari Camp?
faqs.a: The Hide is on a private concession on the eastern boundary of Hwange National Park, Zimbabwe, overlooking a natural waterhole.

faqs.q: How do you get to The Hide?

Alternatively, a 35-minute light-aircraft flight from Victoria Falls lands at Umtshibi Airfield (40 minutes from camp) or Hwange Main Airport (1 hour 30 minutes from camp).

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit The Hide?
faqs.a: The Hide's mid to high season runs April to October, the dry winter, with warm days, clear skies and cold nights. Rain falls from late November to March or April.

faqs.q: How many tents does The Hide have?

faqs.q: Are children welcome at The Hide?
faqs.a: Children of every age are welcome at Tom's Little Hide and The Private Hide, which are booked exclusively. Tom's Little Hide suits six adults and up to four children, with a minimum of four full-paying adults.

faqs.q: What is special about The Hide?
faqs.a: Guests can walk from the deck through a tunnel, past the wine cellar, into an underground hide at the edge of the waterhole. Walking safaris, game drives and night drives are offered, with no limit on activities.

faqs.q: Is The Hide good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. It offers honeymoon deluxe tents, private dining under the stars with a complimentary bottle of wine, and The Dove's Nest treehouse sleep-out, complimentary on stays of three nights or more, subject to availability.

why.title: Where Craters Meet Clouds

facts.best_months: Year round, with July to September the peak dry months and May the quietest time to avoid crowds.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Lake Manyara airstrip, then drive about 3 hours to camp in the Ngorongoro Highlands.
facts.signature_experiences: Ngorongoro Crater game drives, Olmoti and Empakaai Crater hikes, Maasai community visits and the spa.

faqs.q: Where is The Highlands?
faqs.a: The Highlands is in Tanzania's Ngorongoro Conservation Area, perched on the edge of the Olmoti Crater forest. It is about an hour from the Ngorongoro Crater.

faqs.q: How do I get to The Highlands?
faqs.a: Fly to Lake Manyara airstrip, the nearest airstrip, which is a 3 hour drive from camp.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit The Highlands?
faqs.a: Ngorongoro is a year round destination. July, August and September are the peak dry months but the crater can feel busy, while Asilia names May as the best time to avoid crowds.

faqs.q: What are the rooms like at The Highlands?
faqs.a: There are 8 perspex-and-canvas domed suites, including an interconnected family suite and a honeymoon suite with an outdoor hot tub. Each has an en suite bathroom with hot showers and an in-room wood-burning stove.

faqs.q: Does The Highlands welcome children?
faqs.a: Yes. Families with children aged five and older are welcome, and there is a family suite.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at The Highlands?
faqs.a: Game drives on the Ngorongoro Crater floor, hiking to the top of Olmoti, walking down to the soda lake in Empakaai Crater to see flamingos, and cultural visits with the local Maasai community. The camp also has a spa.

faqs.q: Where is Time + Tide Chinzombo?
faqs.a: Time + Tide Chinzombo sits on a sweeping curve of the Luangwa River in South Luangwa National Park, Zambia. Guides take guests across the river by boat into one of the most game-rich areas of the park.

faqs.q: How do you get to Time + Tide Chinzombo?
faqs.a: Fly into Mfuwe Airport, then take a one-hour game drive transfer to camp. Transfers to and from the local airport are included in the rates.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Time + Tide Chinzombo?
faqs.a: Chinzombo is open all year. Boat safaris are seasonal and run from January to April, when the Luangwa River is high.

faqs.q: How many tents does Time + Tide Chinzombo have?
faqs.a: There are six luxury safari tents: five one-bedroom tents and one two-bedroom, two-bathroom family tent. Each has a private pool and a soaking tub with river views.

faqs.q: Is Time + Tide Chinzombo good for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Children of all ages are welcome, there is a two-bedroom family tent, and the camp offers activities for children.

faqs.q: What can you do at Time + Tide Chinzombo?
faqs.a: Morning and afternoon game drives, walking safaris, seasonal boat safaris, a sleepout under the stars, cultural experiences and sundowners. In-room spa treatments are available, and a 20-minute welcome massage is included.

faqs.q: Who is Time + Tide Chinzombo best for?
faqs.a: Families, couples and travellers who want a contemporary riverside camp with private pools, spa treatments and both walking and driving safaris in South Luangwa.

The main camp has dining areas, a lounge, bar, campfire, pool and a wildlife hide.

Riverfront tents at the confluence of the Chongwe and Zambezi Rivers. Private pools in the two suites. Seasonal canoeing and boating safaris. Wildlife hide for photography. Suites for families or couples with privately guided activities. Children of all ages welcome.

onlyHere: Time + Tide Chongwe is for couples, families, solo travelers, and adventure seekers who want riverside wildlife, water adventures, and the classic spirit of the Zambezi.

why.title: Zambezi Wild, River Calm
why.body: Time + Tide Chongwe is perfect for safari lovers, families, couples, and anyone who dreams of hippos, elephants, and river sunsets. Private suites, adventures on water and land, and welcoming staff make this a Lower Zambezi highlight.

facts.best_months: Open 1 April to 15 November, the months Time + Tide recommends for boating, canoeing and predator sightings in the Lower Zambezi.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Royal Airstrip, then a 20-minute drive to camp.
facts.signature_experiences: Canoeing and boating safaris, tiger fishing, walking safaris and a wildlife hide for photography.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, honeymooners, families and active travellers who want river safaris as well as drives and walks.

faqs.q: Where is Time + Tide Chongwe?
faqs.a: Time + Tide Chongwe is in Lower Zambezi National Park, Zambia, at the confluence of the Chongwe and Zambezi Rivers. Time + Tide runs it as Chongwe Camp, Chongwe Suites and the sole-use Chongwe House.

faqs.q: How do you get to Time + Tide Chongwe?
faqs.a: Fly to Royal Airstrip, then a 20-minute drive to camp. Transfers to and from the local airport are included in the rates.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Time + Tide Chongwe?
faqs.a: Chongwe is open from 1 April to 15 November. Time + Tide says April to November is when the Lower Zambezi is at its most magical, with the river right for boating and canoeing and good sightings of wild dogs, lions and leopards.

faqs.q: How many tents and suites does Time + Tide Chongwe have?
faqs.a: Chongwe Camp has eight classic safari tents. Chongwe Suites adds the one-bedroom Cassia Suite for two and the two-bedroom, two-bathroom Albida Suite for four, each with a river-view pool and a dedicated butler.

faqs.q: Are children welcome at Time + Tide Chongwe?
faqs.a: Yes. Children of all ages are welcome, the camp offers children's activities, and the Albida Suite is designed for families who want their own space.

faqs.q: What can you do at Time + Tide Chongwe?
faqs.a: Morning and afternoon game drives, walking safaris, seasonal canoeing and boating safaris, seasonal tiger fishing and a sleepout under the stars. The camp's wildlife hide is good for photography and spotting nocturnal animals.

faqs.q: Who is Time + Tide Chongwe best for?
faqs.a: Couples and honeymooners in the Cassia Suite, families in the Albida Suite, and anyone who wants water-based safaris alongside drives and walks.

faqs.q: Who is Time + Tide Mchenja best for?
faqs.a: Travellers who want an intimate riverside camp with walking safaris and night drives, including families who can use the two-bedroom family room.

stays.tagline: Eight ocean-view rooms and suites on the forested slopes of Nosy Komba

stays.airportDirections: A 20-minute boat transfer from Nosy Be to Nosy Komba. Transfers from Nosy Be Airport, Hell Ville Port or Ankify Port are arranged by road and boat.

paras: Eight ocean-view rooms on the slopes of Nosy Komba: six Ocean View Rooms of 90sqm for up to three guests and two Ocean View Suites of 120sqm for up to four. Each has an en suite private bathroom, a private outdoor lounge area and terrace, double or twin beds, fans and linen mosquito nets. The main lodge has a dining area, lounge and outdoor relaxation spaces, with meals of Malagasy flavours made from fresh local ingredients. Wifi in the rooms is limited by design, to encourage time in nature.

A forest-to-reef safari: lemur trekking in Lokobe National Park, guided walks in the island's forest in search of lemurs, chameleons and endemic species, scuba diving in the Nosy Be archipelago for all levels, snorkelling with turtles, stand-up paddle boarding and kayaking, sunset cruises through the mangroves, village tours, and private beach picnics or dinners. Depending on the season, guests can swim with whale sharks or watch humpback whales from their terrace. In-room spa treatments are available.

Nosy Komba is a forested island of volcanic origin off the northwest coast of Madagascar, about 25km2, a short boat ride from Nosy Be and a hub of the archipelago for snorkelling, diving and lemur trekking. The suites are built from natural materials. Time + Tide took on the lodge's established heritage and runs it on its values of sustainability, connection with local communities and conservation of the island's environment.

onlyHere: Forest and reef from the same doorstep: lemurs in the trees above the lodge, turtles in the water below, and village life on the island all around.

why.title: Forest to Reef on a Volcanic Island
why.body: Best for couples and families with children of any age who want lemurs, snorkelling and diving in the Nosy Be archipelago from a small lodge of eight suites.

facts.best_months: Open all year; whale sharks and humpback whales by season.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Nosy Be, then a 20-minute boat transfer.
facts.signature_experiences: Lemur trekking in Lokobe, snorkelling with turtles and diving the Nosy Be archipelago.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and families with children of any age.

faqs.q: Where is Time + Tide Tsara Komba?
faqs.a: On the forested slopes of Nosy Komba, a small volcanic island in the Nosy Be archipelago off the northwest coast of Madagascar.

faqs.q: How do you get to Time + Tide Tsara Komba?
faqs.a: Fly to Nosy Be, then take a 20-minute boat transfer to Nosy Komba.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Time + Tide Tsara Komba have?
faqs.a: Eight: 6 Ocean View Rooms (90sqm, up to 3 guests) and 2 Ocean View Suites (120sqm, up to 4 guests), each with ocean views and a private terrace.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Time + Tide Tsara Komba?
faqs.a: Yes. Time + Tide welcomes children of all ages.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Time + Tide Tsara Komba?
faqs.a: The lodge is open all year. Whale shark swims and humpback whale sightings depend on the season.

faqs.q: What can you do at Time + Tide Tsara Komba?
faqs.a: Lemur trekking in Lokobe National Park, forest walks, scuba diving, snorkelling with turtles, paddle boarding, kayaking, mangrove sunset cruises, village tours and private beach picnics.

Every guest enjoys genuine Fijian hospitality, personalised service and the freedom to experience island life at an unhurried pace surrounded by extraordinary natural beauty.

stays.name: Tongabezi
stays.tagline: Hidden on the Zambezi, twelve kilometres above Victoria Falls
stays.bestMonthsNote: Devil's Pool usually mid-August to mid-January; lunar rainbows best April to August.
stays.airport: Harry Mwaanga Nkumbula International Airport, Livingstone (LVI)
stays.airportDirections: About 25 minutes by road.

paras: Five River Cottages, four Houses including the Honeymoon House and the Tree House, and three Family Houses, each furnished with pieces chosen from around Africa. Tangala Private House for families and friends who want the place to themselves.

Boat cruises and electric dhow cruises on the Zambezi. Sampan dinners and island picnic lunches. Game drives in Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park and private guides on request. Victoria Falls a short drive away. A visit to the Tongabezi Trust School in the community.

A Green Safaris eco-lodge on the banks of the Zambezi, 12 km upstream of Victoria Falls. Family-created and more than thirty years in the making, from tents with bucket showers in 1990 to the lodge it is today. Expert childminders and family-sized rooms.

onlyHere: Tongabezi is where romance meets the river: houses open to the Zambezi, dinner on an island, and the Falls a short drive away. The New York Times once called it a place worth getting married for.

why.title: The Zambezi, Slowly
why.body: Best for honeymooners, families and anyone pairing Victoria Falls with a safari in Zambia or Botswana.

facts.best_months: Open year-round, with Devil's Pool usually open mid-August to mid-January and lunar rainbows best April to August.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 25 minutes by road from Livingstone Airport (Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International).
facts.signature_experiences: Sampan dinner on the Zambezi, electric dhow cruises, island picnics and Victoria Falls 12 km downstream.
facts.who_its_for: Honeymooners, couples, families, solo travellers and private groups.

faqs.q: Where is Tongabezi?
faqs.a: Tongabezi is a Green Safaris eco-lodge on the banks of the Zambezi River in Zambia, 12 km upstream of Victoria Falls.

faqs.q: How do you get to Tongabezi?
faqs.a: Fly into Livingstone Airport (Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International), which Green Safaris says is about 25 minutes from the lodge. Livingstone connects with hubs such as Lusaka, Johannesburg, Cape Town and Nairobi.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Tongabezi?
faqs.a: Tongabezi is open year-round. Devil's Pool on Livingstone Island usually opens mid-August to mid-January when the river is low, and April to August tends to be best for lunar rainbows over the Falls.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Tongabezi have?
faqs.a: Green Safaris lists five River Cottages, four Houses (including the Honeymoon House and the Tree House) and three Family Houses, plus Tangala Private House for exclusive use.

faqs.q: Is Tongabezi good for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Green Safaris says the team are expert childminders, menus are tailored for children, and there are family-sized rooms such as the Dog House and Garden House.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Tongabezi?
faqs.a: A candlelit sampan dinner on the Zambezi, island picnic lunches, sunrise and sunset cruises including the electric dhow, game drives in Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park and visits to Victoria Falls. The Livingstone Island tour with Devil's or Angel's Pool can be added.

faqs.q: Who is Tongabezi best for?
faqs.a: Honeymooners and couples, families, solo travellers and private groups who want Tangala Private House to themselves.

stays.name: Tswalu Reserve Kalahari
stays.tagline: Luxury and regeneration in Africa’s wild heart.
stays.quote: Come to Tswalu for a journey that leaves footprints and inspires renewal, both in your heart and across the horizon.
stays.bestMonthsNote: During the dry season, wildlife gathers at waterholes, skies are perfect for stargazing, and daytime game drives are ideal in the crisp weather.
stays.airport: Tswalu Private Airstrip (flight charter) · Upington International Airport (UTN) · Kimberley Airport (KIM)
stays.airportDirections: The closest option is Tswalu’s own airstrip, with daily charter flights from Cape Town and Johannesburg. Alternatively, fly into Upington (350 km) or Kimberley (370 km) and enjoy a scenic private transfer through the Kalahari.
stays.founderNote: James's number one. In his words: it changed the way he sees Africa completely. Off the scale: the silence, and the perfection.

paras: The Motse – nine spacious stone-and-thatch suites, including family options.
Tarkuni – five-bedroom exclusive-use homestead with private chef and vehicle.
Loapi – six contemporary tented safari homes forming a private micro-camp.

items: Private game drives with a dedicated ranger and tracker
Guided bush walks and horseback safaris
Stargazing and Malori sleep-outs under pristine skies
San rock art walks and dune-top dining

paras: South Africa’s largest private reserve at 1,200 km² with minimal guest impact.
One of the few places to see desert black rhino, black-maned lion, and pangolin.
Malaria-free and family-friendly, with a Junior Ranger program for children.
Michelin-level cuisine featuring hyper-local ingredients.

onlyHere: Step into the red sands of renewal, where every journey restores both soul and savannah. Tswalu offers a rare blend of luxury in remote wilderness, unmatched exclusivity, and meaningful conservation impact. It is perfect for families, couples, solo explorers, and eco-minded travelers.

why.title: A Regenerative Safari Beyond Compare
why.body: Come to Tswalu to experience true wilderness regeneration, a place where luxury meets conservation and every stay gives back to the land.

facts.best_months: May to September, when wildlife gathers at waterholes and dry skies suit stargazing.
facts.how_to_get_there: Daily charter flights from Cape Town and Johannesburg to Tswalu's private airstrip, or fly into Upington (350 km) or Kimberley (370 km) and take a private transfer.
facts.who_its_for: Families, couples, solo explorers and eco-minded travellers who want remote wilderness with conservation impact.
facts.signature_experiences: Private game drives with a dedicated ranger and tracker, habituated meerkat encounters and Malori sleep-outs.

faqs.q: What makes Tswalu different?
faqs.a: Tswalu is South Africa's largest private reserve at 1,200 km², with minimal guest impact. It is one of the few places to see desert black rhino, black-maned lion and pangolin.

faqs.q: Is Tswalu good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Tswalu is malaria-free and family-friendly, with a Junior Ranger program for children and family options at The Motse.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Tswalu?
faqs.a: May to September. In the dry season wildlife gathers at waterholes, skies are clear for stargazing and crisp days suit game drives.

faqs.q: How do you get to Tswalu?
faqs.a: Fly to Tswalu's own airstrip on daily charters from Cape Town and Johannesburg. You can also fly into Upington (350 km) or Kimberley (370 km) and take a private transfer.

faqs.q: Where can you stay at Tswalu?
faqs.a: The Motse has nine stone-and-thatch suites. Tarkuni is a five-bedroom exclusive-use homestead with private chef and vehicle. Loapi is six tented homes forming a private micro-camp.

stays.name: Tubu Tree Camp
stays.tagline: Classic land safari on the edge of the floodplain
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Maun, then by light aircraft to the Jao Reserve airstrip and on to camp by road.

paras: Eight tented suites raised on wooden platforms beneath marula and jackalberry trees, looking out over a seasonal floodplain.

items: Seasonal boating and mokoro when the flood arrives

paras: Set in the drier western part of the private Jao Reserve. A classic game-viewing camp with access to both floodplain and dry savannah. Swimming pool. Shares its game-viewing area with sister camp Little Tubu.

onlyHere: Tubu Tree is for travelers who come for the animals. Elephant herds, leopard and plains game move through a game-rich corner of the Okavango, and the camp is built for long days out with a guide who knows the ground.

why.title: Classic Safari, Game First
why.body: Best for first safaris, photographers, families and anyone who wants land-based game viewing in the Okavango Delta.

stays.name: Tuludi
stays.tagline: Seven suites among the leadwoods of Khwai
stays.airport: Maun (MUB) or Kasane (BBK), then charter flight
stays.airportDirections: A light-aircraft flight from Maun or Kasane to the private Khwai airstrip, then a game drive into camp.

paras: Seven widely spaced suites under high, pitched canvas roofs, linked by elevated boardwalks and shaded by leadwood trees, including a family tent.

items: Boat trips and mokoro (water levels permitting)
Dawn patrols with the reserve's rangers
A night at Skybeds from April to October

paras: In the 200,000-hectare Khwai Private Reserve in the northern Okavango Delta, a partnership with Khwai Village. A raised main deck, a firepit over the floodplains, a large pool, a treehouse library four metres up with a slide, and a handcrafted mosaic bar. 100% solar powered. Open all year.

onlyHere: A private reserve where lion, leopard, cheetah and wild dog all hunt year round, and where your stay supports Khwai Village through the reserve's community partnership.

why.title: Predators and Privacy

Set near Placencia village, it offers a quieter resort atmosphere without feeling removed from local life. facts.who_its_for: Travelers seeking a relaxed Caribbean beachfront stay with distinctive Balinese-inspired design, access to Placencia village, and opportunities for coastal excursions. Suitable for couples, families, and solo travelers; confirm family-specific services directly.
facts.signature_experiences: Enjoy the Caribbean shoreline, explore the Placencia Peninsula, and arrange outings to the Belize Barrier Reef, nearby cayes, or inland landscapes.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Turtle Inn have?

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Turtle Inn?

faqs.q: What can you do from Turtle Inn?

stays.name: Ubuntu Migration Camp by Asilia
stays.tagline: Follow the herds, live the migration, sleep wild
stays.quote: Wake to the sound of hooves thundering across the plains and track the Great Migration from the comfort of your classic mobile camp
stays.bestMonths: June to mid-November (Northern Serengeti), mid-December to mid-March (Southern Serengeti)
stays.bestMonthsNote: July to October for the Mara River crossings in the north; January to mid-March for calving in the south. The camp closes mid-March to May and mid-November to mid-December while it moves.
stays.airport: Lamai Airstrip (North, June to mid-November); Kusini (Serengeti South) Airstrip (South, mid-December to mid-March)
stays.airportDirections: North: 1 hour 40 minute drive from Lamai. South: 90 minute drive from Kusini.

paras: Ten canvas safari tents, including a four-sleeper family tent, all with en suite bathrooms, bucket showers, and private porches. Main area with lounge, open-air dining room, and campfire. Camp location shifts with the migration.

onlyHere: Ubuntu Migration Camp is for adventurous travelers, couples, families, and migration enthusiasts seeking front row seats to nature’s greatest show and the thrill of mobile safari life.

why.title: Chase the Wildebeest
why.body: Ubuntu is perfect for those wanting real adventure, close wildlife, and the excitement of moving with the migration. Best for couples, solo travelers, photographers, and families.

facts.best_months: July to October for northern river crossings and January to mid-March for southern calving season; closed mid-March to May and mid-November to mid-December.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly to Lamai airstrip (June to mid-November, 1 hour 40 minute drive) or Kusini airstrip (mid-December to mid-March, about 90 minutes).
facts.signature_experiences: A mobile camp that moves with the herds, for Mara River crossings on the Lamai Wedge and calving season on the southern plains.
facts.who_its_for: Migration followers and photographers, plus families with children aged five and over.

faqs.q: Is Ubuntu Migration Camp a mobile camp?
faqs.a: Yes. Ubuntu is a tented camp that can be disassembled in a couple of days and moved to follow the Great Migration. It is on the Lamai Wedge in the northern Serengeti from June to mid-November, and at Kusini in the southern Serengeti from mid-December to mid-March.

faqs.q: How do I get to Ubuntu Migration Camp?
faqs.a: It depends on the season. From June to mid-November, fly to Lamai airstrip, a 1 hour 40 minute drive from camp; from mid-December to mid-March, fly to the Kusini (Serengeti South) airstrip, about a 90 minute drive away.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Ubuntu Migration Camp?
faqs.a: July to October is best for river crossings in the northern Serengeti, and January to mid-March is best for the calving season in the south. The camp is closed from mid-March to May and from mid-November to mid-December while it moves.

faqs.q: How many tents does Ubuntu Migration Camp have?
faqs.a: There are 10 canvas safari tents, including one four-sleeper family tent. Each tent has an en suite bathroom with a traditional safari-style bucket shower and flushing toilet.

faqs.q: Does Ubuntu Migration Camp accept children?
faqs.a: Yes, children as young as five are welcome, and the family tent sleeps up to four. Walking safaris have a minimum age of 12.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Ubuntu Migration Camp?
faqs.a: Twice daily game drives following the herds, river crossings in the north, and calving season predator action in the south. Walking safaris are offered at the northern location only, and hot-air balloon flights are possible over the southern plains.

faqs.q: Who is Ubuntu Migration Camp best for?
faqs.a: Travellers who want to be close to the Great Migration in a classic tented camp, including photographers looking to capture the first river crossings.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Bisate Lodge?
faqs.a: Wilderness Bisate Lodge sits at the foot of Rwanda's Virunga volcanoes on the edge of Volcanoes National Park in north-western Rwanda, about 15 km from the town of Musanze. The villas overlook Mount Bisoke, Karisimbi and Mikeno, and the lodge lies within a private area adjacent to the park that Wilderness manages for conservation and reforestation.

faqs.q: How do you get to Wilderness Bisate Lodge?
faqs.a: Fly into Kigali International Airport. Helicopter transfers are offered. By road, Bisate is approximately a three-hour drive from Kigali via Musanze, and most guests transfer by road with Wilderness Touring, operating as Thousand Hills Rwanda. As flights often arrive early in the morning or late at night, Wilderness recommends a night in Kigali before the drive to the lodge.

faqs.q: What are the rooms like at Bisate Lodge?
faqs.a: There are six en-suite forest villas, each designed as an homage to Rwandan royal heritage, with a fireplace, a king-sized bed and views of Mount Bisoke, Karisimbi and Mikeno. A maximum of 12 guests stay at the lodge at any one time.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum age for gorilla trekking from Bisate?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Rwandan park regulations, children under 15 are not permitted on gorilla treks. Wilderness also notes that the lodge is not suited to guests unable to walk two to five hours over hilly terrain.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Bisate Lodge?
faqs.a: Bisate is open year-round and gorillas can be tracked in all seasons. The dry seasons, June to September and December to February, offer the easiest trekking conditions underfoot. The green seasons, March to May and October to November, bring lush landscapes and lower rates. Wilderness recommends three to four nights, which allows for two gorilla treks.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences, and are gorilla permits included?
faqs.a: Guests trek to one of 12 habituated gorilla groups in Volcanoes National Park for an hour with the gorillas. Golden monkey trekking, a Mount Bisoke hike, the Dian Fossey gravesite, nature and bird walks, village visits and tree planting complete a stay. Gorilla trekking permits, park fees and the conservation levy are charged separately from the lodge rate.

faqs.q: Who is Bisate Lodge best suited to?
faqs.a: Wilderness describes it as best for serious wildlife travellers with a specific interest in primates, and says solo travellers, couples and small groups do well here. It is not suited to guests unable to walk two to five hours over hilly terrain.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Bisate Reserve?

faqs.q: How do you get to Wilderness Bisate Reserve?
faqs.a: Fly into Kigali International Airport, then charter a helicopter from Kigali to Bisate, the recommended option, subject to weather and the helicopter model. Alternatively, drive roughly three hours to Musanze, the closest village to Volcanoes National Park.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences, and are gorilla permits included?

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Busanga Bush Camp?
faqs.a: It sits on an island under sycamore fig trees in the heart of the Busanga Plains, in the remote north-west of Kafue National Park, Zambia.

faqs.q: How do you get to Busanga Bush Camp?
faqs.a: Only by light aircraft. Wilderness flights from Livingstone (LVI) or Lusaka (LUN) to the Busanga airstrip take around an hour and a half, and they do not run at set times.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Busanga Bush Camp?

faqs.q: How many tents does Busanga Bush Camp have?

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Busanga Bush Camp?

faqs.q: Who is Busanga Bush Camp best for?

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Desert Rhino Camp?
faqs.a: Wilderness names the cooler months, May to September, as particularly enjoyable for exploring Namibia's desert on foot. November to April is warmer, and occasional rains bring new life to the landscape. The camp page lists no seasonal closure.

faqs.q: How many suites does Desert Rhino Camp have?
faqs.a: The newly rebuilt camp has six contemporary canvas and stone suites, including one family unit. Each suite has its own stargazing deck, and there is a pool.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Desert Rhino Camp?
faqs.a: One of the six suites is a family unit. Wilderness does not publish a minimum age on the camp page, so we confirm the child policy, including for rhino tracking on foot, when planning.

faqs.q: What is the signature experience at Desert Rhino Camp?
faqs.a: Tracking black rhino on foot with rhino monitors, in partnership with Save the Rhino Trust. Nature drives, nature trails, UV scorpion spotting at night, campfire evenings and stargazing complete the stay.

faqs.q: Who is Desert Rhino Camp best suited to?
faqs.a: Travellers who want conservation at the heart of their safari. The camp's partnership with three community conservancies and Save the Rhino Trust protects one of the last free-roaming black rhino populations, and every stay contributes directly.

stays.name: Wilderness Doro Nawas
stays.tagline: Desert dreams and star beds in Damaraland
stays.quote: Wake to sunrise over rocky hills, search for desert-adapted elephants, and sleep beneath Namibia’s endless sky
stays.bestMonthsNote: May to October is dry, cool, and best for desert wildlife, hiking, and star beds. November to April is warmer, green, and quieter.
stays.airportDirections: Fly to Windhoek, connect by light aircraft to Doro Nawas or Twyfelfontein Airstrip, 30 minute road transfer to camp

paras: Sixteen wood, canvas and thatch guest rooms, each with a private outdoor shower, an airy veranda for sleeping out under the stars, and views across Damaraland in every direction. The camp also offers a family suite.

Guided nature drives and walks for desert-adapted elephant, giraffe, zebra, oryx and springbok. San rock art and engravings at Twyfelfontein. Damara culture in camp and at the Damara Living Museum. Excursions to the Petrified Forest, Burnt Mountain and Organ Pipes. Night walks for desert critters. Birding and stargazing.

Sleep-outs on your deck under the stars. Set on a rocky outcrop on the edge of the dry Aba-Huab River, with views in every direction. Pool and locally crafted keepsakes. A family suite. A joint venture with the Doro !Nawas Conservancy. Locally grown ingredients in traditional recipes, cooked in the boma or on the rooftop BBQ.

onlyHere: Wilderness Doro Nawas is for the explorer who craves silence, stars, and Namibia’s rugged landscapes. Perfect for couples, families, solo travelers, and anyone who dreams of star beds and rare desert wildlife.

why.title: Sleep Under Namibia's Stars
why.body: Wilderness Doro Nawas combines desert adventure, ancient rock art, and sleep-outs under the stars for an immersive stay. Best for families, couples, photographers, and anyone who wants wild beauty and cultural connection.

facts.best_months: Wilderness recommends the cooler months of May to September for exploring Namibia's desert, with clear winter skies for stargazing.
facts.how_to_get_there: Doro Nawas features on Wilderness self-drive and fly-in itineraries, with inter-camp transfers on Wilderness Air.
facts.signature_experiences: Nature drives for desert-adapted elephant, Twyfelfontein rock art, the Damara Living Museum and sleep-outs on your deck.
facts.who_its_for: First-time visitors to Namibia, families and travellers interested in culture, rock art and desert-adapted wildlife.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Doro Nawas?
faqs.a: Doro Nawas sits on a rocky outcrop on the edge of the dry Aba-Huab River in Damaraland, northwest Namibia. It is a base for exploring the rock art and engravings at Twyfelfontein, Namibia's first World Heritage Site.

faqs.q: How do you get to Doro Nawas?
faqs.a: Wilderness includes Doro Nawas in both self-drive and fly-in Namibia itineraries, with private inter-camp transfers on Wilderness Air. The camp page does not publish an airstrip or transfer time, so we confirm routing when planning.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Doro Nawas?
faqs.a: Wilderness names the cooler months, May to September, as particularly enjoyable for exploring the desert, with crystal-clear winter skies for stargazing. November to April is warmer and suits sleeping out on your deck. The camp page lists no seasonal closure.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Doro Nawas have?
faqs.a: Doro Nawas has 16 wood, canvas and thatch guest rooms, each with a private outdoor shower and a veranda where you can sleep out under the stars. The camp also offers a family suite.

faqs.q: Is Doro Nawas good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, the camp has a family suite for privacy. Wilderness does not publish a minimum age on the camp page, so we confirm the child policy when planning.

faqs.q: What is there to do at Doro Nawas?
faqs.a: Guided nature drives and walks for desert-adapted elephant, giraffe, zebra, oryx and springbok, plus visits to the San rock art at Twyfelfontein and the Damara Living Museum. Excursions reach the Petrified Forest, Burnt Mountain and Organ Pipes, and nights bring scorpion walks and stargazing.

faqs.q: Who is Doro Nawas best suited to?
faqs.a: Travellers who want culture and community alongside desert wildlife. The camp is a joint venture with the Doro !Nawas Conservancy, and Wilderness calls it an excellent introduction to Namibia's desert landscapes.

onlyHere: Wilderness Hoanib Skeleton Coast is for explorers who want wild desert, epic scenery, and rare wildlife, from desert-adapted elephants and lions to the seals and shipwrecks of the Skeleton Coast. Suited to intrepid travellers seeking Namibia's untamed edge.

why.title: Where Dunes Meet Ocean
why.body: Wilderness Hoanib Skeleton Coast offers epic landscapes, desert-adapted wildlife, and a feeling of true remoteness. Best for adventurers who want desert wonders and the haunting beaches of the Skeleton Coast.

facts.best_months: May to September is ideal for desert wildlife, while October to November can be very hot.
facts.how_to_get_there: Reached only by light aircraft with Wilderness Air, landing at the Hoanib Airstrip within the concession.
facts.signature_experiences: A Skeleton Coast excursion to Möwe Bay's seal colonies, desert-adapted wildlife drives and lion research presentations.
facts.who_its_for: Intrepid adventurers seeking remote desert, desert-adapted wildlife and the Skeleton Coast.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp?
faqs.a: In Namibia's Kaokoveld, straddling the private Palmwag Concession and Skeleton Coast National Park. The camp overlooks a wide desert valley that slopes down to the Hoanib River, with a waterhole visited by elephants and giraffes.

faqs.q: How do you get to Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp?
faqs.a: Only by light aircraft with Wilderness Air, landing at the dedicated Hoanib Airstrip within the concession. The nearest town, Sesfontein, is several hours' drive away over rough terrain.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp?
faqs.a: The cooler months, May to September, are ideal for desert wildlife viewing, when animals concentrate along the Hoanib River. October to November can be very hot, and the Skeleton Coast trip runs year-round, weather permitting.

faqs.q: How many suites does Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp have?
faqs.a: Eight generously appointed tented suites, totally solar-powered, with an open design that reflects the surrounding desert.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp?
faqs.a: Wilderness does not publish a child policy or a family unit on the camp page. We confirm current age guidance with Wilderness before booking a family.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Hoanib?
faqs.a: The Skeleton Coast excursion to Möwe Bay by light aircraft or road, with Cape fur seal colonies and shipwreck remnants, is included on stays of three nights or more. Nature drives search for desert-adapted elephant, giraffe, lion and brown hyena, and research presentations explain the area's lions.

faqs.q: Who is Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp best suited to?
faqs.a: Intrepid travellers who want true remoteness, desert-adapted wildlife and the haunting beaches of the Skeleton Coast in one stay.

stays.name: Wilderness Kulala Desert Lodge

Pool, and waterhole views from the wraparound veranda. Two family units. Set on the private Kulala Wilderness Reserve, rewilded from former goat farmland.

onlyHere: Kulala Desert Lodge is for the desert dreamer, the adventurer, and the family explorer. With exclusive-use gate access to Sossusvlei, rooftop stargazing, and unique desert experiences, it suits photographers, couples, solo travelers, and those seeking the heart of Namibia's wild beauty.

why.title: Where Dunes and Dreams Meet
why.body: Wilderness Kulala Desert Lodge blends adventure and comfort beside the red dunes of Sossusvlei. Perfect for nature lovers, families, couples, and photographers looking for unique landscapes and true silence.

facts.best_months: May to September brings comfortable dawn temperatures for the dunes, and the lodge is open year-round.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly with Wilderness Air to the private Kulala Airstrip, or drive by road from Windhoek or Swakopmund.
facts.signature_experiences: Sunrise at Sossusvlei through an exclusive-use gate, hot-air ballooning, electric fatbikes and rooftop sleep-outs.
facts.who_its_for: Families, groups and self-drive guests looking for a comfortable base for Sossusvlei.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Kulala Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: On the private Kulala Wilderness Reserve in the south of the Namib Desert, which borders Namib-Naukluft National Park, home to Sossusvlei and Deadvlei.

faqs.q: How do you get to Kulala Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: Fly by light aircraft with Wilderness Air to the private Kulala Airstrip inside the reserve, or drive by road from Windhoek or Swakopmund. The lodge welcomes self-drive guests.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Kulala Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: May to September, when dawn temperatures are comfortable for dune climbing and wildlife is more active. December to February can be extremely hot, and the lodge is open year-round.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Kulala Desert Lodge have?
faqs.a: 21 canvas and thatch rooms, including two family units. Each room has a flat rooftop for sleep-outs under the stars.

faqs.q: Is Kulala Desert Lodge good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Wilderness says the lodge beckons groups, families and self-drive guests, with two family units and electric fatbike rides that are a family favourite. No minimum age is published on the camp page, so we confirm it when planning.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Kulala Desert Lodge?
faqs.a: First access to Sossusvlei at sunrise through an exclusive-use gate for Wilderness guests on privately guided journeys, with Big Daddy dune and Deadvlei. Hot-air balloon flights (book in advance), Sesriem Canyon, nature drives, electric fatbikes and rooftop sleep-outs complete the stay.

faqs.q: Who is Kulala Desert Lodge best suited to?
faqs.a: Families, groups and self-drive travellers who want a down-to-earth, comfortable base for the Sossusvlei dunes.

why.body: Stay at Wilderness Linyanti Camp for uncrowded safaris, huge skies, seasonal waterways, and the comfort of home in Botswana’s wild north. Best for those who value privacy, connection to nature, and world-class guiding.

Catch and release fishing in the channels

Bird watching in one of Africa’s richest habitats

onlyHere: Only here do you wake to the sound of elephants moving quietly below your deck, watch red lechwe skim through the shallows, and drift out onto the water for breakfast as hippos grunt in the lagoon. Little DumaTau is a rare mix of ultra-intimate camp, big-landscape wilderness, and real conservation impact.

why.title: Luxury, Solitude, Sossusvlei
why.body: Wilderness Little Kulala blends romance, adventure, and sustainability. Ideal for couples, honeymooners, photographers, and those who want Namibia's desert in comfort, privacy, and style.

facts.signature_experiences: Exclusive-use gate access to Sossusvlei, hot-air ballooning, roll-out star beds and private plunge pools.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, honeymooners and photographers wanting an intimate, design-led base for Sossusvlei.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Little Kulala?

faqs.q: How do you get to Little Kulala?

faqs.q: How many suites does Little Kulala have?
faqs.a: Eleven recently refurbished suites for a maximum of 22 guests, each with a private plunge pool, a rooftop for sundowners and a roll-out star bed on the deck.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Little Kulala?

faqs.q: Who is Little Kulala best suited to?

onlyHere: At Magashi Peninsula, hippos and crocodiles fill the lake below the main area, and elephants, buffalo and plains game wander freely. why.body: Choose Magashi Peninsula for an intimate, private safari where luxury, adventure and conservation meet on the shores of Lake Rwanyakazinga.

facts.signature_experiences: Day and night game drives in a private area of Akagera, boat safaris on Lake Rwanyakazinga, catch-and-release fishing and rooftop Star Bed sleep-outs.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Magashi Peninsula?
faqs.a: Wilderness Magashi Peninsula is in Akagera National Park on Rwanda's north-eastern border, set on a 4,287-hectare (10,590-acre) private area at the furthest reaches of the park. It overlooks Lake Rwanyakazinga, with its own stretch of lake shoreline and the Mutumba Mountains beyond.

faqs.q: How do you get to Magashi Peninsula?
faqs.a: Most guests come from Kigali, and the recommended way is a charter helicopter flight of approximately 22 minutes. By road, the drive to Akagera takes about two and a half hours. Helicopters also link Akagera with Volcanoes National Park for guests combining a safari with gorilla trekking.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Magashi Peninsula?
faqs.a: Wilderness names the dry seasons, June to September and December to February, as the best time for an Akagera safari. Wildlife gathers around water sources in these months, which makes sightings more predictable.

faqs.q: How many suites does Magashi Peninsula have?
faqs.a: There are just two couple's suites, set 200 metres apart, and one exclusive-use villa with two en-suite rooms plus an extra room adaptable as a gym, office or children's room. The suites and the villa each have their own plunge pool and a rooftop Star Bed.

faqs.q: Is Magashi Peninsula good for families?
faqs.a: Yes, Wilderness points families and groups to the exclusive-use villa, which has its own private guide, in-villa meals, kitchen, living and dining space, and a spare room that can serve as a children's room.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Magashi Peninsula?
faqs.a: Day and night game drives in the only private access area in Akagera, guided nature walks, boat safaris on Lake Rwanyakazinga, catch-and-release fishing and Star Bed sleep-outs. Akagera is home to lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and white and Eastern black rhino.

faqs.q: Who is Magashi Peninsula best suited to?
faqs.a: The suites are designed for couples, and the villa suits families and groups who want privacy. Every stay contributes to the rehabilitation of Akagera National Park, which Wilderness supports as a concessionaire alongside African Parks and the Rwanda Development Board.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Ruckomechi?
faqs.a: Ruckomechi is on the banks of the Zambezi River in northern Zimbabwe, on a private conservation area bordering the western boundary of Mana Pools National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

faqs.q: How do you get to Ruckomechi?
faqs.a: Wilderness says domestic travel to its Mana Pools camps is handled by Wilderness Air and ground transfers, so routing is arranged when you book.

faqs.q: When is Ruckomechi open, and when is the best time to go?
faqs.a: The camp is open from 1 April to 19 November and closes seasonally from 20 November to 31 March. Wilderness names the dry season, June to November, as the best time to visit Mana Pools.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Ruckomechi have?
faqs.a: There are ten spacious en-suite suites, not tents, two of them designed for families, all facing the Zambezi River.

faqs.q: Is Ruckomechi good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Two of the ten suites are family units, and Wilderness describes a Ruckomechi safari as best shared with loved ones.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Ruckomechi?
faqs.a: Game drives on the floodplain, canoeing and boat safaris on the Zambezi, catch-and-release tigerfish fishing, guided walking safaris and a night on the elevated Star Bed platform.

stays.name: Wilderness Sabyinyo
stays.tagline: Where gorilla dreams and Rwandan hospitality meet
stays.quote: Breathe deep, feel the mountain mist, and walk with giants
stays.bestMonths: June to September, December to February
stays.bestMonthsNote: Driest months give the easiest trekking. March to May and October to November bring rain, lush forest and fewer visitors.
stays.airportDirections: Helicopter transfer from Kigali on request (recommended), or drive about three hours to Musanze; the lodge is 15 minutes from park headquarters.

paras: Six stone cottages, two suites with king-size four-poster beds and one family unit with two separate bedrooms. Each has a fireplace, a large sitting area, an en-suite bathroom and a sheltered veranda with views of the Virunga volcanoes.

A 16-hectare property on the edge of Volcanoes National Park, about 15 minutes from the park headquarters where treks begin. Rwanda's first community-owned lodge, owned by the SACOLA community trust and operated by Wilderness. Menus inspired by daily harvests from the organic vegetable gardens. Fireplaces in every cottage. Wi-Fi in the main area.

onlyHere: Wilderness Sabyinyo is made for travellers who want gorilla treks, golden monkey trekking and Rwandan culture at the door. Stay here for an authentic Rwandan experience, warm hospitality and a direct contribution to conservation and community empowerment.

why.title: Journey to the Heart of the Volcanoes
why.body: Sabyinyo pairs comfortable stone cottages and knowledgeable guides with access to Rwanda's mountain gorillas. Just by staying here, you contribute to wildlife conservation and community empowerment initiatives.

facts.best_months: June to September and December to February are the driest months and the best for gorilla trekking, though gorillas can be tracked all year.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly into Kigali, then take a helicopter transfer on request (recommended), or drive about three hours to the Volcanoes National Park area; the lodge is 15 minutes from park headquarters.
facts.signature_experiences: Mountain gorilla and golden monkey trekking, the Dian Fossey gravesite hike, guided birding and community walks with SACOLA.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers who want gorilla trekking and an authentic, community-owned Rwandan lodge, including families using the two-bedroom family unit.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Sabyinyo?
faqs.a: Wilderness Sabyinyo sits on a 16-hectare property on the edge of Volcanoes National Park in north-western Rwanda, in the foothills of the Virunga Massif. It is about 15 minutes from the park headquarters, where trekking permits are obtained before each trek.

faqs.q: How do you get to Wilderness Sabyinyo?
faqs.a: Fly into Kigali International Airport, then take a helicopter transfer to the lodge, the recommended option, arranged through your travel designer. By road, drive roughly three hours to Musanze, the closest village to Volcanoes National Park, and on to the lodge; Wilderness bookings in Rwanda include a private vehicle and driver-guide.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Sabyinyo?
faqs.a: Gorillas can be tracked all year. Wilderness names the dry seasons, June to September and December to February, as the best times for trekking, while March to May and October to November bring rain, greener forest and fewer visitors.

faqs.q: What accommodation does Sabyinyo have?
faqs.a: Sabyinyo has six stone cottages, two suites with king-size four-poster beds and one family unit with two separate bedrooms. Each has a fireplace, a large sitting area and a sheltered veranda with views over the volcanoes.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Sabyinyo?
faqs.a: Yes, the family unit has two separate bedrooms. Wilderness notes that under Rwandan park regulations children under 15 are not permitted on gorilla treks.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences, and are gorilla permits included?
faqs.a: Gorilla trekking to one of 12 habituated families is the main draw, alongside golden monkey trekking, hikes in the park including to Dian Fossey's gravesite, guided birding, community walks and in-cottage massage. Gorilla trekking permits, park fees and the conservation levy are charged separately from the lodge rate.

faqs.q: Who is Sabyinyo best suited to?
faqs.a: Sabyinyo suits travellers who want an authentic Rwandan experience with gorilla trekking. It is Rwanda's first community-owned lodge, owned by the SACOLA community trust and operated by Wilderness, so every stay supports conservation and the surrounding communities.

Seasonal boating on the Kunene, water levels permitting. Dune-sensitive guided quad biking. Nature drives and walks among the geological formations. Himba cultural visits. Birding on the river, riverside breakfasts and stargazing.

Set under verdant trees on the banks of the Kunene River, on the Namibia and Angola border. Home is the 300,000-hectare Marienfluss Conservancy, owned primarily by the Himba. Reached only by light aircraft. Pool and Wi-Fi. Support for the Himba community through educational programmes, a mobile medical clinic and nutritional aid. Respectful, authentic engagement with the Himba.

onlyHere: Serra Cafema is for the true explorer and dreamer. Here the Kunene River flows through ancient desert, and the Himba live sustainably, as they have for centuries. Suited to couples, families, solo travellers, photographers, and anyone wanting a remote, meaningful and beautiful journey.

why.title: Land of Contrasts
why.body: Wilderness Serra Cafema blends raw adventure, rare culture, and wild beauty. Ideal for explorers, couples, families, photographers, and those craving solitude in a remote corner of the Kunene Region.

facts.best_months: Wilderness recommends May to September for exploring the desert on foot, with Kunene boating subject to water levels.
facts.how_to_get_there: Serra Cafema is only accessible by light aircraft operated by Wilderness Air.
facts.signature_experiences: Himba cultural visits, guided quad biking on a low-impact route and seasonal boating on the Kunene River.
facts.who_its_for: Explorers seeking remoteness, river and desert scenery and respectful cultural encounters with the Himba.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Serra Cafema?
faqs.a: On the banks of the Kunene River on Namibia's border with Angola, in the 300,000-hectare Marienfluss Conservancy, owned primarily by the Himba. The Hartmann's Mountains and the river form the backdrop.

faqs.q: How do you get to Serra Cafema?
faqs.a: Serra Cafema is only accessible by light aircraft operated by Wilderness Air.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Serra Cafema?
faqs.a: Wilderness names the cooler months, May to September, as particularly enjoyable for exploring Namibia's desert on foot. Boating on the Kunene is seasonal and depends on water levels. The camp page lists no seasonal closure.

faqs.q: How many suites does Serra Cafema have?
faqs.a: Eight elevated suites of wood, canvas and thatch, including one family unit, with interiors that pay homage to Himba culture.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Serra Cafema?
faqs.a: The camp has a family unit for privacy. Wilderness does not publish a minimum age on the camp page, so we confirm the child policy, including for quad biking, when planning.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Serra Cafema?
faqs.a: Respectful visits with the Himba, dune-sensitive guided quad biking and seasonal boating on the Kunene, water levels permitting. Nature drives, walks among the geological formations, birding and stargazing round out the stay.

faqs.q: Who is Serra Cafema best suited to?
faqs.a: Explorers who want deep remoteness, a river oasis in the desert and meaningful time with the Himba, from couples and families to solo travellers and photographers.
