paras: Six luxury tented suites on raised wooden platforms overlooking the floodplains, including one family room, each with indoor and outdoor showers and a double basin vanity.

Island setting in the heart of the Busanga Plains, known for its resident lions. Six luxury tented suites on raised wooden platforms. Pool overlooking the floodplain. Massage treatments from an in-house therapist. Wi-Fi. Family unit. Private safaris available.

onlyHere: Wilderness Shumba is for those who want front row seats to the drama of Busanga. Known for its lions and plains game, the camp blends comfort and exclusivity. Ideal for photographers, families and true safari enthusiasts seeking a remote Kafue safari.

why.title: Sleep with Lions, Wake to Wonder
why.body: Shumba delivers abundant predators, endless vistas, and an elegant camp in the remote Busanga Plains. Perfect for wildlife lovers, adventurers, and photographers.

facts.best_months: Open June to October only, when the Busanga Plains have drained and predator activity peaks.
facts.how_to_get_there: Light aircraft from Lusaka or Livingstone, around an hour and a half, to the Busanga airstrip in Kafue National Park.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives and guided walks among the lion prides and antelope herds of the Busanga Plains.
facts.who_its_for: Photographers and dedicated safari travellers who want an elegant six-tent camp in a remote, seasonal wilderness.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Shumba?
faqs.a: Shumba occupies its own small island in the Busanga Plains, in the remote north-west of Kafue National Park, Zambia's oldest and largest protected area.

faqs.q: How do you get to Wilderness Shumba?
faqs.a: By light aircraft from Lusaka or Livingstone to the Busanga airstrip inside Kafue National Park, a flight of around an hour and a half. The Busanga Plains have no road access for casual visitors.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Shumba?
faqs.a: Shumba is open only from June to the end of October, when the plains have drained after the rains and predator activity is at its highest. The camp closes during the wet season while the plains flood.

faqs.q: How many tents does Shumba have?
faqs.a: Six luxury tented suites on raised wooden platforms, each with indoor and outdoor showers and a double basin vanity.

faqs.q: Is Shumba suitable for families?
faqs.a: Shumba has one family room: a large room with a double bed and two three-quarter beds separated by a screen. Wilderness does not publish a minimum age on the camp page, so confirm children's ages when booking.

faqs.q: What is Shumba known for?
faqs.a: Lions. Shumba means lion in Tonga, and the Busanga Plains are known for large lion prides that leap the drying channels, along with cheetah, leopard, wild dog, red lechwe, puku and roan.

faqs.q: Who is Shumba best for?
faqs.a: Wilderness describes the camp as giving access to a remote area favoured by photographers and true safari enthusiasts, with more polish than nearby Busanga Bush Camp.

why.title: Wild Zambezi, Home Comfort

facts.best_months: Good year-round: Victoria Falls is fullest March to May, and August to November brings clearer Falls views and better game viewing.

facts.signature_experiences: White rhino walks with rangers, Zambezi cruises, tiger fishing and an included visit to Victoria Falls.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and families wanting a riverside base for Victoria Falls, wildlife and wellness.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Toka Leya?
faqs.a: On the banks of the Zambezi River in Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, Zambia, about 12 kilometres north-west of Victoria Falls.

faqs.q: How do you get to Toka Leya?
faqs.a: Fly into Harry Mwanga Nkumbula International Airport (LVI) in Livingstone, then take a short road transfer to camp. The Victoria Falls entrance is around 30 minutes from camp.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Toka Leya?
faqs.a: Toka Leya is good year-round. Victoria Falls is at full flow from March to May, while the dry season from August to November makes the Falls easier to view and photograph and brings better game viewing in the park.

faqs.q: How many tents does Toka Leya have?
faqs.a: Thirteen tented suites raised on wooden decks overlooking the Zambezi, three of which are family units with an extra bedroom.

faqs.q: Is Toka Leya good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Three of the thirteen suites are family units with an extra bedroom and expansive decks.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences at Toka Leya?
faqs.a: Guided walks to see Zambia's only wild white rhino population with armed rangers, sunrise and sunset Zambezi cruises, catch-and-release tiger fishing, game drives and a complimentary visit to the Falls are included.

faqs.q: Who is Toka Leya best for?
faqs.a: Travellers who want a luxury riverside base for Victoria Falls, wildlife and adventure activities, plus spa, gym and yoga time before or after a safari.

items: Moves with the Great Migration for best wildlife
Family-friendly and available for exclusive use

onlyHere: Wilderness Usawa Mobile Camp is for those who crave front-row seats to the world’s greatest wildlife event. If you want to be close to the migration, sleep out in wild places, and wake to lions’ roars. This is your adventure. Perfect for couples, solo travelers, families, photographers, and private groups wanting a genuine safari experience.

why.title: The Serengeti, Up Close
why.body: Wilderness Usawa Mobile Camp gives you the thrill of wild Africa, no fences, only nature, the migration, and unforgettable wildlife. Best for adventurous couples, families, and anyone seeking the real Serengeti.

facts.best_months: Year-round, as the camp moves: December to February for calving in the south, April to July in Grumeti and July to October for the northern river crossings.
facts.how_to_get_there: Fly by charter to Kogatende, Seronera or Serengeti South airstrip, depending on where the camp is pitched, then transfer by road.
facts.signature_experiences: Game drives following the Great Migration, guided walks, birding, stargazing and optional hot air balloon flights.
facts.who_its_for: Private groups and families booking sole use, and travellers who want to follow the migration from an intimate, light-footprint camp.

faqs.q: Where is Wilderness Usawa Serengeti?
faqs.a: Wilderness Usawa is a mobile camp that moves between nine sites within Serengeti National Park, with two camps set up at any given time. Locations include the Northern Hills, Lamai, Grumeti and the Southern Plains.

faqs.q: How do I get to Wilderness Usawa?
faqs.a: Charter flights land at Kogatende, Seronera and Serengeti South airstrips, and Wilderness arranges collection from whichever airstrip suits the camp's current site. Transfer times vary: the Northern Hills site is a 1.5-hour game drive from Kogatende, and the Lamai site is 30 minutes from Lamai Airstrip.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Wilderness Usawa?
faqs.a: The camp moves with the migration, so the timing depends on the site: December to February on the Southern Plains for calving, April to July in Grumeti, and July to October in the Northern Hills and Lamai for the Mara River crossings.

faqs.q: How many tents does Wilderness Usawa have?
faqs.a: Each camp has six en-suite safari tents for up to 12 guests and can be booked for sole use. The camps are completely solar-powered, with Wi-Fi and hot water.

faqs.q: Can children stay at Wilderness Usawa?
faqs.a: Yes. Children aged 6 and older are welcome, and children under 16 must share with an adult. Families with children younger than 6 need to book the camp for sole use.

faqs.q: What activities does Wilderness Usawa offer?
faqs.a: Game drives, guided walks in designated walking zones, birding and stargazing. Hot air balloon flights are available at additional cost, depending on weather and season.

onlyHere: Wolwedans Dune Camp is for couples, families with children 7 and over and photographers who want a down-to-earth but stylish camp, a Starbed on their own deck and the quiet of the NamibRand.

why.title: Desert Solitude, Soulful Luxury
why.body: For desert lovers, couples, families and anyone seeking quiet landscapes and a stay connected to the Wolwedans Village, Desert Academy and sustainability projects.

facts.best_months: Open all year, with a minimum 2-night stay.
facts.how_to_get_there: Charter or Tiras Taxi flight to the Wolwedans Airstrip, then a 5-minute transfer, or a 6 to 7-hour drive from Windhoek or Swakopmund.
facts.signature_experiences: Star Bed sleepouts, NamibRand scenic drives, the San-led Interpretive Desert Walk and dune e-biking.
facts.who_its_for: Travellers wanting a down-to-earth but stylish desert camp, including couples and families with children 7 and over.

faqs.q: Where is Wolwedans Dune Camp?
faqs.a: It sits on the edge of a 250-metre-high dune in the NamibRand Nature Reserve in Namibia's Namib Desert. It is where Wolwedans began.

faqs.q: How do I get to Wolwedans Dune Camp?
faqs.a: Charter flights from Windhoek, Swakopmund or elsewhere in Namibia land at the Wolwedans Airstrip, a 5-minute transfer from camp, and Scenic Air's Tiras Taxi flies daily from Eros Airport in Windhoek. By road it is a 6 to 7-hour drive from Windhoek or Swakopmund.

faqs.q: When is Dune Camp open?
faqs.a: Dune Camp is open all year, with a minimum 2-night stay.

faqs.q: How many rooms are there?
faqs.a: Dune Camp sleeps up to 16 guests in 8 rooms: 6 Tented Rooms and 1 two-room tented Family Suite. Each has a private deck with a daybed that converts to a Starbed and a Wolwedans Chiller to cool off in.

faqs.q: Can children stay?
faqs.a: Children aged 7 and over are welcome. The Family Suite sleeps up to 4 adults and 2 children, with its own small kitchen, bar and private dining area.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Sleeping out on the Star Bed, scenic drives across the NamibRand, the Interpretive Desert Walk with a local guide, dune e-biking and the Silence and Solitude experience. Horse riding and ballooning cost extra.

faqs.q: Who is Dune Camp best for?
faqs.a: Wolwedans says Dune Camp appeals to travellers looking for a down-to-earth but stylish experience, including couples and families with children 7 and over.

stays.name: Wren Urban Nest
stays.tagline: A clever little nest in the heart of Dublin.
stays.quote: Small room. Big city. Less footprint. More Dublin.
stays.bestMonthsNote: Dublin is a year round city, but spring through early autumn gives travelers the best opportunity to combine long walks, parks, outdoor cafés, cultural exploring and evenings around the city. Wren's central position makes it particularly easy to adapt your plans to the weather, with museums, galleries, restaurants, pubs and public transport all close by.
stays.airportDirections:
Approximate driving time: 30 to 45 minutes by taxi, depending on traffic.
Best arrival airport: Dublin Airport | DUB
Wren also provides a public transport option from the airport. Bus route 16 connects with Dublin city centre, while taxis take approximately 30 to 45 minutes.
For travelers arriving by car, Wren has a discounted arrangement with Park Rite Drury Street Car Park, approximately three minutes away on foot, subject to availability.
onlyHere: Wren Urban Nest makes a virtue of doing more with less. The rooms are compact by design, but thoughtful rather than restrictive, with clever technology, natural materials, comfortable beds and everything needed for a city stay. Step outside and Dublin opens immediately, from Trinity College and Grafton Street to Temple Bar, museums, galleries, restaurants and the Creative Quarter.

why.title: Sleep small. Live Dublin big.
why.body: Wren is made for travelers who believe the best city hotel is the one that gets you out the door.
The rooms are intentionally compact, efficient and quiet. The location does the rest. Trinity College, Grafton Street, Temple Bar and Dublin's Creative Quarter are all within easy walking distance.

There is also a deeper reason to choose Wren. Sustainability is built into the property rather than added as a marketing layer, with renewable energy, fossil free operations, local organic produce, reduced waste, reusable materials and biodiversity projects forming part of the stay.

Pleasant temperatures also create excellent conditions for wellness retreats, sightseeing, and relaxing by your private villa.

onlyHere: XELA occupies one of the original private villas built on Tulum Beach and keeps the scale of a home: 12 keys, a beach club and an izakaya. It is designed to feel like a secluded house on the sand rather than a resort.

why.title: A private beach villa turned 12-suite hotel
why.body: XELA suits travellers who want to be on the sand in a small, design-led house, with rooftop yoga, ceremonies and sister restaurants close by. Children 12 and older are welcome.

facts.how_to_get_there: Cancún (CUN) about 90 minutes via Highway 307 to Tulum, then to Km 8.7 on the beach road; Tulum airport (TQO) is 30 miles away. Private transfers through the concierge.
facts.signature_experiences: XELA Beach Club and Izakaya, rooftop yoga, temazcal at dusk, weddings on the sand, La Valise Spa, dinner at NÜ Tulum.
facts.who_its_for: Couples and small parties (children 12+) wanting a 12-key beachfront villa hotel that feels like a private home.

faqs.q: What is XELA Tulum?
faqs.a: XELA is a 12-suite boutique hotel on Tulum Beach, built into a former private beach villa and a member of Design Hotels. It is part of the NAMRON Hospitality family with La Valise and NEST.

faqs.q: Where is XELA Tulum?
faqs.a: On the beach road at Carretera Tulum-Boca Paila Km 8.7, Tulum Beach, Zona Hotelera. XELA says it is 90 miles south of Cancún and 30 miles from Tulum International Airport.

faqs.q: How do I get to XELA Tulum?
faqs.a: From Cancún (CUN), take Highway 307 south for approximately 90 minutes to Tulum, then the beach road towards Boca Paila to Km 8.7. From Tulum airport (TQO), follow Highway 307 to Tulum Pueblo and the Hotel Zone signs. XELA offers private transfers through the concierge.

faqs.q: What rooms does XELA Tulum have?
faqs.a: Twelve keys including beachfront suites (Caracol, Coco), ocean suites (Casa Playa, Coqui), ocean rooms (Venus, Sian and Zama), the XELA Master Suite, and garden rooms and studios (Icaro and Ixchel, Coral, Palmas, Selva and Ceiba). Some have bathtubs or a plunge pool.

faqs.q: Can children stay at XELA Tulum?
faqs.a: Children aged 12 and older are welcome. Pets are also welcome, up to two per room.

faqs.q: What is there to do at XELA Tulum?
faqs.a: The XELA Beach Club, XELA Izakaya, a rooftop, pool, gym and yoga, plus ceremonies such as a temazcal at dusk. Guests can also use La Valise Spa and sister restaurants NÜ Tulum, Climo and Los Bowls de Guadalupe.

faqs.q: Does XELA Tulum offer protection against rain?
faqs.a: Yes. Through Sensible Weather, guests can add a Rainy Day Guarantee that refunds up to the full room night cost if it rains during the day, subject to Sensible Weather's terms.

stays.airportDirections: A 25-minute charter flight from Maun, then a short road or boat transfer to the lodge.

paras: Twelve individually designed suites raised above the forest floor, including the two-bedroom Xigera Suite, each with a lounge, private deck with daybed, and indoor and outdoor showers. The Baobab Treehouse sleep-out stands nearly ten metres above the floodplain.

items: A night in the Baobab Treehouse

paras: In Moremi Game Reserve on the western edge of the Okavango Delta. Pool over the Delta. Spa, gym and yoga deck. Library. A collection of contemporary African art by more than 80 artists. Solar powered, no single-use plastics.

onlyHere: Xigera pairs the Delta's water and wildlife with a gallery's worth of African art, and offers one of the great sleep-outs in Africa in its sculpted Baobab Treehouse.

why.title: Art in the Wild
why.body: Best for couples, families, design lovers and returning safari-goers.

stays.name: Zannier Sonop
stays.tagline: Ten tented suites on granite boulders in the southern Namib
stays.bestMonths: Year-round; April to September for cool dry days
stays.bestMonthsNote: April to September is dry with pleasant days and cold nights; December to March is the rainy season, with very warm days.
stays.airport: Sonop private airstrip; Windhoek Hosea Kutako (WDH)
stays.airportDirections: About 1 hour 20 minutes by light aircraft from Windhoek to Sonop's own airstrip, or about 6 hours by road from Windhoek.

paras: Ten tented suites in 1920s colonial style, set on granite boulders: one-bedroom tents with panoramic terraces and two-bedroom tents with a lounge and wide terrace.
On a private reserve on the edge of the NamibRand Nature Reserve. Open-air infinity pool. Spa, gym and daily yoga. Open-air cinema. Cocktail and cigar lounge. Private airstrip. Three Michelin Keys.

onlyHere: Sonop is the desert done with theatre: an explorer's camp on a granite boulder outcrop, gala dinners and a Cocktail and Cigar Lounge, horses and fat bikes on the plains, and night skies full of stars.

why.title: Desert Romance
why.body: Best for couples, honeymooners, riders and anyone who wants the Namib with full luxury. Children from six.

facts.best_months: April to September is the dry season with pleasant days and cold nights.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 1 hour 20 minutes by small plane from Windhoek Hosea Kutako to Sonop's own landing strip, or about 6 hours by road.
facts.signature_experiences: Horse riding, electric fat biking, hot air balloon safaris, nature drives and an open-air cinema under the stars.
facts.who_its_for: Couples, riders and families with children 6 and over looking for old-world desert luxury.

faqs.q: Where is Zannier Sonop?
faqs.a: It is in the Hardap region of southern Namibia, on the edge of the NamibRand Nature Reserve, set among granite boulders within 13,800 acres of private desert. Zannier gives the address as Sonop Farm, Road D707.

faqs.q: How do I get to Zannier Sonop?
faqs.a: Sonop has its own landing strip, about 1 hour 20 minutes by small plane from Windhoek Hosea Kutako International Airport. By road it is about 500 km and 6 hours from Windhoek, or 2 hours 30 minutes from Mariental.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: Zannier describes April to September as the dry winter season, with pleasant days and cold nights. October to December is hot and dry, and December to the end of March is the rainy season, with very warm days.

faqs.q: How many tents are there?
faqs.a: Ten tented suites in 1920s colonial style: one-bedroom tents with a private panoramic terrace, and two-bedroom tents with two bedrooms, separate bathrooms and a lounge for up to 4 adults and 2 children.

faqs.q: Can children stay?
faqs.a: Children aged 6 and over are welcome; for safety reasons Sonop cannot host children under 6.

faqs.q: What are the signature experiences?
faqs.a: Horse riding, electric fat bike and walking trails, hot air balloon safaris, sunrise and sunset nature drives, stargazing and an open-air cinema, with breakfast on the dunes and gala-style dinners.

faqs.q: Who is Zannier Sonop best for?
faqs.a: Couples and families with children 6 and over who want a 1920s-style safari lodge in the desert, with riding, wellness and Three Michelin Keys service.

onlyHere: Zarafa Dhow Suite is perfect for families or friends looking for complete privacy, five star comfort, and front row wildlife in Botswana’s iconic Selinda Reserve.

why.title: Your Private Safari, Redefined
